studies.system: Antihydrogen atoms synthesized from antiprotons of the CERN Antiproton Decelerator and positrons of a positron accumulator and held in the magnetic multipole trap of ALPHA-2
studies.preparation: Mix about 90,000 antiprotons with 3,000,000 positrons in Penning traps to produce about 50,000 antihydrogen atoms per trial, of which about 20 are cold enough (below 0.54 K) to be trapped. Accumulate three mixing cycles, remove leftover charged particles with pulsed electric fields, wait about 10 s for decay to the ground state, expose the trapped atoms for 300 s to 243 nm light in a cryogenic enhancement cavity at one of nine detunings in four interleaved, blinded sets (each including zero and -200 kHz), remove 1S_c atoms by a microwave spin flip, release the survivors by ramping the trap down and count annihilations with a silicon vertex detector; compare the line with a simulation of hydrogen in the same trap.
studies.observable: Annihilations of anti-atoms lost during laser exposure (appearance) and of survivors (disappearance) versus 243 nm detuning; fitted 1S-2S d-d resonance frequency against the hydrogen value calculated for the trap field
studies.finding: About 15,000 trapped antihydrogen atoms over ten weeks show a two-photon 1S-2S line: at zero detuning 219 to 303 atoms per set were lost during laser exposure against 7 to 26 at -200 kHz (Table 1); the scaled line shape and width agree with the simulation for hydrogen, and the fitted d-d resonance, 2,466,061,103,079.4(5.4) kHz, agrees with the hydrogen value for the trap field, 2,466,061,103,080.3(0.6) kHz, to a precision of about 2 x 10^-12.
limitations: Antimatter: the atom is assembled from an antiproton and a positron; that ordinary atoms form in the same way around electrons is an inference supported by the agreement with hydrogen under charge-parity-time symmetry.
The production techniques are described in papers that were not read, and no run without positrons is reported here.
The comparison with hydrogen is model-dependent (simulated trap dynamics and laser powers fitted per set).

studies.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
studies.system: Adult mice walking on a treadmill, crossing a horizontal ladder and swimming: Egr3 knockout mice whose muscle spindles regress after birth (14 to 15 animals) with wild-type controls (13 to 16), and Pv::cre by Isl2::DTA mice in which proprioceptive afferents die selectively
studies.preparation: Implant four pairs of bipolar electromyographic electrodes in hindlimb muscles of adult mice and record during treadmill walking, horizontal-ladder crossing and swimming, comparing mice lacking muscle spindle feedback (Egr3 knockout) and mice lacking all proprioceptive afferents (Pv::cre by Isl2::DTA) with wild-type littermates.
studies.observable: Temporal parameters of the step cycle, onset and offset timing of iliopsoas, semitendinosus and tibialis anterior activity, their relative phasing during walking and swimming, and foot-placement error rate on the ladder
studies.finding: All temporal parameters of stepping were significantly shorter without proprioceptive feedback, and the absence of muscle-spindle feedback produced a selective change in the timing of ankle-flexor activity, with the tibialis anterior offset differing by 33 percent (p less than 0.001). Egr3 mutants still stepped and swam but in a profoundly ataxic manner, with a 30 percent foot-drop error rate on the horizontal ladder against 2 percent in wild-type mice, and during swimming their iliopsoas, semitendinosus and tibialis anterior became active synchronously rather than in the staggered wild-type pattern. In mice lacking all proprioceptors the same three muscles showed synchronous burst onset and offset during both walking and swimming, so the spinal locomotor circuits without proprioceptive feedback drive synchronous flexor activation.
limitations: Mice and hindlimb electromyography in three locomotor tasks.
Both models are constitutive, so developmental compensation cannot be excluded, and the Egr3 model removes spindles while the DTA model removes all proprioceptors.
Animal numbers are given for the spindle model; the all-proprioceptor results rest on fewer animals.
Locomotion persisted in both models, so the evidence concerns the pattern rather than the existence of movement.

studies.system: Mouse embryos with Sox9 conditionally inactivated either before mesenchymal condensation (Prx1-Cre) or after it, in condensed mesenchyme and chondrocytes (Col2a1-Cre)
studies.preparation: The same floxed Sox9 allele is recombined by Prx1-Cre in undifferentiated limb-bud mesenchyme or by Col2a1-Cre in condensed mesenchymal cells and differentiated chondrocytes, giving two time points of removal of the same differentiation switch; loss of Sox9 protein in the Col2a1-Cre mutants is timed by immunohistochemistry from 12.5 to 15.5 dpc. Skeletons of newborn or E17.5 animals are stained with alcian blue and alizarin red, metacarpals and radius are examined histologically with alcian blue and nuclear fast red, proliferation by PCNA staining and mineralisation by the von Kossa method.
studies.observable: Presence and amount of cartilage and bone in endochondral skeletal elements, chondrocyte differentiation and columnar organisation, proliferation and mineralisation
studies.finding: Inactivation before condensation gives a complete absence of both cartilage and bone in the limbs, with no condensations and no expression of Col2a1, Sox5, Sox6 or Runx2. Inactivation after condensation gives a very severe generalised chondrodysplasia: all skeletal elements formed by endochondral bone formation, including ribs, limbs and vertebrae, are extremely small with severely reduced alcian blue staining, most cells remain arrested as condensed mesenchymal cells with little alcian-blue-stainable matrix and do not undergo overt differentiation into chondrocytes, the orderly parallel columns of proliferating chondrocytes are absent, few cells are PCNA-positive and joint formation is defective, while skeletal elements formed by intramembranous ossification lack significant abnormality and bone trabeculae and mineralisation still appear in the malformed elements.
limitations: Two tissue classes are addressed, cartilage and the endochondral bone built on it; intramembranous bone, epithelium, muscle and connective tissue are either unaffected or not tested.
The Col2a1-Cre deletion proceeds over a window of days, so residual Sox9 remains in some cells and the arrest is not a clean all-or-none removal.
Loss of Sox9 also abolishes Sox5 and Sox6 expression, so the differentiation step removed is a whole module rather than a single factor.
The readouts are skeletal staining and histology; the figure images and the Materials and Methods were not read.

studies.system: Mouse embryos with Sox9 conditionally inactivated in undifferentiated limb-bud mesenchyme (Sox9flox/flox;Prx1-Cre), with wild-type littermates
studies.preparation: A Sox9 allele with exons 2 and 3 flanked by loxP sites is combined with the Prx1-Cre transgene, which is expressed in all limb-bud mesenchymal cells from about embryonic day 9.5, so that the chondrogenic switch is removed before mesenchymal condensation; recombination is confirmed by genotyping of the deleted allele. Limb buds are examined histologically at 11.5, 12.5 and 13.5 dpc, by scanning electron microscopy for digit formation, by peanut-agglutinin binding for condensations, and by whole-mount and section in situ hybridization for condensation and differentiation markers and for the markers of each limb axis. Dissociated mutant limb mesenchyme is also plated at high density in micromass culture, which provides cell-cell interactions in vitro.
studies.observable: Presence of chondrogenic mesenchymal condensations, digit formation and limb-bud outgrowth, cartilage nodule formation in micromass culture, and expression of Col2a1, Sox5, Sox6, Runx2 and of the limb-axis markers
studies.finding: Mutant limb buds have no discernible chondrogenic mesenchymal condensations at 12.5 dpc and very little localised peanut-agglutinin binding, and thereafter no cartilage or bone is detectable; scanning electron microscopy shows no distinct digit formation and arrest of limb-bud outgrowth, and newborn mutants have very short limbs in which cartilage and bone are completely absent. Dissociated mutant mesenchymal cells form no alcian-blue-positive cartilaginous nodules in micromass culture, so the source concludes that the cells lose chondrogenic potency even when cell-cell interactions are provided. Expression of Col2a1, Sox5 and Sox6 is essentially abolished and Runx2 and Bsp are undetectable in mutant limb mesenchyme, whereas the markers of the limb axes, Fgf8 in the apical ectodermal ridge, the posterior marker Shh, the dorsal marker Lmx1b, the ventral marker En1, Msx1, HoxD12, HoxD13, Prx1 and Twist, are expressed as in wild type, and the source states that the absence of Sox9 does not produce patterning defects. Myogenin-positive cells still enter the mutant limb buds although muscle bundles are very abnormally organised.
limitations: The source uses the word patterning for the limb-axis marker genes, which are unchanged; what fails here is the realised tissue-scale architecture, the condensations, digits and outgrowth, not positional specification.
One transcription factor in the limb bud and sternum of one mouse line; other organs and other morphogenetic fields are not tested.

Mutant limb mesenchyme also undergoes extensive apoptosis from 13.5 dpc, which the source relates to loss of Noggin and Chordin expression, so the arrest of outgrowth is not separated from cell death.
Condensation and marker readouts are histology and in situ hybridization at single time points; the figure images and the Materials and Methods were not read.

studies.system: Tau leptons from e+e- -> Z -> tau+ tau- recorded by ALEPH at LEP-I in 1991-1995, over 300 000 identified tau decays
studies.preparation: Measure the tau branching fractions with the full LEP-I sample, derive the non-strange hadronic width relative to the electronic width separated into vector and axial-vector parts, and unfold the spectral functions. Fit R_tau and the spectral moments with QCD: the parton-level rate (3/2)|Vud|^2 S_EW per current (|Vud| = 0.9746, S_EW = 1.0198) multiplied by 1 + delta(0), the massless perturbative term in fixed-order and contour-improved perturbation theory with the four-loop RGE and K4 = 25 +/- 25, plus operator-product-expansion terms of dimension 2-8 with the gluon condensate and the dimension-6 and -8 operators free. Compute R_tau,V+A(s0) for hypothetical tau masses sqrt(s0) below m_tau from the measured spectral function and determine alpha_s(s0) at each s0; evolve alpha_s(m_tau^2) to MZ with four-loop running and three-loop matching at the c and b thresholds and compare with the Z-width value of the global electroweak fit.
studies.observable: Non-strange hadronic tau width ratio R_tau,V+A, the strong coupling alpha_s at the tau mass and at lower s0, nonperturbative OPE contributions and alpha_s evolved to MZ
studies.finding: R_tau,V = 1.787 +/- 0.013, R_tau,A = 1.695 +/- 0.013 and R_tau,V+A = 3.482 +/- 0.014. The combined fits give alpha_s(m_tau^2) = 0.340 +/- 0.005 (exp) +/- 0.014 (th), the average of the fixed-order (0.331) and contour-improved (0.350) results, with a total nonperturbative V+A correction of -(4.3 +/- 1.9) x 10^-3. R_tau,V+A(s0) from the data agrees with the prediction using the parameters fitted at the tau mass down to s0 of about 0.8 GeV^2, to about 2 percent at 1 GeV^2; alpha_s decreases by a factor of 1.6 between 1 and 1.8 GeV in agreement with the four-loop RGE for three flavours and reaches about 0.55 at the lowest masses. Evolved to MZ, alpha_s(MZ^2) = 0.1209 +/- 0.0018, in agreement with 0.1186 +/- 0.0027 from the Z width; the source states that this consistency over more than three orders of magnitude in s tests the evolution of the strong coupling predicted by the nonabelian nature of QCD and is a precise test of asymptotic freedom at the 2.7 percent level.
limitations: alpha_s depends on the perturbative expansion: the fixed-order and contour-improved results differ by 0.01-0.02, and the theoretical error dominates.

R_tau,V+A(s0) below the tau mass describes hypothetical tau masses under the assumption of quark-hadron duality; adjacent bins are strongly correlated and below 1 GeV^2 the prediction's uncertainty grows.
The Z-width comparison value is an external global electroweak fit, not an ALEPH measurement in this report.

studies.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
studies.system: Human MCF7 breast and SKOV-3 ovarian carcinoma cells, LKB1-deficient HeLa S3 cells reconstituted with wild-type or T363A Lkb1, HEK293 cells, Epstein-Barr-virus-immortalised ataxia-telangiectasia and control B lymphoblasts, clonal Atm+/+, Atm+/- and Atm-/- mouse embryonic fibroblasts, and Tsc2+/+ and Tsc2-/- (p53-null) mouse embryonic fibroblasts
studies.preparation: Cells are exposed to hydrogen peroxide, to menadione or to phenethyl isothiocyanate, which depletes glutathione, and mTORC1 signalling is followed by immunoblot for phosphorylated S6K1, S6 and 4E-BP1, with N-acetylcysteine and catalase as rescues and with subcellular fractionation and leptomycin B to locate the signalling node; the cascade is tested with ATM-deficient lymphoblasts and Atm-null fibroblasts, ATM, LKB1 and p53 siRNA, the AMPK inhibitor compound C, LKB1-deficient cells reconstituted with wild-type or ATM-site-mutant (T363A) Lkb1, Tsc2-null fibroblasts and a TSC2 allele lacking its AMPK sites. Autophagy is followed in parallel as GFP-LC3 puncta after 1 h of hydrogen peroxide, as LC3-II and p62 by immunoblot and as autophagosomes by electron microscopy.
studies.observable: Phosphorylation of S6K1, S6 and 4E-BP1 and of AMPK Thr172, ACC Ser79 and LKB1 Thr366; GFP-LC3 puncta, LC3-II and p62; autophagosomes by electron microscopy
studies.finding: Oxidative and genotoxic stress represses mTORC1 signalling, rapidly (under 60 min) and at low (under 0.1 mM) hydrogen peroxide concentrations, and N-acetylcysteine and catalase rescue the effect; menadione and glutathione depletion repress it as well, and fractionation with leptomycin B places the signalling in the cytoplasm. Autophagy increases concomitantly: GFP-LC3 puncta rise comparably to rapamycin, LC3-II increases, p62 falls over time and autophagosomes appear by electron microscopy. The repression requires an intact cascade: ATM-deficient lymphoblasts do not repress mTORC1, Atm-/- fibroblasts repress significantly less than Atm+/+ and Atm+/- fibroblasts, ATM and LKB1 knockdown attenuate the repression, LKB1-deficient HeLa S3 cells cannot repress and wild-type but not T363A Lkb1 restores it, compound C attenuates it, and Tsc2-/- fibroblasts do not repress although their AMPK is constitutively active, with a TSC2 allele lacking the AMPK sites likewise deficient. At 1 mM hydrogen peroxide and above, repression also proceeds by LKB1-independent routes. The authors state that ATM- and TSC2-independent routes to autophagy have not been ruled out.
limitations: Autophagy is measured as LC3 and p62 markers and autophagosome counts, and the study does not test genetically whether the ROS-induced autophagy requires ATM, TSC2 or mTORC1.
The oxidant is applied pharmacologically, and in several key experiments the cells also lack TSC2 and p53 or are tumour lines.
Senescence outputs of mTOR are not assessed; the supporting figures S1-S7 and the figure images were not read or inspected.
The published correction redefines the error bars of three panels.

studies.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
studies.system: Amazon Mechanical Turk participants randomized into groups of 12 on a web platform (Empirica): 719 in experiment 1 and 702 in experiment 2
studies.preparation: Groups estimate the correlation in scatter plots over 20 rounds with pay in proportion to performance; signal quality differs between participants, who are not told about it, and is reshuffled at round 11. Experiment 1 randomizes groups to solo work, static networks with three fixed neighbours, or dynamic networks in which each participant chooses up to three peers to follow after each round, all with full performance feedback. Experiment 2 keeps dynamic networks and randomizes feedback (none, own performance, or all members' performance), with a solo baseline. Each round comprises an independent guess, a social-exposure stage with the followed peers' answers and a final guess.
studies.observable: Individual and group (mean) estimation error; network centralization (Freeman centralization of followers), correlation between number of followers and cumulative performance, and weight on self
studies.finding: Dynamic networks with full feedback had the lowest errors (against static networks 17% lower individual and 18% lower group error overall, 36% and 40% in adapted periods). The correlation between a member's number of followers and cumulative performance was strongest with full feedback (r=0.62), against own feedback (r=0.3) and no feedback (r=0.2; P<0.001 for both differences). As performance information accrued, the networks evolved from fully distributed into centralized structures that amplified the influence of well-informed members, decentralized after the information shock (beta=-0.046, P<10^-4) and re-adapted; accurate members also resisted influence more.
limitations: Groups of 12 anonymous online workers over 20 rounds of a perceptual estimation task; influence is measured through following choices and resistance to influence.
The network-structure statistics concern the dynamic conditions; the static condition fixes ties by design.
The SI Appendix (statistical tables, platform screenshots) was not read, and the simulations are not counted as evidence.

studies.system: Variants of the 66-nucleotide core glmS ribozyme transcribed in situ on an Illumina sequencing chip
studies.preparation: Cluster a doped-synthesis DNA library encoding the consensus core glmS ribozyme with all single and 99.8 percent of double mutants in a 54-nucleotide region, plus higher-order mutants, on sequencing chips and transcribe it in situ. Allow more than 20 min for folding, introduce GlcN6P and follow self-cleavage as loss of a Cy3-labelled DNA probe hybridized 5' of the cleavage site, with a Cy5 probe 3' of it marking each cluster; repeat at several GlcN6P concentrations to fit kcat and apparent KM.
studies.observable: Cleavage rate constants kobs at 10 mM GlcN6P, kcat and apparent KM for about 24,000 variants; double-mutant rescue ratios kobs(double)/kobs(single)
studies.finding: Cleavage rates spanned five orders of magnitude (consensus 6.4 x 10^-2 s^-1 at 10 mM GlcN6P); 19 percent of single and 55 percent of double mutants were at least 10^4-fold slower than consensus. Mutations in the helices P1 and P2 were rescued to consensus-like activity by compensatory mutations in their base-pairing partners, and the diagonal rescue pattern reproduced the whole secondary structure. In P2.2 and P2.1, whose nucleotides also help form the active site and cofactor pocket, compensatory pairs rescued only partially (P2.2 to within less than 35-fold of consensus; any alternative C2-G56 pair over 850-fold below consensus). Tertiary contacts (G26 with the G7-C52 pair, residue 50 with the 8-25 pair) also showed rescue interactions.
limitations: One ribozyme measured on surface-attached, in situ transcribed RNA.
Rescue infers interactions from rates, not from structures.
Folding was allowed before ligand addition, so the measurement concerns catalysis by folded variants, not folding kinetics.

studies.system: Groups of four male littermate mice, Oxt::Cre-positive (6 groups) or Cre-negative (5 groups), in an enriched 70 x 50 cm semi-natural arena with automated tracking
studies.preparation: Inject a Cre-dependent stabilized step-function opsin (SSFO) above the paraventricular hypothalamic nucleus (PVN) and mount a head-borne, magnetically switched wireless LED device; group same-genotype littermates at weaning, record four baseline days in the arena, then activate each member's device for about 2 s roughly every 2 hours of the dark phase on two further days as it enters a feeder. Validate oxytocin-neuron activation by slice electrophysiology, c-Fos and plasma oxytocin, and compare changes from baseline between Cre-positive and Cre-negative groups by permutation tests.
studies.observable: 21 automatically tracked individual and pairwise readouts (contact and approach rates, time alone outside the nest, aggressive chases, face-to-back approaches), self-grooming, dominance rank and identity-domain traits
studies.finding: Activation of PVN oxytocin neurons separated the behaviour of Cre-positive from Cre-negative groups on both days (multivariate permutation test, p < 10^-5 and p = 0.00047). On the first day contact rate rose (p = 9 x 10^-7) and time alone outside the nest fell (p = 0.0028) more in Cre-positive mice; on the second day aggressive chases (p = 0.0132) and face-to-back approaches (p = 0.0047) increased more, a difference absent on the first day. The changes were independent of dominance rank, and stable identity-domain traits did not change.
limitations: Eleven groups of four males in one laboratory arena over two activation days; females and free-living populations were not tested.
The manipulation raises the activity of one neuromodulatory population in all group members; the functional specialization of the ensemble itself is not altered.
Group organization is read from interaction rates; the dominance hierarchy and interaction-network structure after activation were not analysed.

studies.system: Mouse embryos and postnatal eyes with Pax6 deleted in the eye surface ectoderm (Le-Cre; Pax6lacZ/Pax6flox, 'Le-mutant') and Pax6lacZ/Pax6flox littermate controls
studies.preparation: A Pax6flox allele (loxP sites around the amino terminus and most of the paired domain) was combined with one Pax6lacZ null allele and the Le-Cre transgene, which expresses Cre and GFP from the Pax6 P0 regulatory region in the surface ectoderm from E9. Pax6 protein disappears from the surface ectoderm between E9 and E9.5, after lens specification, while optic-vesicle Pax6 is kept. Eyes were analysed from E9 to adult stages by Pax6, Sox2, Six3, alphaA-crystallin and neuronal-marker immunolabelling, Prox1, Trp2 and Chx10 in situ hybridization and hematoxylin-eosin histology.
studies.observable: Lens placode thickening and invagination, lens-specific gene expression, presence of lens structures, optic-cup morphology and neuroretina differentiation and lamination
studies.finding: In the Le-mutant, Sox2 is up-regulated in the specified ectoderm, but the ectoderm neither thickens nor invaginates into a lens placode; Six3 protein, Prox1 transcripts and alphaA-crystallin are not detected and no lens structures form. Contact between surface ectoderm and optic vesicle is kept. Optic-cup invagination is delayed by about a day and two or three separate neuroretina folds invaginate, each differentiating into a laminated retina with ganglion, bipolar, horizontal, amacrine and photoreceptor cells, although the outer plexiform layer is incomplete. The authors conclude that Pax6 in the specified ectoderm is essential for lens placode formation and that the early lens is required for the placement of a single retina but not for retinal differentiation.
limitations: Pax6 removal stops lens-specific gene expression as well as placode morphogenesis, so the two are not separated.
The cornea and the optical function of the eye were not assessed in the text read.
Mutants and controls both carry one Pax6 null allele on mixed NMRI and FVB backgrounds; the read text gives no animal numbers.

studies.system: Nine designed 32-residue coiled-coil peptides T1-T9, assembled in aqueous buffer from nine electrophilic thioester fragments E1-E9 and a common N-terminal-cysteine nucleophile N by template-directed fragment condensation
studies.preparation: React all nine electrophiles (50 +/- 5 microM each) with substoichiometric nucleophile (300 microM) in one vessel in 100 mM MOPS pH 7.2 with 5 mM TCEP at 22 C, and follow the formation of all nine products simultaneously by quantitative reversed-phase HPLC with an internal standard, product identities confirmed by MS and co-injection. Repeat the network reaction seeded with about 30 microM of one template at a time to read off the operating auto- and cross-catalytic edges from initial-rate enhancements of at least two-fold. Measure the isolated autocatalytic efficiency of each peptide from single-electrophile reactions with and without added template, fitted to a template-assisted ligation model. Turn off the autocatalysis of T2 or T5 by omitting the corresponding electrophile, and verify single pathways in subnetworks containing only E1 and E4 or only E7. Control: the same network reaction under denaturing conditions, 3 M guanidine hydrochloride.
studies.observable: Rate and yield of formation of each of the nine products; initial-rate enhancements on seeding; fitted Km, kcat and relative autocatalytic efficiency
studies.finding: Under native conditions all nine products formed at different rates and yields, and seeding with a single template selectively accelerated particular products, giving a self-organised network of 8 nodes and 14 directed edges that grew to 25 edges as latent pathways were uncovered by switching off the strongest autocatalysts; T2, T5 and T8 accelerated their own formation, with relative autocatalytic efficiencies of 69, 22 and 11 against the slowest measurable reaction, while T9, T1 and T4 were essentially autocatalytically infertile. The reciprocal cross-catalytic pair T1 and T4 was confirmed in isolation, where seeding with either or both templates accelerated production with negligible autocatalysis, and T7 was shown to receive inputs from T3, T4, T5 and T8. Under denaturing conditions, 3 M guanidine hydrochloride, all nine products still formed but more slowly and in approximately equal yield, which the authors take to show that the assembled three-dimensional coiled-coil structures, not differences in intrinsic fragment reactivity, give rise to the template-directed selectivity.
limitations: A designed peptide system, not a biological network, and only nine of the 81 designed sequences were tested; the mutual production is pairwise cross-catalysis rather than a closed network that regenerates all its own substrates.
The reactions consume externally supplied activated fragments E1-E9 and the nucleophile N, so the network is not fed from a sustained substrate environment.
Edges are scored from initial-rate enhancements above a two-fold threshold, and the graph predictions agree only to about 80 percent; three observed edges were not predicted.
The denaturant control removes the folded coiled-coil but also changes the solvent for every species, so folding is not isolated from solvent effects.
The supporting figures with the kinetic fits were not read.

studies.system: Rods of mice lacking both retinal guanylate cyclases (GC1/GC2 double knockout, GCdko), single GC1-/- and GC2-/- knockouts and wild type
studies.preparation: Generation of GC2-/- and GC1/GC2 double-knockout mice; scotopic electroretinograms over a range of flash intensities; single-rod suction-electrode recordings; immunoblots and immunolocalization of GCAP1, GCAP2, rod PDE6 subunits, rhodopsin and rod transducin alpha; histology of outer segments at 2 and 6 months.

studies.system: Pairs of adult human observers (dyads) in a two-interval contrast-oddball detection task; 15, 11, 14 and 11 dyads in Experiments 1-4
studies.preparation: Each member first decides privately which of two brief intervals contained a slightly higher-contrast Gabor target; the decisions are then shared and, on disagreement, the dyad discusses freely until it reaches a joint decision, with trial feedback except in Experiment 4. Fit individual and dyad psychometric slopes and compare the dyad slope with the better member's slope and with four models (coin flip, behaviour and feedback, weighted confidence sharing, direct signal sharing). In Experiment 2, surreptitiously add noise to one member's, both members' or neither member's stimuli on randomized trials; in Experiment 3, allow only the exchange of choices, a randomly chosen member arbitrating disagreements; in Experiment 4, withhold feedback.
studies.observable: Slopes (sensitivities) of the individual and dyad psychometric functions and the collective benefit, the dyad slope divided by the better member's slope
studies.finding: With free communication, dyads of similar members were more sensitive than their better member (t(14) = 5.24, p < 10^-3), and dyad slopes matched the weighted-confidence-sharing prediction from the two individual slopes. Adding noise to one member's stimuli removed the collective benefit (t(21) = 0.68, p = 0.54), which remained under equal or no noise, and the benefit fell linearly as members' sensitivities diverged (R2 = 0.51). When members could exchange only their choices, the dyad did not exceed its better member (t(13) = 0.18, p = 0.85); without feedback but with communication the benefit remained (t(10) = 2.68, p = 0.022).
limitations: Dyads in a low-level perceptual task; larger groups and other kinds of collective decision are not tested.
No condition removes the members' own decision processes, which a joint decision presupposes; the noise degrades the evidence the members process, not the decision process itself.
Read as the Europe PMC funders' author manuscript (main text and figure legends); the supporting online material with methods and model derivations was not read.

studies.system: Escherichia coli VH1000 (MG1655 background) and derivatives with ribosomal S2-YFP or S2-mEos2, and the rifampicin-resistant rpoB S522F strain SB7
studies.preparation: Cells growing in EZ rich defined medium at 30 C in a microfluidic chamber are stained with SYTOX Orange and imaged by time-lapse phase-contrast and fluorescence microscopy before and after injection of rifampicin (300 µg/ml, 20 times the 24-h MIC; 100 and 600 µg/ml gave similar results), chloramphenicol (300 µg/ml), kanamycin or kasugamycin (5 mg/ml). Normalized cell length, nucleoid width and length, the 30S-YFP ribosome distribution and single-molecule 30S diffusion are quantified for short cells from single fields of view, each experiment repeated at least five times; the rifampicin-resistant SB7 strain controls for drug-specific effects.
studies.observable: Normalized cell length over time, nucleoid width and length, ribosome spatial distribution and 30S diffusion over about 25 min after drug injection
studies.finding: Before rifampicin, cells grow normally; after injection, mean relative cell length deviates from normal growth within 2-3 min, the nucleoid contracts radially (width from 810 to 745 nm within 5 min) and then expands axially over 5-20 min, and ribosomes, which are segregated from the nucleoid in normal growth, mix extensively with it while 30S diffusion increases as polysomes convert to free subunits. Rifampicin-resistant RifR cells continue to grow normally after rifampicin injection and keep normal nucleoid morphology. Chloramphenicol and kasugamycin decelerate cell growth within 1-2 min and also contract the nucleoid radially. The authors attribute the contraction to loss of coupled transcription, translation and membrane insertion (transertion) and the later mixing to conversion of 70S polysomes into free subunits.
limitations: Transcription is blocked by a drug over about 25 min; recovery and viability are not measured.
Ten to fifteen short cells from one field of view are quantified per experiment, with reproducibility stated across at least five experiments.
The transertion and nucleoid-ribosome mixing mechanism is the authors' interpretation, supported by simulation.
One strain background in one rich medium at 30 C.

studies.system: 1,543 farmers randomly sampled from 50 producer cooperatives in nine districts of Uganda, July-September 2009, in public-goods sessions of 8-12 players
studies.preparation: Within each cooperative, randomly assign participants to one of three public-goods games with an endowment of ten 100-shilling coins per round (one round paid): a baseline of six rounds without punishment, or two preliminary rounds after which one player became a monitor who could spend 1 unit to remove 3 units from players whose contribution she disapproved of, chosen by lottery (random monitor) or by secret-ballot election (elected monitor), for rounds 3-6. Players came from six villages, were not allowed to talk and held no leadership positions in the cooperative.
studies.observable: Contributions to the public account by round and condition; change in contributions after monitor selection and after being sanctioned; monitors' sanctioning behaviour
studies.finding: Contributions were 15.0% higher with a random monitor and 25.4% higher with an elected monitor than in the baseline (P<0.001), already in round 3 before any sanction (16.6% and 26.8%), and 9% higher with elected than with random monitors (P=0.005), although matched elected and random monitors sanctioned alike. In the baseline without a monitor, average contributions stayed at about 400-430 of 1,000 shillings and did not decline across rounds 3-6 (Figure 1).
limitations: Six rounds in groups of 8-12 members of the same cooperative; the monitor is a single sanctioning office created by the experimenters.
Elected monitors had a more dominant sociodemographic profile; unobserved selection effects cannot be fully excluded.
Persistence of cooperation without a monitor is shown over six rounds only; the SI Appendix was not read.

studies.system: Mouse macrophages of defined innate-receptor genotypes (TLR2, TLR3, TLR4, TLR7, MD-2, MyD88, TRIF, IRAK4, RIP2, TNFR1/2, NLRP3, caspase-1) and human monocytes including a donor with an IRAK4 Q293X loss-of-function mutation
studies.preparation: Immortalized and primary mouse macrophages expressing ASC-YFP or ASC-CFP are left resting or primed for 4 h through one signalling receptor (LPS, synthetic LPS, Pam2CysK4, poly(I:C), R848, MDP, TNF-alpha, or an activating anti-TLR4/MD-2 antibody UT18 against the blocking antibody MTS510), then stimulated 1 h with ATP, nigericin or crystals; transfected poly(dA-dT) serves as an AIM2 comparison that does not need priming. Knockout macrophages for the receptor or adaptor of each ligand are compared with wild type. Protein synthesis is blocked with cycloheximide and NF-kappaB with Bay11-7082. Nlrp3 and Asc mRNA, NLRP3 and pro-IL-1beta protein, and an Nlrp3 promoter-luciferase reporter co-expressed with MyD88 in HEK293T cells report expression control. Macrophages stably expressing NLRP3-mCitrine from a viral promoter, in wild-type and NLRP3-knockout backgrounds, test whether raised NLRP3 removes the priming requirement.
studies.observable: Cleaved caspase-1 in supernatants and lysates, ASC pyroptosome formation by confocal and epifluorescence microscopy, Nlrp3 and Asc mRNA, NLRP3 and pro-IL-1beta protein, and Nlrp3 promoter-reporter activity
studies.finding: Resting cells and cells given ATP or LPS alone show no ASC pyroptosomes and no caspase-1 cleavage; only cells first primed through a transcriptionally active signalling receptor and then given an NLRP3 activator respond, and caspase-1 cleavage tracks pyroptosome number. Macrophages lacking the receptor for the priming ligand, or doubly deficient in MyD88 and TRIF, fail to activate caspase-1 after ATP, while single MyD88 or TRIF deficiency is compensated; MDP priming depends on RIP2 and TNF-alpha priming fails in TNFR1/2 double-knockout cells. Human monocytes show the same requirement, and monocytes from an IRAK4-mutant patient are primed only by IRAK4-independent ligands, while AIM2 activation by transfected poly(dA-dT) proceeds without priming. Priming is blocked by cycloheximide and by the NF-kappaB inhibitor Bay11-7082; LPS raises Nlrp3 but not Asc mRNA in an NF-kappaB-dependent way and induces NLRP3 protein, and MyD88 activates an Nlrp3 promoter reporter about tenfold. Macrophages stably overexpressing NLRP3 form pyroptosomes and cleave caspase-1 in response to nigericin or ATP without any prior priming, in wild-type and in reconstituted NLRP3-knockout cells, while overexpression alone without an activator does not.
limitations: Mouse macrophage lines and primary macrophages plus human monocytes from healthy donors and one IRAK4-mutant patient; other inflammasome-competent cell types and in vivo inflammation are not tested.
Priming is supplied as defined purified receptor ligands over 4 h; endogenous damage-associated priming in tissue is not examined.
The AIM2 and overexpression arms show the priming requirement is specific to NLRP3 abundance, so the result does not generalise to every inflammasome.
Caspase-1 cleavage and pyroptosome counts are the readouts; mature IL-1beta release is not quantified in the panels read here.

studies.system: Replicatively senescent human BJ foreskin (low p16) and WI-38 lung (high p16) fibroblasts, WI-38 cells with p16 shRNA or lentiviral p16, and human mammary epithelial cells
studies.preparation: Passage fibroblasts in 20 percent oxygen to replicative senescence (<1 percent [3H]thymidine-labelled nuclei; no increase in cell number for >4 weeks) and hold them arrested for 1–3 months. Infect with lentiviruses (>95 percent transduction) expressing GFP, hTERT, the dominant-negative p53 peptide GSE-22, SV40 large T antigen (LgT), the p53-binding LgT-K1 mutant or CDK4m; measure DNA synthesis as percentage labelled nuclei 72 h later and proliferation by colony formation, loss of senescent morphology and population doublings. Suppress p16 by shRNA in pre-senescent WI-38 cells before senescence, or by lentiviral shRNA after senescence, and re-test GSE-22; express p16 ectopically in pre-senescent WI-38 cells.
studies.observable: Percentage of [3H]thymidine-labelled nuclei, colony formation and population doublings after infection; p16, p21 and p53 levels
studies.finding: Telomerase did not reverse the senescence arrest. In senescent BJ cells, GSE-22 and LgT-K1 each stimulated 70–90 percent of cells to synthesize DNA and to proliferate (GSE-22: more than 20 further population doublings, ending in crisis); the source concludes that p53 maintains the senescence growth arrest of these cells. In senescent WI-38 cells, which express more p16, GSE-22 and LgT-K1 stimulated less than 5 percent DNA synthesis and no agent produced proliferation. WI-38 cells that senesced with p16 suppressed by shRNA had elevated p21 and were completely reversed by GSE-22 (>70 percent), whereas ectopic p16 arrested pre-senescent WI-38 cells, which GSE-22 did not rescue; suppressing p16 only after senescence allowed DNA synthesis but proliferation in about 1–2 percent of cells.
limitations: Cultured human fibroblast strains in replicative senescence; damage- or oncogene-induced senescence is not tested with p53 inactivation.
p53 is inactivated with a dominant-negative peptide or viral protein, not deleted, and reversed cells eventually entered crisis.
Several supporting observations (strain 82-6, the senescent morphology and SA-β-gal after ectopic p16) are reported as data not shown; supplementary figures were not read.

studies.system: Escherichia coli FW102 carrying single-copy F128 episomes with engineered lac UV5 promoter-lacZ constructs (no CAP site, internal lacZ O2 destroyed) and wild-type levels of Lac repressor; LacI Y282D as non-functional repressor control
studies.preparation: Place a weak promoter-proximal O2 operator alone, with a strong auxiliary Osym operator upstream or downstream at varied centre-to-centre spacings, or with operators disrupted, on the F128 episome. Measure beta-galactosidase (Miller units) in MOPS-glycerol minimal medium with or without 2 mM IPTG and express repression as RR = Einduced/Erepressed; fit spacing series to a thermodynamic looping model; measure RNA polymerase alpha and sigma70 promoter occupancy by ChIP-qPCR; test T7 promoter constructs with arabinose-induced T7 RNA polymerase.
studies.observable: Repression ratio (IPTG-induced over repressed beta-galactosidase activity), normalized reporter activity E', and RNA polymerase promoter occupancy
studies.finding: With an auxiliary Osym operator 65 bp upstream of O2, in phase, the repression ratio is 99; repression by the weak O2 operator without looping drops by more than 30-fold, a leaky 2-3-fold repression, and no repression is detectable when O2 is disrupted. An in-phase downstream Osym (67 bp) gives a ratio of 68, dependent on both operators. Relative to O2 alone, looping raises the ratio 33-fold upstream and 23-fold downstream; out-of-phase spacing (73 bp) reduces repression to about 4-fold, and below about 40-45 bp no loop-dependent repression is seen. RNA polymerase occupancy is at background at repressed looped promoters, and the authors conclude that loops repress chiefly by raising the local repressor concentration at the promoter-proximal operator.
limitations: Engineered UV5 promoters without a CAP site on a single-copy episome; the native three-operator lac operon is not tested in this study.
The comparison removes the loop-mediated cooperation between two operators; repressor binding at a single operator and allosteric induction by IPTG remain.
Repression ratios are beta-galactosidase activity ratios; downstream operators also change mRNA leaders, and a bound downstream Osym alone gives 4-9-fold repression by blocking elongation.
Figure graphs, Table 1 values and Supplementary Figures S1-S5 and Tables S1-S3 were not inspected.

studies.system: Rats in the helping-behaviour test, in which a free rat can release a trapped cagemate from a restrainer; 16 rats per condition for the trapped condition (uninjected, saline, nadolol, low and high midazolam) and 8 per condition for the chocolate condition
studies.preparation: Test free rats daily for twelve days with a cagemate trapped in a restrainer that only they can open, after giving either no injection, saline, the benzodiazepine anxiolytic midazolam at 1.25 or 2.0 mg/kg, or the peripherally restricted beta-adrenergic antagonist nadolol, which does not cross the blood-brain barrier and so separates central anxiolysis from peripheral sympathetic dampening; repeat the same drug conditions with a restrainer containing chocolate instead of a cagemate as a non-social control.
studies.observable: Latency to open the restrainer door across the twelve days, the decay of that latency as a measure of learning, the plateau latency on days 10 to 12 and the number of openings
studies.finding: Opening latency fell across days in uninjected, saline-treated and nadolol-treated rats (all p less than 0.001) but not in rats given either dose of midazolam, so the anxiolytic removed the evidence of learning to help, and the decay differed significantly between groups (chi-squared(4) equal to 12.0, p equal to 0.02). The plateau latency on days 10 to 12 was significantly longer for high-dose midazolam than for uninjected rats (p equal to 0.01) or nadolol-treated rats (p equal to 0.04), and high-dose animals averaged 1.0 plus or minus 0.5 openings over twelve days against 5.7 plus or minus 1.2 in uninjected rats. With chocolate instead of a cagemate the pattern reversed: midazolam-treated rats showed significantly decreasing latencies while saline-treated rats did not, and the low-dose group opened faster than saline controls (p equal to 0.04), showing that the drug did not simply sedate the animals or prevent door-opening.
limitations: Rats and one prosocial paradigm with door-opening latency as the only behavioural measure.
Midazolam acts broadly on GABA-A receptors, so the affective interpretation rests on the nadolol and chocolate controls rather than on a localised manipulation.
Within each group a substantial subpopulation never opened consistently.
Social recognition itself was not measured, and the methods and remaining analyses were not read.

studies.system: Cultured Hamburger and Hamilton stage 10-11 chicken embryos, with electroporated presomitic mesoderm
studies.preparation: Caudal regions of cultured chicken embryos are laser-ablated and replaced with agarose, and the axis elongation rate is measured by time-lapse microscopy against non-operated embryos. Presomitic-mesoderm cells electroporated with H2B-GFP are tracked together with immunolabelled fibronectin, and cell motion relative to the matrix is obtained by subtracting matrix movement. Cell movement is then reduced pharmacologically with the Rho-kinase inhibitor Y27632 or with blebbistatin, and FGF signalling is reduced by electroporating an inducible dominant-negative FGF receptor after the cells have entered the presomitic mesoderm or by the FGFR1 inhibitor SU5402, and raised by electroporating FGF8, with the segmentation markers Mesogenin 1 and Lunatic fringe and somite formation as controls.
studies.observable: Axis elongation rate, tissue convergence, the anteroposterior profile of cell motility and of cell density, protrusion orientation and segmentation-marker expression
studies.finding: Bilateral deletion of the posterior presomitic mesoderm reduces the axis elongation rate more than deletion of the axial structures, of the anterior presomitic mesoderm or of the lateral plate (P < 0.01, n = 3 to 5 per condition). Tracked cells show a posterior-to-anterior gradient of motility that remains graded but loses all directional bias once matrix movement is subtracted, with mean square displacement scaling with time and protrusion angles indistinguishable from a random distribution. Expressing the dominant-negative FGF receptor lowers cell motility, flattens the motility gradient and decreases the elongation rate (P < 0.001, n = 10) and severely reduces tissue convergence (P < 0.05, n = 10) without changing the density gradient, and SU5402 also slows elongation; FGF8 overexpression keeps motility high anteriorly, abolishes the gradient and likewise reduces elongation (P < 0.01, n = 5) while the tissue expands laterally. Y27632 and blebbistatin, which inhibit cell movement directly, disrupt the motility gradient and diminish elongation and convergence (n = 3 embryos each) while Mesogenin 1 and Lunatic fringe expression is unaffected and somites continue to form.
limitations: Chicken embryo over an eight-hour window: the measured child-side readout is the rate of axis elongation and convergence of an already formed presomitic mesoderm, not the first formation of a tissue pattern.
The source concludes that the cell motion is random rather than directed, so the evidence covers self-propelled motility and not the steering of migration.
Y27632 and blebbistatin are pharmacological inhibitors with targets beyond cell motility, and FGF gain- and loss-of-function change motility in opposite directions while both slowing elongation.
Motility gradients are quantified in three to four embryos per condition, and the supplementary figures, movies and supplementary methods were not read.

studies.system: Forty-nine healthy volunteers pre-screened for state and trait anxiety scores and for basal adrenocorticotropic hormone and cortisol within narrow ranges, divided into four groups
studies.preparation: Induce ischaemic arm pain with a tourniquet for ten minutes with per-minute ratings, twice four days apart, always at 9:00, in a randomised double-blind design in which saline is given to additional subjects to preserve blinding. Group 1 receives no treatment on both tests. Groups 2 to 4 receive, on the second test, an inert pill described as a powerful vasoconstrictor that will worsen the ischaemic pain; groups 3 and 4 additionally receive intravenous diazepam at 0.28 mg/kg or the mixed cholecystokinin A and B antagonist proglumide at 1.5 mg/kg thirty minutes before the tourniquet. Sample plasma adrenocorticotropic hormone and cortisol before and at five and ten minutes.
studies.observable: Pain intensity ratings on a 0 to 10 scale and plasma adrenocorticotropic hormone and cortisol concentrations
studies.finding: The untreated natural history showed no difference between the two tests. The nocebo suggestion raised pain ratings at ten minutes from 5.07 to 8.61 and raised adrenocorticotropic hormone and cortisol. Diazepam blocked both the hyperalgesia and the hormonal hyperactivity; proglumide blocked the hyperalgesia (ratings 5.58) while leaving the adrenocorticotropic hormone and cortisol rise intact; and neither drug reduced pain in the non-nocebo condition. Pain ratings and hormone concentrations did not correlate.

studies.system: US census tracts (N = 21,452), counties and 2003 night-time lights in river watersheds crossing the fall line of the South and Mid-Atlantic, with Midwestern portage routes and falls on Mississippi tributaries; county population densities 1790-2000

studies.system: Web-recruited participants in live naming games in populations of 24, 48 and 96 arranged as spatial lattices (degree 4), random networks (degree 4) or homogeneously mixing populations
studies.preparation: Randomly assign arriving participants to a network condition and a position. limitations: Arbitrary names for one face with small payoffs over about 30 rounds; conventions with sanctions, costs or long persistence are not tested.

studies.system: Higgs bosons produced in CMS proton-proton collisions at 13 TeV, 2016-2018, up to 138 fb^-1
studies.preparation: Combine the CMS Run-2 analyses of Higgs boson production (ggH, VBF, WH, ZH, ttH, tH) and decay (gamma gamma, ZZ to four leptons, WW to two leptons and two neutrinos, Z gamma, tau tau, bb, mu mu), whose event selections do not overlap, in one profile likelihood with about 10^4 nuisance parameters. Fit signal strengths that scale standard-model rates, and coupling modifiers kappa that scale standard-model couplings: kappa_V and kappa_f; then kappa_W, kappa_Z, kappa_t, kappa_b, kappa_tau and kappa_mu with loop processes computed from them; then additionally free effective kappa_g, kappa_gamma and kappa_Zgamma. Search for Higgs boson pair production in several final states.

studies.finding: The overall signal strength is 1.002 +/- 0.057 and the decay-channel signal strengths include gamma gamma 1.13 +/- 0.09, ZZ 0.97 (+0.12/-0.11) and WW 0.97 +/- 0.09. In the six-parameter fit the reduced couplings, with v the vacuum expectation value of the BEH field, lie on the standard-model line proportional to mass for W, Z, t, b, tau and mu (p-value 37.5 percent), which the source calls a remarkable agreement with the predictions of the BEH mechanism over three orders of magnitude of mass. The source states that particle masses arise through gauge couplings (vector bosons) and Yukawa couplings (fermions) to the Higgs field, that the Higgs boson couples to photons and gluons only through loops, and that the diphoton branching fraction scales as (1.26 kappa_W - 0.26 kappa_t)^2. kappa_2V = 0 is excluded at 6.6 standard deviations and kappa_lambda lies between -1.24 and 6.49 at 95 percent CL.

Loop-induced processes are computed in the standard model unless the effective loop couplings are freed.

studies.preparation: Grow alternating layers of 95 percent enriched 57Fe and of 56Fe by molecular beam epitaxy on float glass at room temperature, with an Al cap, so that the film is chemically and electronically homogeneous iron but periodic in isotope. Characterize it by conversion-electron Mössbauer spectroscopy with a 57Co(Rh) source, magnetometry, Auger sputter depth profiling, Rutherford backscattering, scanning tunnelling microscopy and profilometry; measure polarized neutron reflectivity, whose scattering length differs between isotopes, at the IBR-2 reactor in Dubna; and at HASYLAB beamline F4 record time-integrated delayed (resonant) reflectivity of 14.413 keV synchrotron radiation, counted 17-131 ns after each pulse (146 ns in the figure caption), against the prompt non-resonant x-ray reflectivity of the same film, without an external field.
studies.observable: Reflectivity versus momentum transfer Q for delayed nuclear-resonant photons, non-resonant x-rays and polarized neutrons; CEMS line intensities and hyperfine field
studies.finding: CEMS shows pure alpha-iron without significant line broadening, hyperfine field 33.0(1) T. Polarized neutron reflectivity shows a Bragg peak near Q = 1.2 nm^-1 set by the isotope bilayer period. In synchrotron Mössbauer reflectometry the delayed resonant reflectivity shows a Bragg peak almost exactly at the neutron value (Q = 1.25 nm^-1), while no Bragg peak is seen in the non-resonant x-ray reflectivity, whose electron density is homogeneous; the authors conclude that the synchrotron radiation was purely nuclear diffracted by the isotope periodicity of the multilayer and that no significant interdiffusion took place.
limitations: That the 56Fe layers do not scatter resonantly is the design premise; it is inferred from the pure nuclear Bragg peak, and the 56Fe layers are not measured on their own.
One isotopic pair in one alpha-iron film; the Bragg peak is strongly attenuated by roughness and no time spectrum could be recorded at it.
Only the laterally most homogeneous half of the sample was used for the synchrotron measurement; the counting window is given as 17-131 ns in the text and 17-146 ns in the Figure 5 caption.

studies.system: Saccharomyces cerevisiae wild type (JK9-3da) and null mutants of cell-wall-integrity signalling components (wsc1, wsc2, wsc3, wsc4, mid2, rom1, rom2, rho2, bni1, skn7, fks1, bck1, mpk1), haploid and diploid
studies.preparation: Cells grown in rich medium at 24 C are shifted to 37 C for timed intervals, fixed in 3.7 percent formaldehyde and stained with TRITC-phalloidin; small- and medium-budded cells with fewer than 50 percent of their actin patches in the bud are scored as depolarized (n > 200 per point). Zymolyase or 0.02 percent SDS impose cell wall stress at constant temperature, 1 M sorbitol stabilizes the wall osmotically, galactose-induced hyperactive RHO1, PKC1, BCK1 or MKK1 tests sufficiency, and latrunculin A tests the actin dependence of glucan synthase FKS1 redistribution.
studies.observable: Percentage of budded cells with a depolarized actin cytoskeleton over time, and FKS1, RHO1 and WSC1 localization
studies.finding: Heat shock depolarizes the actin cytoskeleton in about 95 percent of small- and medium-budded wild-type cells after about 30 min, with complete repolarization after about 120 min; Zymolyase or SDS cause depolarization that persists for the 120 min observed. wsc1 and rom2 null mutants are severely but not completely defective in depolarization (maximum about 55 and 40 percent, about 30 percent in a wsc1/wsc1 diploid), whereas the other single mutants depolarize like wild type. bck1 and mpk1 null mutants depolarize normally at 35 min, but most cells remain depolarized at 120 min and later. Hyperactivated RHO1 or PKC1, but not BCK1 or MKK1, is sufficient to depolarize actin; FKS1 redistribution requires the actin cytoskeleton.
limitations: One yeast; depolarization is a threshold score on actin patch distribution, a representative of three experiments.
Heat shock is the main stress; 1 M sorbitol only partly blocks its effect (data not shown).
rho1 and pkc1 nulls are inviable and not examined; cargo delivery along actin cables is not measured.

studies.system: Hadronic final states of e+e- annihilation recorded by DELPHI at LEP at centre-of-mass energies of 89-202 GeV and, in events with hard photon radiation, at hadronic energies of 45, 66 and 78 GeV; for the mean of 1 - thrust combined with published data of lower-energy experiments from 14 GeV
studies.preparation: Select hadronic events at the Z pole, at 89 and 93 GeV and at LEP2 energies up to 202 GeV with track, energy and thrust-axis cuts and cuts against radiative-return, two-photon and four-fermion backgrounds, and correct event-shape distributions and their means for detector effects with simulated events. Fit the energy dependence of seven event-shape means with renormalisation-group-invariant (RGI) perturbation theory at next-to-leading order, the scale parameter and beta0 free (or, assuming QCD with NC = CA = 3, the number of active flavours nf) and rho1 fixed to its QCD value. Repeat for the mean of 1 - thrust together with JADE, TASSO, PLUTO, L3, AMY, TOPAZ, MK II and HRS data, leaving out one low-energy experiment at a time for the systematic error, and fit the full logarithmic energy slope without the QCD beta1 to test light gluinos.
studies.observable: Leading coefficient beta0 of the QCD beta function, the number of active quark flavours nf and the logarithmic energy slope of the mean of 1 - thrust
studies.finding: The DELPHI event-shape means give a weighted mean beta0 = 7.7 +/- 0.9 +/- 0.1, or nf = 4.7 +/- 1.2 +/- 0.1, fully consistent with QCD. Including lower-energy data for the mean of 1 - thrust between 14 and 200 GeV, beta0 = 7.86 +/- 0.32 or, assuming QCD, nf = 4.75 +/- 0.44, against the QCD expectation beta0 = 7.67 = (33 - 2nf)/3 for nf = 5; the source expects the slope of the evolution to change at the b production threshold near 14 GeV. The fitted logarithmic slope, 8.70 +/- 0.35 against 8.32 in QCD and 5.66 with massless gluinos, whose loops the source states predict a weaker energy dependence, excludes light gluinos below 5 GeV. The source states that the energy dependence of alpha_s is governed by the beta function and relates the decrease of alpha_s with energy to asymptotic freedom.
limitations: beta0 is extracted with next-to-leading-order RGI perturbation theory with rho1 fixed to QCD; nf follows from beta0 only by assuming QCD with NC = CA = 3.
The precise result combines DELPHI with published lower-energy data whose statistical and systematic errors were combined; small power corrections are assumed negligible for the energy dependence.
The decomposition of beta0 into a gluon and a quark term is the QCD relation the source adopts, not a separate measurement of each term.

studies.system: Adult Nestin-thymidine-kinase transgenic mice on a C57BL/6 background with wild-type littermates, both sexes in age-matched litters
studies.preparation: Express herpes simplex virus thymidine kinase from a nestin promoter and enhancer so that ganciclovir kills only dividing nestin-expressing progenitors. Give ganciclovir (100 mg/kg intraperitoneally) daily for 14 days to transgenics and compare with ganciclovir-treated wild-type littermates and vehicle-treated transgenics. Label proliferation with bromodeoxyuridine or Ki67, count doublecortin-positive and NeuroD-positive immature granule cells stereologically and activated-caspase-3-positive cells, and repeat the labelling 1, 3, 4 and 9 weeks after ganciclovir withdrawal. All quantification is blind to genotype.
studies.observable: Subgranular-zone bromodeoxyuridine-positive and Ki67-positive cell numbers, doublecortin and NeuroD immature-neuron densities, activated-caspase-3-positive cell counts, and newborn neuron versus newborn glia double labels
studies.finding: Ganciclovir in transgenics reduced subgranular-zone proliferation to about half of the two control groups and significantly reduced doublecortin-positive and NeuroD-positive immature neurons, with roughly twice as many activated-caspase-3-positive cells; ganciclovir had no such effect in wild-type mice. Nine weeks after labelling, newborn neurons identified by NeuN and bromodeoxyuridine were reduced while newborn GFAP-positive glia were not. Proliferation measured with Ki67 had recovered within one week of withdrawal and doublecortin-positive cells within four weeks, and the reduction was reproduced in two further transgenic lines without weight loss or dentate inflammation.
limitations: The ablation is partial, about 50 percent of proliferation, and fully reversible, so it does not test the complete absence of the stem-cell compartment.
Subventricular-zone proliferation is reduced as well, so the manipulation is not hippocampus-specific.
Thymidine kinase plus ganciclovir kills dividing cells, which adds apoptotic debris to the niche.
This record covers the ablation and recovery characterisation; the water-maze and extinction experiments in the same paper lie outside the read extent.

studies.system: Healthy undergraduates: 62 in a three-week experience-sampling experiment and 25 right-handed participants in an fMRI experiment
studies.preparation: Randomly assign participants to acetaminophen or placebo pills taken daily for three weeks: 1,000 mg per day (30 against 32 participants) with nightly Hurt Feelings Scale and positive-emotion ratings in experiment 1; 2,000 mg per day (10 against 15) in experiment 2. At the end of experiment 2, scan participants at 3 T while they play a virtual ball-tossing game (Cyberball) with two presumed co-players, included in round 1 and excluded in round 2, and compare exclusion-versus-inclusion activity between groups in structurally defined dorsal anterior cingulate and anterior insula regions and in a whole-brain analysis.
studies.observable: Daily hurt feelings and positive emotion; BOLD activity during exclusion versus inclusion; self-reported social distress after the game
studies.finding: Hurt feelings declined over the three weeks with acetaminophen (slope -0.0081, P<0.05) but not with placebo and were lower from day 9 to day 21, while positive emotion did not change. In the scanner, the acetaminophen group showed less exclusion-related activity in the dorsal anterior cingulate cortex (t(23)=2.13, P<0.05) and bilateral anterior insula (t(23)=2.31, P<0.05) and, in whole-brain analysis, less in posterior insula, amygdala and other regions, with no region more active; self-reported social distress after exclusion did not differ between groups (P=0.24).
limitations: Small fMRI sample (10 acetaminophen and 15 placebo participants) and one exclusion episode.
Acetaminophen is an analgesic with an incompletely understood central mechanism; it alters pain-related affect, not affective processing selectively.
Self-reported distress after exclusion was unchanged; the supplemental material was not read.

studies.system: Mouse pancreatic beta cells with RIP-Cre-mediated conditional deletion of Dnmt1 (RIP-Cre:Dnmt1fl/fl), R26R-LacZ or R26R-YFP lineage tracing, and the Min6 beta-cell and alpha-TC1 cell lines
studies.preparation: Dnmt1 is deleted in beta cells by RIP-Cre, with Dnmt1fl/fl or RIP-Cre:Dnmt1fl/+ littermates as controls. Islets are examined from birth to 8 months by 5-methylcytosine staining, insulin/glucagon immunostaining with area quantification (n = 4 animals) and glucose tolerance tests (n = 5 per genotype); cells that transcribed the insulin gene are heritably labelled and scored for glucagon co-staining (n = 3 per group at 4 days and 8 months). Arx upstream-region methylation is mapped by MeDIP and bisulfite sequencing of FACS-purified alpha, beta and lineage-labelled cells, and Dnmt1, MeCP2 and Prmt6 siRNA knockdowns in Min6 cells test methylation, chromatin marks and lineage-marker expression.
studies.observable: Insulin- and glucagon-positive islet area, glucagon expression in lineage-traced former beta cells, glucose tolerance, Arx UR2 CpG methylation, histone marks and alpha/beta marker expression
studies.finding: Islets of conditional Dnmt1 mutants are normal at birth and in young mice, whose beta-cell DNA methylation is not yet reduced. With age, as dividing beta cells passively lose methylation, the mutants show reduced methylation, more glucagon-expressing and fewer insulin-expressing cells and abnormal glucose tolerance, and lineage tracing shows that glucagon-expressing cells derive from cells that had transcribed insulin, their number increasing dramatically in older mutants. The alpha-cell lineage determinant Arx is methylated in its UR2 region and repressed in beta cells, unmethylated in alpha cells and unmethylated in a subset of lineage-labelled Dnmt1-deficient cells; Dnmt1 knockdown in Min6 cells progressively demethylates UR2 with cell duplications and reduces MeCP2 binding, and MeCP2 or Prmt6 knockdown de-represses Arx with alpha markers. The authors conclude that propagation of DNA methylation during cell division is essential for repression of alpha-cell lineage genes to maintain beta-cell identity.
limitations: One cell type in mice; the conversion is gradual and partial and tied to beta-cell replication.
Converted cells are classified as alpha-like by glucagon and marker expression; RIP-Cre specificity is checked by immunohistology.
Small animal numbers (n = 3-5 per group); the MeCP2/PRMT6 mechanism rests mainly on cell-line knockdowns, and supplementary figures were not inspected.

studies.system: Budding yeasts Saccharomyces castellii (RNAi-competent; Δdcr1 and Δago1 deletions with ectopic rescue) and Saccharomyces cerevisiae, which lacks RNAi genes, with S. castellii DCR1 and AGO1 integrated into S. cerevisiae
studies.preparation: Delete DCR1 or AGO1 in S. castellii, confirm loss or reduction of siRNAs by RNA blot and small-RNA sequencing with ectopic rescue, and compare poly(A) mRNA-Seq of wild-type, Δago1 and Δdcr1 strains. In GFP-expressing S. cerevisiae, integrate S. castellii DCR1 alone or with AGO1 together with an inducible strong (hairpin) or weak (convergent) GFP silencing construct or none, and measure GFP siRNAs, GFP fluorescence by FACS and GFP mRNA; test a URA3 hairpin by growth without uracil and on 5-FOA; measure Ty1 Gag protein, Ty1 mRNA and HIS3-marked Ty1 transposition.
studies.observable: siRNA accumulation, mRNA-Seq transcript abundance, GFP fluorescence and mRNA, Ura3p-dependent growth, and Ty1 Gag protein, mRNA and transposition
studies.finding: S. cerevisiae lacks recognizable Argonaute, Dicer and RNA-dependent RNA polymerase homologs and siRNA-like small RNAs. In S. castellii, siRNAs fail to accumulate in Δdcr1 and are reduced in Δago1, both rescued by the deleted gene; the mutants are viable with no obvious growth disadvantage in minimal or rich media, and transcript-abundance changes are modest except the consensus Y' ORF, more than 7-fold higher in both mutants, and a palindromic Ty-fragment ORF, more than 4-fold higher in Δdcr1. In S. cerevisiae, Dcr1 alone yields GFP siRNAs; Dcr1 with Ago1 gives intermediate silencing with the weak and robust silencing with the strong construct, with a more than 100-fold decrease in GFP mRNA, silences an endogenous URA3 gene with phenotypic consequences, and strongly reduces Ty1 Gag protein, Ty1 mRNA and Ty1 transposition, the recipient strain showing no obvious abnormalities.
limitations: Removal and addition concern the Dicer-Argonaute RNAi pathway; other regulatory non-coding RNAs are not removed.

Expression without RNAi is shown by viability and transcript abundance in S. castellii mutants and by reporter and Ty1 expression in S. cerevisiae; regulated induction programmes are not measured separately.
In S. cerevisiae the pathway is reconstituted with integrated S. castellii genes and engineered silencing constructs; the authors note that overexpression may contribute.

studies.system: CD11b-DTR transgenic mice in carbon-tetrachloride-induced liver fibrosis and in its spontaneous resolution
studies.preparation: Transgenic mice expressing a human diphtheria-toxin-receptor-GFP fusion from CD11b regulatory elements (line 34) allow conditional killing of CD11b-expressing mononuclear phagocytes; specificity was checked by flow cytometry and cytology of peritoneal and splenic populations after two doses of toxin at 25 ng/g, which removed F4/80-positive macrophages while leaving CD3+, B220+ cells and granulocytes, and by selective loss of blood F4/80-positive monocytes from 6.5 +/- 3.3% to 1.5 +/- 1.3%. Fibrosis was induced by 12 weeks of carbon tetrachloride. In the injury arm, mice received three depleting doses of toxin, intraperitoneally or intravenously, or PBS, during the twelfth week; in the recovery arm, a separate cohort recovered spontaneously for one week while receiving toxin or PBS for five days from 48 hours after the last carbon tetrachloride. Livers were assessed by F4/80 staining for scar-associated macrophages, picrosirius red morphometry, collagen III and elastin staining, alpha-smooth-muscle-actin counts of activated hepatic stellate cells, BrdU uptake, apoptosis counts and a perisinusoidal fibrosis score.
studies.observable: Area of scar-associated macrophages; area of sirius-red-positive matrix, collagen III and elastin; number and proliferation and apoptosis of alpha-smooth-muscle-actin-positive stellate cells; perisinusoidal fibrosis score
studies.finding: Toxin treatment markedly attenuated scar-associated macrophages at peak fibrosis and reduced them by about 50% during recovery. Depletion during injury markedly reduced sirius red area and substantially reduced collagen III and elastin, and markedly reduced the number of alpha-smooth-muscle-actin-positive stellate cells, with fewer proliferating and fewer apoptotic scar-associated cells. Depletion during recovery had the opposite effect: sirius red material fell by 85% in controls between peak fibrosis and recovery but persisted in depleted mice, rising from 1% to more than 3% of the biopsy, the perisinusoidal fibrosis score stayed at 1.9 against 1.0 in recovering controls and 2.5 at peak fibrosis, collagen III was 50% higher and elastin showed no reduction, while the trend to persisting stellate cells was not significant. The source concludes that functionally distinct macrophage subpopulations act in the injury and the recovery phases of inflammatory scarring.
limitations: Diphtheria-toxin depletion removes CD11b-expressing mononuclear phagocytes as a population and does not isolate a defined activation or polarization state.
One toxic injury model in mouse liver, with short depletion windows and histological endpoints; the proposed matrix-degrading mechanism is inferred rather than tested here.
The recovery sampling time was chosen when most scar-associated macrophages had already left control livers, so overall macrophage numbers did not differ significantly at that point.
Persistence of activated stellate cells after depletion during recovery was a non-significant trend, so the mechanism of failed resolution is not established.

studies.system: CD11b-DTR transgenic mice during spontaneous recovery from carbon-tetrachloride-induced liver fibrosis
studies.preparation: Establish liver fibrosis in CD11b-DTR transgenic mice by repeated carbon tetrachloride over 12 weeks, then withhold further injections so that a recovery cohort resolves the scar spontaneously over one week. Deplete CD11b-positive scar-associated macrophages during that recovery window with diphtheria toxin, against PBS-treated diseased controls recovering with their macrophages intact, and against the companion experiment in which the same depletion is applied during the injury phase. Compare scar-associated macrophage numbers, sirius-red-stained matrix as a percentage of the biopsy, the perisinusoidal fibrosis score, collagen III, elastin and alpha-smooth-muscle-actin-positive cells, with peak fibrosis as the upper reference.
studies.observable: Scar-associated macrophage numbers, percentage of biopsy occupied by sirius red material, perisinusoidal fibrosis score, collagen III and elastin content and alpha-smooth-muscle-actin-positive cells
studies.finding: Removing macrophages during the recovery phase abolishes the resolution of the scar. Sirius red material decreased by 85 percent in control PBS-treated mice after recovery, whereas in macrophage-depleted mice it rose from 1 percent of the biopsy to more than 3 percent, and the perisinusoidal fibrosis score increased from 1.0 to 1.9 as a result of the depletion, against 2.5 at peak fibrosis in diseased controls. Depleted recovering livers held 50 percent more collagen III and showed no evidence of a reduction in elastin content, with a non-significant trend towards persistence of alpha-smooth-muscle-actin cells. The Abstract states that macrophage depletion during recovery, by contrast, led to a failure of matrix degradation, in contrast to depletion during the injury phase, which reduced the scar.
limitations: Conditional ablation of CD11b-positive cells removes monocytes and macrophages broadly rather than one resolution programme, and depends on a transgene-driven toxin system.
Resolution is measured as scar-matrix resorption and fibrosis scores in one organ, not as termination of an inflammatory cytokine state or clearance of apoptotic cells.
Scar-associated macrophage numbers in treated recovering livers fell by about half, and the overall difference from controls at day 7 was not significant because most had already gone in controls.
Matrix metalloproteinases and their inhibitors were not measured in the recovery experiments, so the degradation mechanism is inferred.

The read extent covers the Abstract, Results and Discussion of the PubMed Central full text: the Methods, which give the toxin doses and a schedule that differs from the one stated in the Results, the figures themselves and any supplemental material are outside it, and the page text ended inside the reference list.

studies.system: Fpr2-null mice and wild-type littermates in K/B x N serum-transfer arthritis, carrageenan paw edema and mesenteric ischemia-reperfusion
studies.preparation: Generate a mouse colony in which the murine formyl-peptide receptor 2 gene is deleted, with GFP in the Fpr2 promoter region, verifying deletion by Southern blot and PCR and the functional absence of the receptor by radioligand binding, and compare the knockouts with wild-type littermates. Induce arthritis by a single injection of 150 microlitres of pooled K/B x N arthrogenic serum on day 0 and score a clinical index of up to 22 points, one point per affected digit, tarsal or wrist joint, following the response to day 18 and recording cumulative incidence. In the same colony, measure carrageenan-induced paw swelling after 50 microlitres of 1 percent carrageenan with paw histology at 4 hours, and leukocyte adherence and emigration in mesenteric postcapillary venules 45 and 90 minutes after 30 minutes of ischemia. Test macrophage responses to Fpr2 ligands and the antimigratory actions of annexin A1, lipoxin A4, compound 43 and dexamethasone in wild-type and knockout mice.
studies.observable: Arthritis clinical index and its time course, cumulative disease incidence, paw volume, leukocyte adherence and emigration, and the antimigratory efficacy of pro-resolving agonists
studies.finding: Deleting one pro-resolving receptor leaves inflammation able to start but unable to finish. Administration of K/B x N serum provokes arthritis that peaks at day 7 in both strains, but the disease is strikingly exacerbated and prolonged in Fpr2-null mice, whose symptoms are still evident at day 18 when the response has subsided in wild-type mice, which the authors describe as the first evidence of a tonic inhibitory action mediated through Fpr2 in a model of chronic pathology. The same mice show increased leukocyte adherence and emigration after prolonged reperfusion and an augmented acute paw edema, about 2.5-fold at 4 hours and 60 percent higher at the 8-hour peak, with more infiltrating leukocytes on histology. In vitro, Fpr2-null macrophages do not respond to serum-amyloid-A-induced chemotaxis and show markedly attenuated ERK phosphorylation to the annexin A1 peptide Ac2-26 and other Fpr2 ligands, and in vivo the antimigratory properties of compound 43, lipoxin A4, annexin A1 and dexamethasone are notably reduced.
limitations: One G-protein-coupled receptor is deleted germline; the wider pro-resolving signalling network and other receptors for the same ligands remain.
Resolution is scored as a joint clinical index and paw volume, not as cellular clearance or mediator class switching.
No difference between genotypes appeared in IL-1beta air-pouch or zymosan-peritonitis trafficking, so the phenotype is model-dependent.
Serum-transfer arthritis is an innate-effector model in which the inflammatory trigger is given once; a chronic organism-scale inflammatory baseline is not measured.
The binding, chemotaxis and ERK figures and the Discussion were read only as the Abstract and Results text report them, and no supplementary material was read.

studies.system: Ultrahigh-purity Ne, Ar, Xe, N2, CO2 and N2O gases, with helium as the pressure reference, in the NIST MIRE triple-cell heterodyne laser refractometer at 293.15 K and 632.99 nm
studies.preparation: Pump all three cells of the MIRE triple-cell below 1 mPa and record the interferometer phase; fill the inner cell with gas and record the phase change, from which n - 1 follows (Eq. 5, corrected for window distortion), at pressures stepped from 50 to 500 kPa in 30 kPa increments, with overnight pump-down and new vacuum zeros. Pressure is realized with transducers calibrated in situ against helium refractivity, whose relation to pressure is calculated from first principles. Fit p = c1(n - 1) + c2(n - 1)^2 + c3(n - 1)^3 by weighted orthogonal distance regression, take the molar polarizability A_R = 2RT/(3c1) from the Lorentz-Lorenz relation and compare it with literature values, including static dielectric polarizabilities of neon and argon corrected to 633 nm.
studies.observable: Refractivity n - 1 of each gas versus pressure on the isotherm; proportionality coefficients c1-c3; molar polarizability A_R at 633 nm
studies.finding: For each gas the refractivity rises with pressure from the vacuum zero and is described by a gas-specific first-order coefficient, giving molar polarizabilities at 633 nm of 1.000211(16) cm3/mol for neon, 4.195685(64) for argon, 4.446107(68) for nitrogen, 6.64343(11) for carbon dioxide, 7.49921(12) for nitrous oxide and 10.39081(16) for xenon, each within 16 x 10^-6 relative standard uncertainty (Table III); dn/dp of argon and nitrogen is about 8 times and of nitrous oxide about 14 times that of helium. Static dielectric polarizabilities of neon and argon from another laboratory, corrected to 633 nm for dispersion and magnetic susceptibility, give 1.00028(6) and 4.1956(6) cm3/mol, in agreement with the refractive values within mutual uncertainties for neon and in excellent agreement for argon.
limitations: The conversion from refractivity to molar polarizability assumes the Lorentz-Lorenz relation, and the pressure scale rests on calculated helium refractivity.
The static polarizabilities and the dispersion corrections used in the comparison come from other studies that were not read.
Dilute gases at one wavelength and temperature; absorption, scattering and condensed media lie outside the preparation.
Read in the PMC NIST author manuscript; the supplementary data and the published version were not examined.
