studies.system: Thirty-nine healthy screened adults aged 18 to 36, randomly assigned to endotoxin (23) or placebo (16)
studies.preparation: In a randomised double-blind placebo-controlled design, give an intravenous bolus of Escherichia coli O113 endotoxin at 0.8 ng/kg or the same volume of saline. Sample blood hourly for interleukin-6 and tumour necrosis factor alpha, collect hourly self-reported sickness symptoms and depressed mood, and have a blinded experimenter rate depressed mood at baseline and two hours. Two hours after injection, scan participants during a monetary incentive delay task, analysing left and right ventral striatum regions of interest and the whole brain, with mediation analyses and a hippocampal-gyrus control region.
studies.observable: Circulating interleukin-6 and tumour necrosis factor alpha, self-reported and observer-rated depressed mood, task hit rates, reaction times and earnings, and ventral striatum BOLD signal during reward anticipation
studies.finding: Endotoxin raised cytokines, temperature, pulse and sickness symptoms and increased both self-reported and observer-rated depressed mood, with 43 percent of the endotoxin group rated as more depressed against 6 percent of the placebo group. Reward-anticipation activity in left ventral striatum was lower in the endotoxin group in both region-of-interest and whole-brain analyses, with no group difference in hit rates, reaction times or earnings, and the left ventral striatum cluster significantly mediated the relation between condition and observer-rated depressed mood while the control region did not.
limitations: A single acute endotoxin challenge in healthy young adults; chronic or low-grade inflammation is not modelled.
Unequal group sizes and a between-subjects design; the right ventral striatum region of interest showed no difference.
The self-reported mood effect was not independent of fatigue in the authors' earlier report of this sample.
Mediation is statistical, and one reward task at one time point is sampled.

studies.system: BALB/c mice persistently infected with 2 x 10^6 PFU LCMV clone 13, compared with LCMV Armstrong and naive mice
studies.preparation: Infected mice receive 250 micrograms of neutralising anti-IL-10 receptor antibody (1B1.3a) or rat IgG1 isotype control intraperitoneally, either from the start on days 0, 7 and 14 or therapeutically on days 7 and 14 after infection, once the response is already under way. Splenocytes are taken on days 20 and 150, counted, stimulated with the immunodominant NP118-126 peptide for 5 h with brefeldin A and stained intracellularly for IFN-gamma; PD-1 expression on CD4 and CD8 T cells is measured 90 days after infection, and IL-10 in 48 h splenocyte culture supernatant by ELISA.
studies.observable: Spleen cell numbers, IL-10 production by cultured splenocytes, numbers of IFN-gamma-producing CD8 T cells after peptide restimulation, percentage of PD-1-expressing T cells, and viral titres
studies.finding: Persistent clone 13 infection is associated with deletion of virus-specific CD8 T cells, lymphopenia and drastically increased IL-10 production. Anti-IL-10R treatment, given from day 0 or therapeutically on days 7 and 14, reverses the lymphopenia, significantly reduces endogenous IL-10 production, and yields significantly higher numbers of IFN-gamma-secreting CD8 T cells than isotype-treated mice, particularly at later time points, with the therapeutic regimen producing a similar enhancement. T cells from isotype-treated infected mice show as much as a 25-fold induction of PD-1 over naive mice, and anti-IL-10R treatment reduces PD-1 expression about threefold relative to isotype control at day 90. The treated mice resolve the persistent infection without immunopathology.
limitations: One mouse strain and one persistent virus; the blockade removes signalling through a single cytokine receptor.
The antibody acts on all IL-10-responsive cells, so the effect is not restricted to the exhausted CD8 T cells themselves.
The authors state it is difficult to determine whether the enhanced CD8 response is cause or consequence of the reduced viral load.
Function is read as IFN-gamma production after peptide restimulation and PD-1 as a single surface marker; the wider exhaustion program is not profiled.
Read in the Europe PMC full text with figure legends; supplemental material was not inspected.

studies.system: Csf1r-null mice (exon 5 deletion) on a C57Bl/6N background with littermate controls, Csf1-null (Csf1op/op) mice and Csf1r-EGFP reporter mice
studies.preparation: Compare brains of Csf1r-null mice and wild-type littermates at embryonic day 16, postnatal day 1 and three weeks of age by Iba1 and F4/80 immunostaining, counting labelled cells per region in matched sections with non-parametric tests and quantifying cell circularity. Examine ventricular and parenchymal morphology, myelination and cortical Nissl, NeuN, Nogo-A and GFAP counts. Because receptor nulls rarely survive to adulthood, test olfaction by food finding in viable Csf1-null mice, and use the Csf1r-EGFP reporter with lineage antibodies to ask which brain cells express the receptor.
studies.observable: Iba1-positive and F4/80-positive cell numbers and shape by brain region, ventricle size and parenchymal architecture, cortical neuron, astrocyte and oligodendrocyte counts, food-finding performance, and reporter co-localisation
studies.finding: Microglia were more than 99 percent depleted at embryonic day 16 and postnatal day 1 and about 94 percent depleted overall at three weeks, from 99 percent in thalamus and hypothalamus to about 65 percent in piriform cortex, and the few remaining Iba1-positive cells were rounded rather than ramified. Embryonic brain development appeared normal while postnatal architecture became perturbed, with enlarged ventricles, compressed parenchyma most marked in olfactory bulb and cortex, higher cortical neuronal density, more astrocytes and fewer oligodendrocytes. The reporter was expressed only in microglia and macrophages, and Csf1-null mice had significantly impaired olfaction.
limitations: A constitutive germline receptor deletion: the depletion is developmental, so secondary consequences cannot be separated from the acute loss of microglial function.
Receptor nulls rarely survive past three weeks and the brains examined are from young animals; counts are bimodal and summarised as medians.
Olfaction was tested in the ligand-null genotype, not in the receptor null.
The circuit consequences recorded here are structural and histological; no circuit function was measured.

studies.system: Patient SM, a 44-year-old woman with focal bilateral amygdala lesions and a neuropsychological profile stable for two decades, compared with five healthy female viewers for the film clips and with normative samples for the questionnaires
studies.preparation: Expose the patient to three classes of fear-inducing situation with her written informed consent: live snakes and spiders in an exotic pet store, a professionally staged haunted house, and ten fear-inducing film clips interleaved with clips targeting disgust, anger, sadness, happiness and surprise; record overt behaviour, especially avoidance or withdrawal, query her fear on a 0 to 10 scale during each situation, administer eight validated fear questionnaires repeatedly over three years, sample her emotional state at three random times a day for three months with 50 emotion terms, and interview her about past threatening events with police reports as corroboration.
studies.observable: Overt behavioural signs of fear or avoidance, self-reported fear ratings, questionnaire scores converted to percent of maximum possible, and experience-sampling ratings of 50 emotion terms
studies.finding: The patient showed no avoidance in any of the three situations: she held a snake for over three minutes, asked fifteen times to touch larger snakes the staff had called dangerous, tried to touch a tarantula, led strangers through the haunted house and approached and poked the staged monsters, with fear ratings never above 2 and zero throughout the haunted house. She reported little or no fear across all ten fear films while showing and reporting the appropriate emotion for the other clips, scored near floor on all eight questionnaires on every occasion, and across 156 experience-sampling points rated afraid, nervous, scared and fearful at the lowest possible level while reporting every other basic emotion, with fearless the highest-rated of the 50 terms. Past events in which her life was threatened were recalled without fear, though with anger and distress.
limitations: A single human case with a rare bilateral lesion, so individual history cannot be separated from the lesion.
Fear was measured from overt behaviour and self-report, not from a physiological marker in these sessions.
Emotions other than fear were preserved, so the dependence shown is specific to fear rather than to affective processing as a whole.
No matched experience-sampling control group was collected.

studies.system: Ketosteroid isomerase (wild type and the conservative active-site mutants Tyr16Phe, Tyr16Ser, Asp103Asn and Asp40Asn) with the bound product-like inhibitor 19-nortestosterone as a vibrational probe
studies.preparation: Calibrate the carbonyl stretch of 19-nortestosterone as a field probe in two ways: Stark spectroscopy of the frozen glass at 77 K under a known external field of 1.0 MV/cm, and infrared spectra in a series of solvents of increasing polarity whose average field on the C=O bond is computed by molecular dynamics. Then record infrared spectra of 19-nortestosterone bound to wild-type and mutant KSI, confirming band assignment with the C=18O isotopologue, map the measured frequencies onto the field scale and plot the apparent activation barrier of each variant, calculated from its kcat taken from the literature, against the field.
studies.observable: Stark tuning rate of the C=O stretch; C=O peak frequency and linewidth in solvents and in each enzyme variant; ensemble-average active-site electric field; apparent activation free energy
studies.finding: The C=O stretch shifts about 1.4/f cm-1 per MV/cm, and across solvents from hexane (1690.2 cm-1) to water (1634.0 cm-1) the frequency tracks the computed solvent field linearly (R2 = 0.99). Bound in wild-type KSI the same bond absorbs at 1588.3 cm-1, 46 cm-1 further red than in water, mapping to an ensemble-average field of -144 +/- 6 MV/cm in an unusually narrow band. The conservative mutations shift the band towards the blue in proportion to their catalytic cost: Tyr16Phe, which lowers the rate about 10^4-fold, moves it to 1647.5 cm-1 (a field of -60 +/- 3 MV/cm), Tyr16Ser less so and Asp103Asn least. Activation barrier and field are linearly related (slope 1.05, R2 = 0.98), and extrapolating to zero field gives 18.8 kcal/mol against 11.5 for the wild type, so the active-site field contributes 7.3 +/- 0.4 kcal/mol, about 70 percent of the catalytic speed-up. The general base Asp40Asn breaks the trend, shifting the frequency by only 6 cm-1 while costing 10^6-fold in rate, which the authors assign to an orthogonal, positioning function.
limitations: One enzyme and one bound inhibitor; the probe reports the field at a single bond at one position in the active site, and nitrile probes elsewhere in the same site report ordinary fields.

The wild-type frequency lies outside the range calibrated by solvatochromism, so the quoted field relies on extrapolated linearity, which the authors estimate may overestimate the field by up to 10 percent.
The mutants change the field and the structure together; the partition of the catalytic effect assumes that the field at the C=O bond is the same in substrate and transition state.
kcat values for the variants are taken from the cited literature, not measured here, and classical simulations did not reproduce the measured fields.
The supplementary methods, texts and tables were not read.

studies.system: Adult male Sprague Dawley rats with cell-body-specific lesions of the thalamus (10 injected, 6 sham), the basal forebrain (11 with orexin-saporin, 5 with IgG192-saporin, 5 with the lower orexin-saporin dose) or the parabrachial-precoeruleus complex (4 precoeruleus, 7 medial and 5 lateral parabrachial, 11 for the whole complex, 8 adjacent control lesions)
studies.preparation: Inject ibotenic acid into the thalamus or saporin immunotoxins into the basal forebrain or the parabrachial-precoeruleus complex, implant EEG and EMG electrodes in the same surgery, record continuously from the seventh postoperative day for at least seven days with states scored in 12 s epochs before histology and blind to lesion extent, then stimulate the animals behaviourally for two hours, by moving between open cages or by gentle handling when they were unresponsive, and process the brains for Nissl staining, choline acetyltransferase and c-Fos immunohistochemistry.
studies.observable: Percentage of time in wake, NREM and REM sleep by light and dark period, EEG power spectra and sleep spindles, behavioural responsiveness, and numbers of c-Fos-expressing neurons in cingulate cortex, tuberomammillary nucleus, orexin neurons and locus coeruleus
studies.finding: Rats with nearly complete thalamic lesions had unchanged amounts of NREM and REM sleep and a wake, NREM and REM power spectrum indistinguishable from controls apart from reduced nocturnal theta, with normal cortical c-Fos during arousal, but sleep spindles were no longer seen at NREM-REM transitions or at other times. Seven of eleven rats with large bilateral basal forebrain lesions abruptly entered a coma-like state about ten days after injection, unresponsive to sound and pinch, with a monotonous sub-1 Hz EEG and cingulate c-Fos of 5.0 plus or minus 1.3 against 75.5 plus or minus 10.3 in sham controls, while tuberomammillary, orexin and locus coeruleus c-Fos stayed at waking levels; selective cholinergic or selective non-cholinergic basal forebrain lesions changed neither sleep-wake amounts nor power spectra nor c-Fos. Lesions of the whole parabrachial-precoeruleus complex produced coma with a continuous slow-wave EEG and cingulate c-Fos of 6.0 plus or minus 3.5, whereas lateral or medial parabrachial lesions alone only increased dark-period sleep and adjacent pontine control lesions changed little.
limitations: Rats, and consciousness is inferred from behavioural responsiveness, cortical EEG and c-Fos rather than measured directly.

Saporin immunotoxins kill the targeted cell bodies over days and their selectivity is incomplete; modest damage to the pedunculopontine tegmentum and locus coeruleus was present in the comatose animals.
Animals were euthanized after five to seven days of coma, so recovery was not assessed.
Lesions were made in adult animals, so they bear on the dependence of the waking regime, not on its ontogeny.

studies.journal: The London, Edinburgh, and Dublin Philosophical Magazine and Journal of Science
studies.system: Alpha particles from radium emanation and radium C scattered by thin foils of carbon, aluminium, copper, silver, tin and gold, counted by zinc-sulphide scintillations
studies.preparation: Narrow, intense alpha pencils in evacuated chambers strike thin foils. Scintillations of the scattered particles on a zinc-sulphide screen are counted, over 100,000 in total, as functions of scattering angle, foil thickness, foil material (thickness expressed as stopping-power air equivalent, with counts corrected for source decay and alpha slowing) and alpha velocity. The fraction scattered through 45 degrees by gold is found against the counted or gamma-calibrated main beam.
studies.observable: Scintillations per unit area versus angle, thickness, atomic weight and velocity, and the absolute fraction scattered through 45 degrees
studies.finding: The counts follow Rutherford's single-scattering law for an atom with a strong central charge concentrated in dimensions small compared with the atom: the number scattered varies as 1/sin^4(phi/2) from 5 to 150 degrees while the counts change from 1 to 250,000, is proportional to thickness for thin foils, varies per atom approximately as the square of the atomic weight from carbon to gold, and approximately as the inverse fourth power of the alpha velocity. The fraction of radium C alpha particles scattered through 45 degrees by gold foil of 1 mm air equivalent gives a central charge of about half the atomic weight in elementary charges, correct to about 20 percent. The authors state that the results afford strong evidence that an atom contains a strong charge at the centre, of dimensions small compared with the diameter of the atom.
limitations: The compact central charge is inferred from the agreement of the scattering laws with Rutherford's theory; its composition from protons and neutrons is not measured.
Atoms from carbon to gold only; hydrogen, whose nucleus is a single proton, is not tested.
Scintillation counting with about 20 percent uncertainty on the central charge; the ratio of counts to A^(3/2) rises slightly with decreasing atomic weight.
The angle, thickness and velocity tables on pages 607-615 and 618-621 were read only through the authors' summary.

studies.system: Negatively charged hexagonal boron nitride nanospheres (TEM diameter about 110 nm, zeta potential -41 mV at pH 7 and 1 mM) dispersed at 5 mg/L in aqueous salt solutions at 25 C
studies.preparation: Synthesize the nanospheres by chemical vapour deposition from trimethyl borate and ammonia with annealing, characterize them by XRD, FTIR and TEM, and add them from a stock dispersion to filtered solutions of NaCl, KCl, CsCl, NaNO3, CH3COONa, MgCl2, LaCl3, K2SO4 or K3[Fe(CN)6] over a wide concentration range at pH 7. Follow the early stage of aggregation by time-resolved dynamic light scattering (100 consecutive measurements), take the apparent aggregation rate coefficient from the initial slope of the hydrodynamic radius, normalize it to the diffusion-controlled rate measured in each system to obtain the stability ratio, and measure electrophoretic mobilities under the same conditions to derive zeta potentials and slip-plane charge densities.
studies.observable: Stability ratio W versus salt concentration and valence, critical coagulation concentrations, zeta potentials and charge densities
studies.finding: At low concentrations of every monovalent salt the stability ratio was of order 10^3 (slow aggregation); it fell with rising salt concentration until it reached unity, where aggregation is diffusion controlled, the same for all monovalent salts with a CCC of about 0.25 M. The zeta potentials became less negative with salt as the double layer was compressed, with a charge density of about -14 mC/m2 for all monovalent ions. Multivalent counterions lowered the CCC to 30 mM (Mg2+) and 0.7 mM (La3+) and reduced the charge density (to -4 and -0.6 mC/m2), multivalent coions only to 110 mM (SO4 2-) and 75 mM (Fe(CN)6 3-), following the direct and inverse Schulze-Hardy rules. The CCCs calculated from the measured charge densities with a DLVO relation (fitted Hamaker constant 4.0 x 10^-21 J) agreed with the measured ones; the authors conclude that double-layer repulsion stabilizes the dispersions at low ionic strength and that, once salt screens it, van der Waals attraction makes the particles aggregate rapidly.
limitations: One particle type at one particle concentration and pH; the dispersed state is followed only in the early stage of aggregation.
The attribution to double-layer repulsion and van der Waals attraction rests on DLVO fits with a fitted Hamaker constant.
Salt screens or reduces the particle charge rather than removing ionic interactions; sterically stabilized dispersions are not studied.

studies.system: Aqueous bovine serum albumin at 13 weight percent, and pure water, between -25 and 85 degrees C
studies.preparation: The unfolding of the protein is located by circular dichroism, taking the temperature at which the alpha-helix fraction reaches 41 percent, the midpoint between 66 and 16 percent, and by differential scanning calorimetry over three heating cycles between 25 and 85 degrees C. The hydration of the same solutions is then measured three ways: attenuated-total-reflection terahertz time-domain spectroscopy between 0.3 and 2.5 THz, whose fitted slow-relaxation amplitude gives the number of water molecules whose collective rotation is bound; differential scanning calorimetry of the melting enthalpy before and after heating to a chosen temperature, which gives the unfreezable water; and infrared spectroscopy of the OH stretching region fitted with three Gaussians for strong, intermediate and weak hydrogen bonds. Pure water is measured in parallel under the same conditions, with four to six repeats per condition.
studies.observable: Alpha-helix fraction, DSC curves and melting enthalpies, the terahertz hydration number per protein, the unfreezable-water number per protein, and the fractions of the three OH stretching bands
studies.finding: The protein unfolds irreversibly at about 60 degrees C by both circular dichroism and calorimetry, the endothermic peak appearing only in the first heating. The terahertz hydration number falls gradually from about 3300 at 25 degrees C while the protein is native and then jumps upward at 60 degrees C, whereas the number of unfreezable water molecules, about 2000 in the native state, falls on denaturation; the infrared band fractions, which follow pure water below 60 degrees C, change at the transition towards stronger water-water hydrogen bonds. The authors conclude that unfolding exposes hydrophobic groups that acquire weakly bound water held by stronger water-water hydrogen bonds, while the entangling of hydrophilic groups removes sites for strongly bound water.
limitations: One model protein at a single high concentration; unfolding is produced by heating, so temperature and conformation change together and the native values come from the same heating series.

Hydration numbers are model-dependent: the terahertz number comes from a fitted relaxation amplitude with the other parameters fixed, and the unfreezable water from melting enthalpies, so the two methods count different water.
The hydration shell changes rather than disappears: the denatured protein still structures water, and no ionic distribution is measured.

A 2024 Correction revises the description of the melting anomaly and the axis label of Figure 4b and states that Figure 3 and the conclusions do not change; the supporting-information tables were not read.

studies.system: Interleukin-1 receptor antagonist-deficient mice on BALB/cA and C57BL/6J genetic backgrounds, with wild-type and heterozygous littermates
studies.preparation: Replace all exons of the secreted form of the IL-1 receptor antagonist gene with a neo cassette, destroying all four isoforms, and backcross the mutation five to eight generations onto BALB/cA or C57BL/6J. Intercross heterozygotes to obtain homozygous mutants with wild-type and heterozygous littermate controls, keep mice specific-pathogen-free, and examine each joint weekly for swelling and redness on a graded severity scale. studies.observable: Incidence and severity of joint swelling, joint histopathology, and joint transcript levels of IL-1beta, IL-1alpha, IL-6, TNF-alpha, COX-2, IL-1RI and IL-1RII
studies.finding: Loss of the endogenous IL-1 inhibitor produces joint-restricted chronic inflammation. On the BALB/cA background the first signs appear at 5 weeks, over 80 percent of mutants are arthritic before 8 weeks and all are arthritic by 13 weeks, whereas no wild-type or heterozygous littermate develops arthritis. Histology of the ankle joints shows marked synovial and periarticular inflammation with proliferating synovial lining cells, pannus formation, neutrophil and lymphocyte invasion, fibrin clots in the synovial space and articular and bone erosion with activated osteoclasts, and no other histopathological abnormality is found. The same mediators are already elevated in non-arthritic joints at 4 weeks and at 10 to 12 weeks, which the source reads as low normal IL-1 levels inducing inflammatory genes once the antagonist is absent. None of the mutants on the C57BL/6J background is arthritic at 16 weeks, so a further genetic factor is required.
limitations: One tissue, the joint, in one knockout; whether other tissue inflammatory microenvironments depend on the same cytokine set-point is not tested.
The phenotype is strain-dependent and absent on a C57BL/6J background at 16 weeks, so the shifted cytokine baseline is not sufficient on its own.
Autoantibodies against immunoglobulin G, type II collagen and double-stranded DNA also rise, so an adaptive contribution is not excluded.
Joint mediator levels are Northern-blot transcript measurements on pooled joint tissue without protein or spatially resolved data.

studies.system: Twitter Home-timeline users in a randomized holdback experiment maintained since June 2016 (58,087,969 account IDs on 5 June 2020, 20% in control), with original tweets of 3,634 legislator accounts in seven countries and tweets linking to rated US news sources
studies.preparation: When Twitter introduced machine-learning personalization of the Home timeline in 2016, a randomly chosen control group of accounts was kept on reverse-chronological timelines of the accounts they follow, while a treatment sample received the personalized ranking (with an opt-out). Count linger impressions (at least 50% of a tweet visible for 500 ms) of original tweets by legislators of major parties in the United States, Japan, the United Kingdom, France, Spain, Canada and Germany (reach within each country) and of 2020 tweets linking to news sources rated by AllSides and Ad Fontes Media, and compare reach in the treatment and control groups.
studies.observable: Amplification ratio: reach of a set of tweets among treatment-group users relative to control-group users, 0% meaning equal proportional reach, for parties, individual legislators and media-bias categories
studies.finding: Personalized ranking raised the reach of every studied party's tweets above chronological timelines, in some cases by more than 200%. In six of seven countries the mainstream right was amplified significantly more than the mainstream left (Canada Liberals 43% against Conservatives 167%, United Kingdom Labour 112% against Conservatives 176%; Germany not significant), while individual legislators' amplification ranged from below 0% to 400% with no significant association with party, and far-left and far-right parties were generally amplified less than moderate ones. With AllSides ratings, partisan news sources were amplified more than Center sources and the partisan Right marginally more than the partisan Left; with Ad Fontes ratings the partisan Left was amplified least (10.5%).
limitations: Treatment and control users share one platform and see each other's content, so the comparison violates the no-interference assumption; the source reports simple group comparisons rather than causal effect estimates and expects interference to shrink the differences.
The ranking algorithm changed over time and was tuned with this comparison; amplification measures exposure through linger impressions, not attention, beliefs or discourse.
One platform; the news-source results depend on the media-bias rating used; the authors were employed by or consulting for Twitter; the SI Appendix was not read.

studies.system: Rods of mice lacking the CNGB1 subunit of the rod cyclic nucleotide-gated channel (CNGB1-/-) and wild-type controls
studies.preparation: Gene targeting of CNGB1; immunolabeling of CNGA1 in rod outer segments, including strong laser intensities to detect residual subunit; suction-electrode recordings from single rods at P17; dark-adapted and light-adapted electroretinograms in 1- and 6-month-old mice.
studies.observable: CNGA1 in rod outer segments, single-rod light responses and rod- and cone-driven ERG responses
studies.finding: In the absence of CNGB1 only trace amounts of CNGA1 were found on rod outer segments. The vast majority of isolated CNGB1-/- rods failed to respond to light: only 3 of 35 recorded P17 rods responded, with amplitudes 10-15 percent of the wild-type response. CNGB1-/- mice showed no rod-mediated ERG responses; their dark-adapted mixed response lacked a substantial a-wave and appeared only from about 10-30 mcd/m2, resembling cone-only mice, while light-adapted cone responses did not differ from controls. The rods degenerated slowly by apoptosis, with retinal gliosis. The authors conclude that the rod system is not functional in the CNGB1-/- mouse.
limitations: The channel is lost from the outer segment through impaired CNGA1 targeting; a few rods with residual homomeric CNGA1 channels gave small responses.
Mouse rods with slow degeneration; upstream steps of the cascade (transducin and PDE6 activation) were not measured.
Residual rod signals below ERG detection are not excluded.

studies.system: Single-ring GroEL variant GroELSR with concatenated GroES7 cochaperonins carrying I25A or I25D mutations in selected modules, and the double-ring GroEL-GroES system for comparison; malate dehydrogenase as folding substrate and the conditional-lethal Escherichia coli strain MGM100 for function in vivo
studies.preparation: Express a concatenated groES7 gene so that mutations can be placed in one, two or three of the seven GroES modules instead of all seven, purify the variants and measure the inhibition of GroEL or GroELSR ATPase activity (malachite green), the binding affinity by microscale thermophoresis in the presence of ADP, and the refolding of guanidine-unfolded malate dehydrogenase from its recovered enzymatic activity (1 microM GroEL or 2 microM GroELSR, 4 microM cochaperonin, 0.7 microM monomeric MDH, at least three independent experiments). Test chaperone function in vivo by complementing MGM100 at 37 and 42 C with each GroELSR-GroES7 pair.
studies.observable: Fractional inhibition of ATPase activity; dissociation constants; yield and kinetics of malate dehydrogenase refolding; growth of the conditional-lethal strain
studies.finding: Weakening the chaperonin-cochaperonin interface in a graded way turned a non-functional single-ring chaperonin into a working one. With unmutated GroES, GroELSR refolded less than 10 percent of the unfolded malate dehydrogenase, because the tight complex traps the substrate; one mutated module raised the yield to 20-30 percent, and two mutated modules gave both yield and kinetics comparable to the canonical double-ring GroEL-GroES, while a third module returned the yield to the minimum. In parallel, one mutated module lifted ATPase inhibition from about 90 to 80 percent and raised Kd from 3.7 +/- 2.2 to 8.5 +/- 3.3 nM, two modules relieved inhibition to about 50 percent, as in the canonical system, and weakened binding more than tenfold, and three modules abolished detectable binding. Three variants, GroES7I25A1,3, GroES7I25D1,4 and GroES7I25A1,4,7, supported growth of the conditional-lethal strain with GroELSR at both 37 and 42 C, although in vivo function did not track the refolding yield. The authors conclude that a working interaction must be neither too tight nor too loose.
limitations: One chaperonin system with an engineered single-ring GroEL and a concatenated cochaperonin, so the quantitative values need not carry over to the natural double-ring cycle.
The authors note that refolding activity and function in vivo did not correlate, and that malate dehydrogenase is not an authentic cellular substrate.
The interface mutations change binding, ATPase inhibition and cycling together, so inter-subunit coupling is not separated from affinity in a single step.
Folding is scored as recovered enzymatic activity in a bulk assay, and the supplementary tables with the individual Kd and yield values were not read.

studies.system: Germ-free C57BL/6J mice and germ-free mice conventionalized with the microbiome of specific-pathogen-free wild-type mice, with alpha-naphthylisocyanate- or 3,5-diethoxycarbonyl-1,4-dihydrocollidine-induced cholestasis
studies.preparation: Rear mice germ-free and conventionalize a subset by gavage with faecal matter from specific-pathogen-free wild-type mice three weeks before the experiment. Induce cholestasis with alpha-naphthylisocyanate at 100 mg per kg by oral gavage for 48 hours, or with a 0.1 per cent dihydrocollidine diet for one week, against vehicle controls. Pretreat subsets of conventionalized mice with clodronate liposomes at 10 mL per kg intraperitoneally 24 hours before, at the time of and 24 hours after the gavage, or with the NLRP3-specific inhibitor MCC950 at 20 mg per kg alongside the gavage and 24 hours after. Measure intestinal permeability as serum fluorescein isothiocyanate after oral administration, tight-junction proteins by western blot on duodenum, jejunum, ileum and colon with occludin immunofluorescence, circulating lipopolysaccharide-binding protein, liver immune-cell composition by flow cytometry, and faecal microbiome composition by 16S ribosomal RNA sequencing, with four to eight animals per group.
studies.observable: Serum fluorescein isothiocyanate after oral gavage, colonic occludin and E-cadherin protein, colonic AKT phosphorylation, circulating lipopolysaccharide-binding protein, regional intestinal TNF and IL1beta, liver macrophage infiltration and cleaved caspase 1 and IL1beta, serum transaminases and alkaline phosphatase, and faecal 16S microbiome composition
studies.finding: In conventionalized germ-free mice, cholestasis raised serum fluorescein isothiocyanate more than tenfold and reduced tight-junction protein expression, most markedly in the colon, where TNF and IL1beta reached their highest concentrations; in germ-free mice the same insult raised fluorescein isothiocyanate only moderately with a mild attenuation of tight-junction proteins. Depleting macrophages with clodronate liposomes and inhibiting NLRP3 with MCC950 each reduced serum fluorescein isothiocyanate, restored colonic occludin and E-cadherin, attenuated colonic AKT phosphorylation and lowered circulating lipopolysaccharide-binding protein, alongside reduced liver macrophage infiltration, practically undetectable cleaved caspase 1 and cleaved IL1beta, reduced liver inflammation and transaminases and improved liver histology. Alkaline phosphatase and hepatic bile-acid accumulation were comparable with the untreated cholestatic group, so the protection did not come from a lower degree of cholestasis. Both interventions also shifted faecal microbiome composition, with no significant difference between the clodronate and MCC950 groups.
limitations: Clodronate liposomes remove macrophages rather than re-biasing their activation between states, and MCC950 inhibits one activation route, so the preparation does not vary a polarization bias while holding macrophage number fixed.
A 48-hour chemically induced cholestasis model, not a chronic barrier-failure or metabolic-endotoxemia regime.
Translocation is inferred from serum fluorescein isothiocyanate and lipopolysaccharide-binding protein; endotoxin activity was not assayed and no organ cultures were reported.
Four to eight animals per group, and the supporting figures holding the dihydrocollidine arm and the binding-protein data were not read.

studies.system: Laser-cooled one-component plasmas of 10^5 to 10^6 9Be+ ions at densities of 10^8 to 10^9 cm^-3 in a cylindrical Penning trap (B = 4.465 T)
studies.preparation: Confine 9Be+ ions in a Penning trap, whose magnetic field takes the place of the uniform neutralizing background of a one-component plasma, and cool them with a 313 nm laser beam along the field axis tuned below a hyperfine-Zeeman component of the 2s 2S1/2 to 2p 2P3/2 transition (estimated T about 10 mK, coupling parameter about 200). Sweep the laser frequency over 10 to 30 s from several gigahertz to 10 MHz below resonance, carrying the plasma from above to below the liquid-solid transition temperature. Record time-integrated and stroboscopic (rotation-synchronized, passive or phase-locked timing) optical Bragg diffraction patterns with an imaging photomultiplier and a gated intensified CCD, and determine the rotation frequency and density from photon correlations.
studies.observable: Optical Bragg diffraction: ring and spot positions in units of q a_WS compared with bcc and fcc lattices, single-crystal patterns, orientation and size of the ordered region
studies.finding: In about 30% of the cooling sweeps a pattern of several sharp rings appeared, indicating that a crystal had formed. For approximately spherical plasmas of 270,000 and 470,000 ions the peak positions agreed with a bcc lattice within the 2.5% angular calibration and disagreed by about 10% with an fcc lattice, and the ratios of the first five peaks agreed with bcc within about 1%. Stroboscopic patterns resolved single bcc crystals (for example a square grid for a <100> orientation, grid spacing within about 1% of the calculated one) with a cubic lattice spacing of 17 micrometres and ordered regions at least about 14 lattice spacings (about 6000 ions) across; oblate plasmas also showed hexagonal fcc-like spots that the authors attribute to surface layers.
limitations: A one-component plasma of like-charged ions held by the trap; cation-anion salt crystallization is not tested.
Crystal formation is inferred from the appearance of Bragg patterns after cooling sweeps; the temperature is estimated and the melting transition is not characterized.
Finite plasmas with a 17 micrometre lattice spacing whose surface layers depart from the bulk bcc structure.

studies.system: Awake head-fixed mice with multielectrode recordings in the whisker barrel cortex: 5 intact and 6 olfactory-bulbectomized animals, plus 3 anaesthetised tracheotomized animals
studies.preparation: Record local field potentials and spikes in the barrel cortex while monitoring respiration non-invasively from air temperature at the nostrils, and compare intact animals with animals whose olfactory bulb has been surgically removed, quantifying the coherence between respiration and the field potential at the respiratory frequency over 50 s segments. Then, in separate anaesthetised animals, open the trachea so that spontaneous breathing bypasses the nose, monitor respiration from chest movement and drive an artificial nasal airflow of about 0.15 ml at 0.8, 1.6 and 3.2 Hz; finally, with nasal airflow eliminated by tracheotomy, stimulate the ipsilateral olfactory bulb electrically at the same three frequencies.
studies.observable: Coherence and cross-correlation between respiration or nasal airflow and the barrel-cortex field potential, delta-band oscillation, delta-gamma phase-amplitude coupling, and stimulus-locked field fluctuations
studies.finding: Olfactory bulbectomy eliminated barrel-cortex delta-band oscillations and the correlation between respiration and the field potential, reducing respiration-field coherence by 91 percent on average (p less than 0.001), and also eliminated delta-gamma phase-amplitude coupling. In tracheotomized animals the field potential was only weakly correlated with tracheal respiration but strongly correlated with the artificial nasal airflow at all three frequencies, highest at 1.6 Hz, and with nasal airflow removed, rhythmic electrical stimulation of the olfactory bulb produced stimulus-locked rhythmic field fluctuations in the barrel cortex.
limitations: Mice, one cortical area and a small number of animals per condition.
Bulbectomy removes a whole structure, and the tracheotomy and stimulation controls are in anaesthetised animals.
Respiration was monitored from nostril temperature or chest movement rather than from airflow volume in the awake condition.
The delta-gamma coupling analyses themselves and the figures were not read or inspected here.

studies.system: Mouse embryos and embryonic stem cells carrying a targeted null mutation of Hif1a, the gene of the oxygen-regulated HIF-1alpha subunit
studies.preparation: Hif1a was disrupted by homologous recombination in embryonic stem cells and transmitted through the germ line. Hif1a-/-, Hif1a+/- and Hif1a+/+ embryos from heterozygous intercrosses were harvested, staged by somite number and genotyped from yolk sacs. Vascular pattern was compared by whole-mount immunoperoxidase staining for the endothelial marker PECAM at E8.5-E8.75, E9.25 and E9.75; cranial and cardiac regions were compared histologically in stage-matched embryos; cell death was assessed by supravital Nile blue sulfate staining. HIF-1alpha and HIF-1beta protein in conceptus lysates from E8.5 to E18 were quantified against topoisomerase I. In parallel, hypoxic induction of vascular endothelial growth factor and of glucose-transporter and glycolytic-enzyme mRNAs was compared in Hif1a-/- and Hif1a+/+ embryonic stem cells and cystic embryoid bodies.
studies.observable: Vascular pattern by whole-mount PECAM staining, histology of the cephalic mesenchyme and presumptive myocardium, mesenchymal cell death, embryonic survival, and hypoxia-induced mRNA levels
studies.finding: Vascularization of Hif1a-/- and Hif1a+/+ embryos was indistinguishable at E8.5-E8.75. By E9.25 the heads of Hif1a-/- embryos contained only a sparse network of small vessels in place of the profusion of vessels in wild-type mesenchyme, together with large anomalous endothelial-lined structures; the branchial-arch vessels were severely hypoplastic or absent and the dorsal aortae were present but abnormal in morphology with localized dilatation. The deficiencies were more pronounced at E9.75, and all Hif1a-/- embryos showed irregularities of the dorsal aortae and intersomitic vessels, with developmental arrest and lethality between E10.0 and E11.0. The source states that vascularization is initiated properly but fails progressively between E8.75 and E9.75. Histology showed marked loss of viable cranial mesenchymal cells, prolapsed neural folds and hyperplasia of the presumptive myocardium within an enlarged pericardial cavity. Wild-type HIF-1alpha protein rose 7- to 8-fold between E8.5 and E9.5-E10, coincident with the onset of the mutant defects, and vascular endothelial growth factor mRNA expression was markedly decreased in hypoxic Hif1a-/- embryonic stem cells and cystic embryoid bodies.
limitations: A constitutive whole-body knockout: the source cannot separate the vascular failure from the mesenchymal cell death that it reports to begin earlier, and states that it is unclear whether the dilated vascular structures are cause or consequence of that cell death.
Vegf expression was measured in embryonic stem cells and embryoid bodies, not in situ in the embryo; the source says in-situ analysis is required to confirm the proposed molecular basis.
Part of the cell-death evidence is cited by the source as its authors' unpublished data.
One mouse line and the mid-gestation window E8.5-E11 only; postnatal vascular remodelling is not assessed.

studies.system: C57BL/6 mice and bone-marrow-derived macrophages, wild type or deficient in Nlrp3, ASC, caspase-1, IL-1R or P2X7R, challenged with necrotic B16 melanoma cells, thioglycollate or renal ischemia-reperfusion
studies.preparation: Pressure-disrupted (necrotic) B16 cells are injected intraperitoneally and peritoneal neutrophils (Ly-6G+ 7/4+) are counted by flow cytometry 16 h later; thioglycollate tests general neutrophil migration. Macrophages are stimulated with the necrotic cells and IL-1beta and IL-1alpha secretion and caspase-1 processing are measured by ELISA and immunoblot. Renal pedicles are clamped for 45 min (lethal model) or 30 min (non-lethal model) and survival, tubular necrosis, plasma urea and creatinine, neutrophil infiltration, KC and IL-1beta are measured; age- and sex-matched C57BL/6 mice serve as wild type and sham-operated mice as surgical controls.
studies.observable: Peritoneal neutrophil influx, macrophage IL-1beta secretion and caspase-1 processing, and survival, renal function and kidney neutrophil infiltration after ischemia-reperfusion
studies.finding: Neutrophil influx 16 h after intraperitoneal necrotic cells is significantly diminished, not abolished, in mice deficient in Nlrp3 inflammasome components, while thioglycollate-induced influx is intact in Nlrp3- and ASC-deficient mice. Nlrp3-deficient macrophages show a marked defect in processing and secreting IL-1beta in response to necrotic cells. In the lethal renal ischemia-reperfusion model 86 percent of Nlrp3-deficient mice survive to 5.5 days against 8 percent of wild type (ASC-deficient 38 percent against none); in the non-lethal model tubular necrosis is similar, while plasma urea and creatinine, kidney neutrophil infiltration, KC and IL-1beta are lower in Nlrp3-deficient mice.
limitations: The percentage reduction of peritoneal influx is not stated in the text read; figure graphs were not inspected.
Necrotic tumour cells disrupted by pressure are an experimental preparation; freeze-thawed cells induce less influx independently of caspase-1.
In vitro readouts are IL-1beta and IL-1alpha only; a PubMed-linked comment letter (PNAS 2010;107(10):E32) was not read.

studies.system: A monoclonal murine IgG1 anti-His-tag antibody binding designed anti-parallel coiled-coil antigens that present either two His-tag epitopes at a controlled spacing of 7 to 20 nm (APH6 to APH18) or a single epitope (APHhalf)
studies.preparation: Design and refold a series of anti-parallel coiled-coils of 6 to 24 heptad repeats, validate their secondary structure and dimensions by synchrotron-radiation circular dichroism, small-angle X-ray scattering and dynamic light scattering, and model the inter-epitope distances. Capture the antibody on a surface-plasmon-resonance chip through an immobilised polyclonal anti-mouse IgG so that both Fab arms stay free, inject a twofold dilution series of each antigen at pH 5.8 (and pH 6.0 and 6.2 for one variant), and fit the association to a 1:1 model for the monovalent antigen and the biphasic dissociation globally to a biexponential decay for the bivalent antigens. Controls: the monovalent single-epitope antigen, a reference flow cell without the anti-His antibody and double buffer referencing.
studies.observable: Helix content, radius of gyration, hydrodynamic radius and modelled inter-epitope distance; monovalent KD; monovalent and bivalent dissociation rate constants and the avidity enhancement beta = koff_mono/koff_bi
studies.finding: The same antibody bound the single-epitope antigen with a KD of 340 +/- 9 nM at pH 5.8 and 40 +/- 0.2 nM at pH 6.2, so monovalent recognition was fully retained; with two epitopes on a rigid spacer, dissociation became biphasic, the slow phase corresponding to the bivalently bound complex. The avidity enhancement reached a maximum of 30-fold at an epitope spacing of 13 nm and fell only about twofold over the whole range, to 12.8 at 20 nm and 16.8 at 6 nm, an energy difference of about 400 cal/mol, less than RT. Raising the monovalent affinity by increasing the pH raised the enhancement from 30-fold to 51- and 84-fold. The authors conclude that the energy landscape of avidity is broad and flat for IgG1, so that bivalent engagement stabilises the complex across a wide range of spacings.
limitations: One antibody with a short linear His-tag epitope on designed coiled-coil antigens, measured on a surface rather than in solution; the authors note that fixed-angle or protein epitopes may behave differently.

Avidity is quantified from the dissociation rate alone, since the ring-closing step is not observed and the fitted second association rate was vanishingly small; the association rates are not well constrained.
Some coiled-coils deviated from the idealised model in scattering or apparent molecular weight, and the longest variant did not adopt the intended structure and was excluded.
Bivalent coupling is varied by changing the antigen, not by removing coupling within the antibody, and the supplementary rate constants were not read.

studies.system: Ribosome-free Escherichia coli S150 extract transcription-translation reactions programmed with a T7 firefly-luciferase plasmid
studies.preparation: Ribosomal components are added to the extract: mature 23S and 5S rRNA with the total 50S proteins (TP50) plus native 30S subunits, or mature 16S rRNA with TP30 plus native 50S subunits; in the integrated (iSAT) reactions the mature rRNA is replaced by a plasmid carrying its gene behind a T7 promoter. studies.finding: Without the 23S rRNA (alone or together with the 5S rRNA), without the 23S rRNA gene, without the 16S rRNA or without the total proteins of the subunit, no active particles and no luciferase are made. 50S subunits assembled in the extract from mature rRNA yield 3.27 +/- 0.46 nmol/l luciferase, and 50S subunits built from unmodified, in vitro-transcribed 23S rRNA yield 0.63 +/- 0.10 nmol/l. studies.system: Mouse embryonic fibroblasts (wild type, ulk1−/− and ulk1−/− reconstituted with Ulk1 or kinase-dead Ulk1-K46A), K562 and 293T cells, and differentiating mouse erythroid cells
studies.preparation: Identify Ulk1 partners by affinity purification and mass spectrometry; disrupt Hsp90–Cdc37 with the Hsp90 inhibitor 17AAG (2.5 μM, 1–21 h) or cdc37 siRNA; measure Ulk1 kinase activity, phosphorylation, protein level and turnover by pulse-chase, with MG132 or bafilomycin A1; measure starvation-induced autophagic flux with a Luc-LC3 turnover reporter; add 17AAG during the final 24 h of erythroid culture and score autophagosomes containing mitochondria by electron microscopy; score Parkin-mediated clearance of CCCP-depolarized mitochondria in MEFs pretreated with 17AAG or cdc37 siRNA.
studies.observable: Ulk1–Hsp90–Cdc37 association, Ulk1 kinase activity, phosphorylation and turnover, Luc-LC3 turnover, reticulocytes with mitochondria-containing autophagosomes, and the fraction of Parkin-expressing cells lacking mitochondria
studies.finding: Ulk1 is a client of the Hsp90–Cdc37 chaperone complex: 17AAG or cdc37 knock-down disrupted the complex, inhibited Ulk1 phosphorylation and kinase activity, and triggered rapid proteasome-mediated turnover of Ulk1, which is otherwise long-lived (half-life close to 24 h), without changing ulk1 mRNA; Ulk2 was not affected. Pretreatment with 17AAG impaired amino-acid-starvation-induced autophagy to an extent similar to ulk1−/− cells; 17AAG during the final 24 h of erythroid culture reduced Ulk1 and the reticulocytes harbouring mitochondria-containing autophagosomes without impairing reticulocyte development; 17AAG or cdc37 knock-down reduced Parkin-mediated clearance of depolarized mitochondria, as did ulk1 loss, and kinase-dead Ulk1 failed to restore clearance.
limitations: 17AAG inhibits all Hsp90 clients, including PI3K–mTOR pathway kinases and Pink1; cdc37 knock-down corroborates the Ulk1 effects, and the source mentions an initial transient increase in autophagy after Hsp90 inhibition under normal growth (unpublished).
The starvation-flux data (Luc-LC3 reporter) are in supplementary figures that were not read; the main-figure readouts are mitochondrial clearance assays.

studies.system: Reactor electron antineutrinos from Japanese power reactors detected by inverse beta decay in the 1 kton KamLAND liquid scintillator
studies.preparation: Select delayed coincidences of a prompt positron signal (2.6-8.5 MeV) and a delayed 2.2 MeV neutron-capture signal (1.8-2.6 MeV), 0.5-1000 microseconds and less than 2 m apart, inside a 5.5 m fiducial radius (543.7 t) for March 2002 to January 2004 (766 ton-year, 515.1 days livetime). Predict the no-oscillation spectrum from reactor operation records and fission yields; estimate accidental, 9Li/8He and 13C(alpha,n)16O backgrounds. Fit a two-flavour oscillation by unbinned maximum likelihood to rate and shape, and compare the L0/E dependence with neutrino-decay and decoherence models by a simulation-calibrated goodness of fit.
studies.observable: Number and prompt-energy spectrum of antineutrino candidates, survival ratio versus L0/E, oscillation parameters and goodness of fit of alternative disappearance models
studies.finding: 258 candidates are observed against 365.2 +/- 23.7 expected without disappearance and 17.8 +/- 7.3 background events, confirming disappearance at 99.998 percent significance; the average survival probability is 0.658 +/- 0.044 +/- 0.047. The scaled no-oscillation spectral shape has a goodness of fit of 0.4 percent. The rate-and-shape two-flavour fit gives Delta m^2 = 7.9 (+0.6/-0.5) x 10^-5 eV^2 and tan^2 theta = 0.46 with goodness of fit 11.1 percent, and the observed-to-expected ratio plotted against L0/E shows the oscillatory pattern; neutrino decay and decoherence give goodness of fit of 0.7 and 1.8 percent.
limitations: The mass splitting and mixing are inferred from the same disappearance data.
Two-flavour analysis; decay and decoherence are examples of non-oscillation disappearance, not every alternative.
Goodness-of-fit values depend on the binning choice, as the source notes; the L0/E display assumes a single 180 km baseline.
The 13C(alpha,n) background (10.3 +/- 7.1 events) is partly floated in the fit.

studies.system: Adult rats trained to press a lever twice with a prescribed 700 ms inter-press interval, with bilateral ibotenic-acid motor cortex lesions before training (11 rats), intact controls (18 rats) and extra-motor parietal lesions (3 rats)
studies.preparation: Lesion forelimb motor cortex bilaterally by injecting 1 percent ibotenic acid at three sites per hemisphere, with the lesion extent verified histologically and reproducibility established in four separately sacrificed animals, let the rats recover and then introduce them to the timed lever-press task for the first time; compare the first 1000 trials and the full learning curves with intact animals, and repeat the same lesions 5 mm posterior to motor cortex as an anatomical control.
studies.observable: Mean and coefficient of variation of the inter-press interval, fraction of trials within 10 percent of the target, reward rate, number of lever presses, reward-tone response, and the fraction of animals reaching criterion
studies.finding: Over the first 1000 trials lesioned and intact rats did not differ in the mean or coefficient of variation of the interval, the fraction of on-target trials, reward rate, number of presses or reward-tone response, so exploratory pressing and reward sensitivity were intact. None of the 11 lesioned rats reached criterion despite 97 plus or minus 23 training days and about 60,000 trials; their asymptotic timing variability was nearly double that of intact animals and only 27 percent below their own starting value, their mean interval stayed at 601 plus or minus 67 ms against the 700 ms target, and only 1 of 11 learned the 1.2 s inter-trial delay. Rats with equally large parietal lesions learned the task and the delay normally.
limitations: Rats and one timed lever-press task without a dexterity requirement.
Excitotoxic lesions destroy local cell bodies and may affect fibres and downstream circuits.
The study shows that the task-specific sequence is not acquired, not that no movement occurs: lesioned rats pressed the lever and collected reward.

studies.system: 36 University of Pennsylvania undergraduates playing 81 one-minute networked consensus games in one session
studies.preparation: Assign subjects at random to the 36 vertices of an experimenter-built network (101 +/- 1 edges) in every game; pay everyone only if the whole network reaches unanimous red or blue within one minute, with individual payments favouring one colour, and show each subject only the current choices of their neighbours. In 27 Minority Power games, give the 6, 9 or 14 highest-degree vertices of preferential-attachment networks incentives for the colour opposed by the majority; in 54 Cohesion games, split preferences 18:18 with varied inter- and intra-group connectivity in Erdos-Renyi or preferential-attachment networks; vary incentive strength and symmetry; run three trials per scenario.
studies.observable: Whether and when global consensus was reached, which colour won, and individual behaviour (colour changes, stubbornness)
studies.finding: Minority Power games reached consensus in 24 of 27 games against 31 of 54 Cohesion games (P < 0.001), and in all 24 the consensus was the colour preferred by the well-connected minority, including minorities of 6 of 36 subjects. In Cohesion games, preferential-attachment connectivity, more inter-group connectivity and asymmetric incentives raised success, and in 18 of 22 successful asymmetric games the strongly motivated group's colour won.
limitations: One session with one pool of 36 students; positions and incentives were assigned by the experimenters for one-minute games, not held as durable social roles.
Minority Power and Cohesion networks differ in preference split and network type, and no control placed the same minority in low-degree positions.

studies.system: Saccharomyces cerevisiae RNA polymerase II elongation complexes assembled on synthetic DNA-RNA scaffolds carrying nonpolar thymidine isosteres
studies.preparation: Five low-polarity thymidine isosteres (H, F, L, B, I), from which all carbonyl and NH groups are removed and which span about 1 Angstrom in size, are placed at one template position of synthetic scaffolds beside thymidine controls, and purified Pol II elongation complexes are assembled on them. Incorporation is followed on denaturing gels from 5'-32P-labelled RNA; single-turnover assays at 25 to 1000 micromolar nucleotide give kpol and the apparent Kd for ATP and UTP by global fitting. Separate scaffolds carry a matched A:X or mismatched U:X pair at the 3' RNA end for the next incorporation, and the same scaffolds are used for TFIIS-stimulated cleavage in the absence of any nucleotide.
studies.observable: Extension products on denaturing PAGE, kpol, apparent Kd and the specificity constant kpol/Kd,app for each nucleotide and template base, and TFIIS-stimulated cleavage rates
studies.finding: On the thymidine template, ATP incorporation has kpol 750 +/- 210 per min, apparent Kd 90 +/- 20 micromolar and a specificity constant of 8.3 per micromolar per min, against 1.9 x 10^-5 for the mismatched UTP, a discrimination of (4.4 +/- 1.9) x 10^5. With the nonpolar isostere F, nearly the same size and shape as thymidine, the specificity for ATP falls 3.5 x 10^4-fold and that for UTP rises about 13-fold, so discrimination collapses to 1.0 +/- 0.3; the same holds for L, B and I, while the smallest analogue H keeps about 100-fold discrimination because UTP incorporation stays very low. Extension from a matched 3' end is almost unchanged by the analogues (A:T 8.7, A:F 5.0, A:I 9.5 per micromolar per min), whereas extension from a U:T mismatch rises 250-fold on F and 1030-fold on I, and TFIIS-stimulated cleavage of a matched 3' end accelerates from 0.6 to 6.4 per min on H and 4.4 per min on F. Full-length transcripts still appear on every analogue template on prolonged incubation.
limitations: One template position is modified in a short synthetic scaffold with one eukaryotic polymerase; hydrogen bonding is not removed from the rest of the template, from the RNA-DNA hybrid or from the enzyme.

Removing the carbonyl and NH groups removes hydrogen-bond donors and acceptors together with the local dipoles, so hydrogen bonding and dipolar interactions are not separated; only the size series resolves sterics.
Synthesis is slowed and made unselective rather than abolished: full-length products are still obtained on the analogue templates.
Rate constants come from global fits of single-turnover data, and the synthesis and characterization of the nonpolar nucleosides are in supplementary figures that were not read.

studies.system: C57BL/6 mice made genetically deficient in interleukin 15 by gene targeting, with IL-15+/+ and IL-15+/- littermate controls
studies.preparation: Splenocytes from naive IL-15-/- and littermate control mice are immunophenotyped for NK1.1 and CD3 and assayed for cytolytic function in an overnight chromium-release assay against NK-sensitive YAC-1 targets, with NK-resistant P815 targets as a specificity control, 24 h after a single injection of PBS or 100 micrograms polyinosinic-polycytidylic acid. studies.system: Collagen-VI-null mice crossed onto the leptin-deficient ob/ob background and collagen-VI-null mice on high-fat diet, with littermate controls
studies.preparation: Mate heterozygous collagen-VI-null mice with heterozygous leptin-deficient mice to obtain littermate-controlled collagen-VI-null ob/ob and ob/ob mice, and keep separate pure-background collagen-VI-null and wild-type cohorts on chow or high-fat diet. studies.finding: Removing one adipose extracellular-matrix component loosens the matrix and lowers the local inflammatory load. Collagen-VI-null ob/ob adipose tissue is less dense and less structured by scanning electron microscopy and contains larger adipocytes, although Sirius red staining and hydroxyproline content show unchanged total collagen. ERK and, less markedly, JNK phosphorylation fall while p38 is unchanged. Total collagen content is unchanged, so the intervention alters matrix organization rather than removing the matrix.
Group sizes are four mice and several inflammatory readouts reach significance only in mesenteric and not in epididymal fat.

studies.system: Male heterozygous Thy1-channelrhodopsin transgenic mice with optical fibres over the thalamic reticular nucleus and electroencephalogram and electromyogram electrodes
studies.preparation: Compare four photostimulation protocols applied to the thalamic reticular nucleus during daytime recordings: spindle-like trains, 1 Hz stimulation, and unilateral or bilateral single pulses, with five recordings per condition per mouse in six mice. Detect spindles in the electroencephalogram, score wake, non-REM and REM states, and measure spindle co-occurrence with each stimulus, spindle density per state, state durations and transitions, and the distribution of single wake-episode durations. Spindle-like protocols at 10 and 12 Hz serve as controls for non-specific effects such as local heating.
studies.observable: Spindle co-occurrence rate and density by state, total time awake and in non-REM and REM sleep, numbers of each state transition, and cumulative distributions of wake-episode duration
studies.finding: Only the spindle-like protocol evoked spindles, coinciding with 51.1 plus or minus 2.6 percent of stimuli against 3.6 percent or less for the other protocols, and only it raised spindle density above spontaneous levels. That protocol increased total non-REM sleep and decreased time awake, increased non-REM to REM and REM to non-REM transitions without changing the three transitions involving wake, removed wake episodes longer than 35 minutes, and left individual non-REM and REM episode durations unchanged; spindle density correlated with non-REM duration (R equal to 0.5987). The 1 Hz protocol changed neither spindle density nor sleep architecture, and the bilateral pulse protocol disturbed sleep and was dropped.
limitations: Six mice and daytime recordings only.
One transgenic line expressing channelrhodopsin broadly rather than in a genetically defined reticular cell type.
Spindles are induced, not removed, so the necessity of spindles for sleep stability is not tested.
The density-duration relations are correlations across animals and conditions.

studies.system: e+e- collisions recorded by L3 at LEP2: W-pair events at 189-209 GeV (1998-2000, 629.2 pb^-1), combined with lower-energy W-pair, single-W (161-209 GeV) and single-photon events

Fit the trilinear couplings g1Z, kappa_gamma, lambda_gamma, g5Z, kappa_Z and lambda_Z by binned maximum likelihood to multi-differential distributions with Monte Carlo reweighting (KandY, EXCALIBUR), imposing kappa_Z = g1Z - tan^2 theta_W (kappa_gamma - 1) and lambda_Z = lambda_gamma for the first three, combine with earlier W-pair, single-W and single-photon results, and evaluate systematic effects of the W-pair cross section, backgrounds, charge confusion, Monte Carlo statistics, radiation, W mass and width, hadronisation, colour reconnection and Bose-Einstein correlations.

studies.system: Purified engineered proteins made of repeats of a folded SH3 domain (SH3m, m = 1-5) and of its proline-rich motif ligand (PRMn, n = 1-5), the tetravalent RNA-binding protein PTB with an RNA oligonucleotide, and the natural nephrin/Nck/N-WASP system with the Arp2/3 complex
studies.preparation: Mix purified multivalent proteins at defined module concentrations in aqueous buffer and score droplet formation by bright-field and fluorescence microscopy after more than 12 hours; map phase boundaries against valency. Test whether assembly drives demixing by adding a high-affinity monovalent ligand PRM(H)1, and follow species size by dynamic light scattering and small-angle X-ray scattering during PRM titrations into SH35, with droplets removed by centrifugation. Image droplets by electron cryo-microscopy and measure exchange by photobleaching. In cells, co-express mCherry-SH35 with eGFP-PRM5 or eGFP-PRM3. For function, measure pyrene-actin assembly with fixed Arp2/3 complex, Nck, triply phosphorylated nephrin peptide and N-WASP plus increasing amounts of an N-WASP truncation that polymerises but cannot bind Arp2/3. Controls: single components alone, low-valency partners, mixtures below the droplet concentration and an N-WASP lacking the proline-rich region.
studies.observable: Presence and size of liquid droplets and the phase boundary in module concentration; partition coefficients; hydrodynamic and gyration radii; fluorescence recovery; half-time of Arp2/3-mediated actin assembly
studies.finding: Mixing the folded multivalent proteins produced sharp liquid-liquid demixing: SH34 with PRM4 at 300 microM modules gave spherical droplets of about 1 to more than 50 micrometres that coalesced over time and concentrated both proteins about 100-fold (116-fold for SH35+PRM5). The phase boundary depended strongly on valency, and phase separation was blocked by the monovalent ligand PRM(H)1 and absent with PRM1, which cannot polymerise, while PRM2 and PRM4 increased the apparent radii before droplet formation. Electron-dense objects of 50-500 nm appeared only in the mixtures, not with either protein alone or below the droplet concentration, and in cells puncta formed only on co-expression of the two high-valency proteins. In the nephrin/Nck/N-WASP system droplet formation shifted the phase boundary with the degree of nephrin phosphorylation, and actin assembly by the Arp2/3 complex rose sharply as the total N-WASP concentration crossed the droplet boundary. The authors conclude that interactions between multivalent macromolecules produce sharp liquid-liquid phase separation coupled to a sol-gel transition.
limitations: The SH3 and PRM constructs are engineered repeat proteins, and the nephrin system is reconstituted in vitro, so the concentrations and geometry need not match a cell.

The folded SH3 domain is not unfolded in a control, so the experiment shows condensates forming from multivalent folded domains rather than that folding is required for phase separation; condensates of disordered proteins are known from other work.

The sol-gel transition inside the droplets is inferred from scattering, photobleaching and cryo-EM edges, not observed directly, and the supplementary simulations and cyclization analysis were not read.
The actin assembly readout is a half-time in a bulk pyrene assay, and the sharp rise is correlated with the separately determined phase boundary rather than measured in the same reaction.

studies.system: Human HEK293, HCT116, ARPE and RCC4 cells with the tricarboxylic-acid cycle perturbed by SDHD knockdown or by cell-permeating esters of succinate or fumarate, reported by a GFP-ODD degradation sensor and by endogenous HIF1alpha
studies.preparation: Synthesise benzyl, octyl and trifluoromethylbenzyl monoesters of alpha-ketoglutarate; measure free intracellular alpha-ketoglutarate in extracts with a glutamate-dehydrogenase assay after 2 hours of treatment. Assay prolyl hydroxylase activity in vitro on in-vitro-translated HA-tagged ODD with HeLa extracts, iron and ascorbate at fixed succinate and varied alpha-ketoglutarate, reading hydroxylation as a gel shift. In cells, express GFP-ODD with HA-pVHL, raise succinate or fumarate with dimethyl-succinate or monoethyl-fumarate or suppress SDHD by short-hairpin RNA, then add the alpha-ketoglutarate esters and follow GFP-ODD and HIF1alpha by immunoblot, the ODD-pVHL interaction by co-immunoprecipitation, and the glycolytic rate as conversion of [5-3H]glucose to tritiated water. Controls: scrambled hairpin, underivatised and benzyl alpha-ketoglutarate, CoCl2 as a hydroxylase inhibitor acting by another mechanism, the proteasome inhibitor MG132 and pVHL-negative RCC4 cells.
studies.observable: Free intracellular alpha-ketoglutarate; in vitro ODD hydroxylation; GFP-ODD and HIF1alpha protein levels; ODD-pVHL co-immunoprecipitation; glycolytic rate
studies.finding: Blocking the cycle changed the regime of the oxygen-sensing signalling pathway through its metabolites, and restoring the substrate reversed it. Succinate at 1 mM inhibited prolyl hydroxylase in vitro, and adding 0.1 to 1 mM alpha-ketoglutarate restored hydroxylation in a concentration-dependent way, showing competitive inhibition. In cells, the octyl and trifluoromethylbenzyl esters raised free alpha-ketoglutarate about fourfold, and about twofold more in SDH-deficient than in control cells, whereas underivatised and benzyl alpha-ketoglutarate did not. Raising succinate or fumarate, or knocking down SDHD, stabilised GFP-ODD and HIF1alpha under normoxia and reduced the hydroxylation-dependent ODD-pVHL interaction; the permeating esters reversed all three within 12 hours, restored the pVHL interaction, and abolished the increase in glycolytic rate, while having no effect on CoCl2-induced HIF1alpha and no effect in pVHL-negative cells.
limitations: Cultured human cell lines with the cycle perturbed either by RNA interference against one SDH subunit or by externally supplied esters of cycle intermediates, not by a defined change of cycle flux.

The alpha-ketoglutarate esters raise the substrate of a whole family of alpha-ketoglutarate-dependent dioxygenases, and the authors note that prolyl hydroxylases are not the only ones, so effects beyond this pathway are not excluded.
Readouts are immunoblots and a reporter, with one experiment under 10 percent rather than ambient oxygen to obtain maximal induction; HIF2alpha responded much less than HIF1alpha.
Intracellular concentrations of the esters and of succinate were not measured directly, and the supplementary data were not read.

studies.system: Caenorhabditis elegans hermaphrodites: social npr-1(ad609) loss-of-function mutants and solitary wild-type (N2) animals, assayed as populations of 150 adults on bacterial lawns
studies.preparation: Kill the RMG inter/motor neuron, the hub of a gap-junction network that links seven classes of neurons in the C. elegans wiring diagram, among them sensory neurons that promote aggregation, with a laser microbeam at the L1 stage in an ncs-1::GFP strain, confirm the loss of RMG fluorescence, and score the adults about 72 hours later against mock-ablated animals for aggregation (touching two or more animals two hours after plating), bordering and speed on food; in further experiments express npr-1 only in RMG by an intersectional Cre/Lox strategy, silence RMG or ASK/ASJ synapses with tetanus toxin, activate RMG-coupled neurons with a gain-of-function protein kinase C in solitary animals, and test osmotic avoidance of RMG-ablated animals.
studies.observable: Fractions of animals aggregating and bordering, locomotion speed on food, ascaroside chemotaxis and osmotic avoidance
studies.finding: RMG-ablated npr-1 animals did not aggregate (0% against 40% of mock-ablated animals), rarely bordered (17% against 97.1%; chi-square 43.05, P < 0.001) and lost rapid movement on food, whereas killing RMG in solitary wild-type animals had no effect and RMG-ablated animals still avoided high osmolarity. limitations: One nematode species and one social genotype; in solitary wild-type animals RMG ablation has no aggregation to remove.
A single hub neuron of an otherwise wired nervous system was removed; the formation of the network as a whole was not prevented, and the gap junctions are defined anatomically.

studies.system: ON, OFF transient and OFF sustained ganglion cells in isolated retinas of adult (5-8 week) male C57BL/6 mice
studies.preparation: Whole-cell current- and voltage-clamp recordings at 30-34 degrees C in Ames' medium with a synaptic blocker mixture (50 micromolar L-APB, 20 CNQX, 50 APV, 1 strychnine and 50 picrotoxin), which made the retina insensitive to light; 0.1 micromolar TTX was added in further experiments. Somatic current steps depolarized ON cells to match OFF-cell firing or hyperpolarized OFF cells; slow voltage ramps from -90 to -10 mV before and after TTX isolated a persistent Na+ current.
studies.observable: Membrane potential, maintained and spontaneous spike rate and regularity, subthreshold oscillations and TTX-sensitive persistent Na+ current
studies.finding: In synaptic blockers ON cells hyperpolarize (to -65.5 mV) and stop spiking, whereas OFF transient and OFF sustained cells depolarize (to about -55 mV) and fire more regularly (20.3 and 43.3 Hz), showing intrinsic spontaneous activity. Hyperpolarizing current modulates and silences this firing. All three types have a TTX-sensitive persistent Na+ current activating near -65 mV, which is active at rest in OFF but not ON cells. TTX at 0.1 micromolar abolishes fast spikes first, then subthreshold oscillations, and hyperpolarizes the cells by about 3-5 mV.
limitations: TTX blocks voltage-gated Na+ channels; the Na+ concentration gradient itself is not removed.
The spikes studied are maintained and spontaneous, recorded with the retina made insensitive to light.
Whole-cell recordings from three ganglion-cell types of one mouse strain.

studies.system: 96 students of the University of Groningen in 12 analysed computer-laboratory sessions of eight participants (18 sessions run, six excluded)
studies.preparation: Each participant received three of twelve pre-rated arguments about where to build a leisure centre between two hypothetical towns, two favouring one town (types A and B assigned at random); participants were told that argument sets differed but not about the two types, so that no social categorization was possible. Each then interacted once by computer with every other participant, first three times with same-type partners (homophilous matching), then four times with other-type partners, in three randomly assigned conditions: exchange of opinions only, of arguments only, or of both. Opinions were rated on a scale from -50 to +50 after each interaction.
studies.observable: Degree of bi-polarization (opinion distance between the two types) across interaction periods, estimated by regressions on two period effects in each condition
studies.finding: Initial opinions differed between the types in all conditions. During homophilous matching, bi-polarization increased by 1.71 (t=2.98) and 1.91 (t=2.15) per interaction when arguments were exchanged, significantly more than with opinions only, where it did not change (-0.21, t=-0.42). During heterophilous matching it decreased in all conditions (by 2.75, 2.74 and 1.01), with no sign of negative influence.
limitations: Small laboratory sample (four sessions of eight per condition) on an artificial issue; homophily was imposed by the matching schedule.
The two opinion types were created by argument assignment, and the increase in polarization reversed once partners were mixed.
The formal model and simulations of the paper are not counted as evidence; the supplementary tables were not read.

studies.system: Mice with the interleukin-6 receptor alpha gene inactivated in myeloid cells and floxed littermate controls, and their bone-marrow-derived macrophages, challenged with bacterial lipopolysaccharide
studies.preparation: Bone-marrow-derived macrophages of both genotypes are stimulated with lipopolysaccharide alone or together with IL-6 and assayed for M1 marker and inflammatory cytokine transcripts. Mice of both genotypes then receive a single sublethal intraperitoneal dose of lipopolysaccharide at 1 mg per kg body weight, and body weight, food intake and respiratory exchange ratio are recorded, circulating TNF, IL-1beta, IL-12 and IL-4 are measured after injection, and liver and white adipose tissue are profiled for inflammatory and M2 marker transcripts 48 hours later.
studies.observable: Lipopolysaccharide-induced inflammatory transcripts in macrophages, and in vivo body weight, food intake, respiratory exchange ratio, circulating cytokines and tissue transcripts after the challenge
studies.finding: Lipopolysaccharide alone induces Nos2, Tnf, Il1b and Il12a equally in macrophages of both genotypes, but co-stimulation with IL-6 blunts that induction by about half in control and not at all in receptor-deficient macrophages. In vivo the challenge reduces body weight, food intake and respiratory exchange ratio in both genotypes, and all three responses are significantly stronger in the myeloid receptor knockouts, which also show significantly higher circulating TNF, IL-1beta and IL-12 after injection, higher circulating IL-4, and significantly increased inflammatory gene expression in liver and adipose tissue at 48 hours with reduced Il4ra and Retnla in adipose tissue.
limitations: The defence response occurs in both genotypes and is in fact larger without the parent, so the preparation shows a change of the operating regime and not a requirement for the response to arise.
A single sublethal endotoxin dose in young male mice; no pathogen, no barrier and no surveillance or clearance endpoint is measured.
Myeloid deletion by LysM-Cre is lineage-wide and constitutive, and the readouts are circulating cytokines, whole-tissue transcripts and whole-body physiology rather than resolved immune architecture.
The polarization mechanism proposed by the source rests on the IL-4-receptor experiments, which were not read.
