studies.system: Mice with the interleukin-6 receptor alpha gene inactivated in myeloid cells (Il6ra-flox with LysM-Cre) and Cre-negative floxed littermate controls, on normal chow or high-fat diet
studies.preparation: Il6ra is conditionally deleted in the myeloid lineage and the deletion verified by absent IL-6-induced STAT3 phosphorylation in bone-marrow-derived macrophages. Mice of both genotypes are fed chow or high-fat diet from 4 to 19 weeks of age with body weight, body composition, fat-pad weight, serum leptin, oxygen consumption and caloric intake monitored. Glucose homeostasis is assayed by glucose- and insulin-tolerance tests, fasting insulin and HOMA-IR, and by euglycemic-hyperinsulinemic clamps in awake mice with tissue-specific glucose uptake, suppression of lipolysis and suppression of hepatic glucose production. Adipose, brown adipose and liver tissue are profiled for inflammatory and M1 and M2 polarization markers, crown-like structures are counted, and JNK activation is measured by immunoprecipitation and in vitro kinase assay; conventional Il6-null and Cre-only mice are used as further controls.
studies.observable: Body weight and composition, glucose and insulin tolerance, clamp glucose infusion rate, tissue glucose uptake, suppression of hepatic glucose production and of lipolysis, tissue M1 and M2 marker expression and crown-like structure number
studies.finding: Myeloid deletion of the IL-6 receptor leaves obesity development unchanged: body weight, body composition, fat-pad weight, serum leptin, oxygen consumption and caloric intake do not differ between genotypes on either diet. On high-fat diet the knockouts are nevertheless significantly more glucose intolerant and more insulin resistant than controls, with higher fasting insulin and HOMA-IR, a 50 percent lower clamp glucose infusion rate, insulin-stimulated glucose uptake reduced by 25 percent in white and 40 percent in brown adipose tissue with no difference in skeletal muscle, impaired insulin suppression of lipolysis and of hormone-sensitive-lipase expression, and insulin-mediated suppression of hepatic glucose production reduced by 50 percent with raised hepatic glucose-6-phosphatase. The same tissues show increased Tnf, Il1b, Il6, Il12a and Nos2, an increased M1 marker and reduced Il4ra, Mrc1 and Retnla, a two-fold increase in crown-like structures and a six- to ten-fold increase in JNK activation, while chow-fed knockouts show no inflammatory or polarization differences; Cre-only controls are unchanged.
limitations: The organism keeps regulating glucose in both genotypes: what the deletion changes is the set-point and insulin sensitivity under a dietary load, not the existence of organ-scale regulation.
LysM-Cre deletes in the myeloid lineage broadly rather than in one tissue macrophage population, and the receptor is removed from conception.
Polarization is read as surface markers and transcript panels in whole tissues; the inflammatory and metabolic changes are not separated from one another.
The phenotype appears only on high-fat diet, so the dependency is conditional on the dietary challenge.
The IL-4-receptor and STAT3 mechanism experiments and all supplementary figures were not read.

studies.system: Adult mice (tamoxifen at postnatal day 60 or 90) carrying Pdgfra-CreERT2 and Rosa-YFP with one or two floxed Myrf alleles, plus Sox10-CreERT2 Myrf deletions and wild-type runners, on a mixed C57B6/CBA/129 background
studies.preparation: Inactivate myelin regulatory factor in oligodendrocyte precursors with tamoxifen, which simultaneously labels the recombined precursors with yellow fluorescent protein, and compare with littermates in which one allele is inactivated. Count new and pre-existing oligodendrocytes and precursors by YFP, CC1 and Pdgfra immunolabelling and by a week of 5-ethynyl-deoxyuridine in drinking water; assess myelin by Eriochrome cyanine histochemistry and electron microscopy, with Sox10-driven deletion as a demyelinating comparison. Test motor coordination on an accelerating rotarod and motor learning on a running wheel with irregularly spaced rungs, including a cohort introduced to the wheel before tamoxifen and retested after it, plus high-speed filming of gait.
studies.observable: Numbers of newly formed and pre-existing oligodendrocytes and precursors, myelin histology and g-ratio, rotarod latency, and wheel running distance, average and maximum speed
studies.finding: Deleting Myrf in precursors cut new oligodendrocyte production to about a tenth of control, from 301 to 33 cells per square millimetre in anterior corpus callosum and from 5.7 to 0.2 percent of oligodendrocytes labelled by 5-ethynyl-deoxyuridine, without changing precursor numbers, pre-existing oligodendrocytes, myelin histology, g-ratio or rotarod performance, whereas Sox10-driven deletion produced frank demyelination and rotarod impairment. On the complex wheel the precursor-deletion mice reached lower average and maximum speeds across five pooled experiments (P equal to 0.0063 for accumulated distance) with equal time spent turning the wheel, while mice that had learned the wheel before tamoxifen ran at speed immediately after it.

studies.system: Synthetic DNA primer-template duplexes and the Klenow fragment (exo- mutant) of Escherichia coli DNA polymerase I, with difluorotoluene deoxynucleoside (F) as a nonpolar isostere of thymidine

For replication, use 28-mer templates with a variable base and 23-mer (standing start) or 18-mer (running start) 32P-labelled primers with Klenow fragment (exo-) pretreated with inorganic pyrophosphatase; survey single-nucleotide insertions at 2 microM dNTP and run steady-state kinetics by varying dNTP concentration (5 microM duplex, 13-200 nM enzyme, 50 mM Tris pH 7.5, 10 mM MgCl2, 1 mM DTT, 0.1 mg/ml BSA, 37 C), resolving products on denaturing polyacrylamide gels. studies.system: Escherichia coli BW25113 and isogenic single-gene deletions of twelve global regulators (ArcA, ArcB, Cra, CreB, CreC, Crp, Cya, Fnr, Hns, Mlc, OmpR, UspA) in glucose-limited chemostats at a dilution rate of 0.1 per hour

Controls: the parent strain in triplicate, duplicate 13C experiments per mutant (68 in total), and complementation of the Crp mutant with plasmid-borne crp.

studies.finding: In the parent and in nearly all mutants the glyoxylate shunt supplied 45 to 65 percent of oxaloacetate, so the PEP-glyoxylate cycle carried substantial flux. limitations: One organism under one condition, severe glucose limitation at a low dilution rate; the authors note that the controlling mechanism is highly condition-dependent and that ArcA dominates instead in batch culture.

Fluxes are inferred from 13C labelling of proteinogenic amino acids through a stoichiometric model with flux-ratio constraints, not measured directly, and some ratios enter only as boundary constraints.
Deleting a global regulator changes more than one enzyme and also changes the biomass yield, so the effect on cycle flux is not attributable to a single transcriptional target.
The in vitro activities are duplicate measurements in crude extracts and are qualitative corroboration of the flux data.

studies.system: Ultracold 40K and 87Rb atom pairs associated into 40K87Rb molecules in an optical dipole trap
studies.preparation: Associate a near-degenerate 40K-87Rb atom mixture into extremely weakly bound Feshbach molecules (binding h x 230 kHz at 545.9 G) by an adiabatic magnetic-field sweep across the 546.7 G Fano-Feshbach resonance. Transfer them by one-step STIRAP into the rovibrational ground state of the triplet a3Sigma+ potential (binding h x 7.18 THz, about 240 cm^-1) or of the singlet X1Sigma+ potential (binding h x 125.319703 THz, about 0.5 eV). The deeply bound molecules are dark to the imaging light and are counted only after reverse STIRAP to Feshbach molecules and absorption imaging. Measure dc Stark shifts of two-photon dark resonances at 0-2 kV/cm between transparent plates outside the glass cell, treating the initial Feshbach state as having a negligible moment.
studies.observable: Feshbach-molecule number after one-way and round-trip STIRAP, two-photon binding energies of the triplet and singlet v=0 levels, and dc Stark shifts giving permanent electric dipole moments
studies.finding: Pairs of 40K and 87Rb atoms are converted into molecules: a few 10^4 Feshbach molecules formed from the atomic mixture are transferred with one-way efficiencies of 56 percent (triplet) and 83 percent (singlet) into rovibrational ground-state molecules bound by h x 7.18 THz and h x 125.3 THz below the atom-pair threshold. Stark spectroscopy gives permanent electric dipole moments of 0.052(2) D for the triplet v=0 state and 0.566(17) D for the singlet v=0 state, about ten times larger. The source compares these with a calculated 5 x 10^-11 D for the initial Feshbach molecules and states that only tightly bound molecules have an appreciable electric dipole moment.
limitations: One heteronuclear alkali dimer formed through a Feshbach resonance and coherent STIRAP transfer at nanokelvin temperatures, not a general chemical-bond formation pathway.
The negligible Feshbach-molecule moment is a source calculation and an assumption of the Stark analysis, not a measured zero.
Dipole magnitudes rest on an electric field known to about 3 percent; a later author-thesis correction of the singlet value, recorded in the graph's ni2008-krb-stark study, was not read here.
Only permanent dipoles of two bound states are measured; induced polarizability, dipole-dipole interactions and dielectric behaviour are not.

One chaperone in one organism, with point mutations that could in principle affect more than the catalytic step; loss of p23 binding is excluded as the cause of lethality only by the separate finding that p23 is not essential.
The ATPase turnover is slow and was measured only on purified recombinant protein, where contaminating activity had been a known difficulty; the authors control for it with geldanamycin inhibition.
The crystal structure is of the human N-terminal domain while the genetics is in yeast, and the refinement was not replayed.

studies.system: Hadronic Z0 decays recorded by OPAL at LEP, 1991-1995, separated into event hemispheres of the five primary quark flavours
studies.preparation: From about 4.1 million hadronic Z0 decays retain 2 820 220 well-contained events with at least eight tracks. In each thrust hemisphere identify the highest-momentum particle with xp = 2p/sqrt(s) > 0.2 (charged pion, kaon or proton by dE/dx, K0S and Lambda by decay vertex, electrons, muons, D*+- and displaced-vertex bottom tags). Solve the single- and double-tagged hemisphere counts for the probabilities eta_q^i that a primary quark q yields a hemisphere led by particle i, with the Z0 hadronic branching fractions fixed to measured or standard-model values, hadronisation symmetries such as eta(pi, d) = eta(pi, u) imposed and detector effects corrected with JETSET.
studies.observable: Probabilities eta_q^i for xp > 0.2 that a jet of primary flavour d, u, s, c or b has a leading pi+-, K+-, proton, K0S or Lambda
studies.finding: For xp > 0.2: leading charged pions in 0.3866 +/- 0.0027 +/- 0.0257 of d jets and 0.1701 +/- 0.0062 +/- 0.0139 of s jets; leading charged kaons in 0.2390 +/- 0.0056 +/- 0.0187 of s jets against 0.0617 +/- 0.0102 +/- 0.0080 of d and 0.1227 +/- 0.0136 +/- 0.0244 of u jets; leading K0S in 0.1210 +/- 0.0028 +/- 0.0096 of s jets against 0.0228 +/- 0.0107 +/- 0.0100 of u jets; leading Lambda in 0.0493 +/- 0.0046 +/- 0.0041 of s jets against 0.0231 +/- 0.0025 +/- 0.0020 of d jets; leading protons in 0.0569 +/- 0.0086 +/- 0.0109 of u jets against 0.0362 +/- 0.0063 +/- 0.0075 of d jets. The source concludes that the flavour of the primary quark is reflected in the leading particle, that leading protons are more frequent in up than in down quark jets, and that baryons are suppressed relative to mesons in jets of the same flavour; it describes Lambda baryons forming when the primary quark picks up a diquark.
limitations: Probabilities rest on fixed Z0 branching fractions, imposed hadronisation symmetries and JETSET-based corrections.
Only the leading particle above xp = 0.2 is flavour-resolved.
The proton up/down contrast carries a statistical correlation of -0.825 between the two probabilities.

studies.system: Hadronic Z0 decays recorded by OPAL at LEP within 3 GeV of the Z peak, 1991-1995
studies.preparation: Select about 3.6 million well-contained hadronic events, about 250 000 of them four-jet events in the Durham scheme at ycut = 0.008 with jet energies above 3 GeV. Correct four-jet angular correlations (Bengtsson-Zerwas, Nachtmann-Reiter, Koerner-Schierholtz-Willrodt and the angle between the two softest jets), the four-jet rate and the differential two-jet rate bin by bin for detector and hadronization effects with JETSET samples generated with standard QCD colour factors. Fit NLO (and resummed) perturbative predictions simultaneously for alpha_s, CA/CF and TR/CF, assuming a non-abelian gauge symmetry, and vary detector, hadronization, scale, matching, fit range, five-parton background and ycut.
studies.observable: Colour factors CA and CF of the gauge group of the strong interaction, the ratio TR/CF and alpha_s(MZ)
studies.finding: CA/CF = 2.25 +/- 0.08 +/- 0.14 and TR/CF = 0.37 +/- 0.04 +/- 0.06, converted with TR = 1/2 to CA = 3.02 +/- 0.25 +/- 0.49, CF = 1.34 +/- 0.13 +/- 0.22 and alpha_s(MZ) = 0.120 +/- 0.011 +/- 0.020, in agreement with the SU(3) values CA = 3 and CF = 4/3 and with earlier LEP measurements; the SU(3) point lies inside the 68 percent contour and a light-gluino scenario outside the 95 percent contour. The source describes CA and CF as eigenvalues of the quadratic Casimir operators of the underlying gauge group and notes that alpha_s depends on the colour factors through its running.
limitations: The fit assumes a non-abelian gauge theory and corrects the data with Monte Carlo generated with standard QCD colour factors.
Theoretical (scale and matching) uncertainties dominate; the Bayesian combination of systematic variations gives smaller errors than the largest deviations.
TR = 1/2 and five light flavours are assumed in converting the ratios.

studies.system: Perforin-deficient (Prf1-null) and wild-type C57BL/6 mice aged to 2, 12 and 24 months, and 18-month-old Prf1-null mice given the senolytic ABT-737
studies.preparation: Breed Prf1-null mice, which lack perforin-dependent cytotoxic killing by natural killer and T cells, alongside wild-type C57BL/6 controls under specific-pathogen-free conditions, with equal numbers of both sexes and mice that became obese in the first year excluded. Sacrifice cohorts at 2, 12 and 24 months and compare liver senescence and SASP transcripts, immune infiltration of liver, pancreas and lung by flow cytometry, liver immune foci by immunofluorescence, serum cytokine arrays on pooled samples, white blood counts, spleen weight, organ histology, serum damage markers, voluntary exercise, grip strength and natural lifespan. Separately treat 18-month-old Prf1-null mice for two months with two consecutive daily intraperitoneal injections of ABT-737 at 25 mg per kg at the start of each month, or vehicle, and analyse them at 20 months for senescent-cell burden, serum cytokines, white blood counts, spleen weight, tissue immune infiltration, fibrosis and tissue transcriptomes.
studies.observable: Liver SASP and p16 transcripts, tissue and circulating immune-cell numbers, serum cytokine array intensities, spleen weight, fibrotic area, SASP gene scores and survival
studies.finding: Loss of perforin-dependent cytotoxicity intensifies rather than prevents the age-related inflammatory state, and removing senescent cells reverses much of it. Tissue-infiltrating immune cells increase with age in both genotypes and are further escalated in old Prf1-null mice, whose livers also show immune foci dominated by CD3-positive and NK1.1-positive cells and higher Il-6, RANTES and JE transcripts than old wild-type livers. In the senolytic experiment, ABT-737 reduces senescent-cell burden and the top five serum cytokines reduced include some of the most elevated proteins of old Prf1-null serum, while white blood counts, spleen weight, tissue immune infiltration and fibrotic area all fall and tissue transcriptomes show general repression of immune response and cytokine production with SASP gene scores driven towards those of young mice.
limitations: Perforin deficiency removes cytotoxic killing by natural killer and T cells together, so the natural-killer contribution is not isolated.
The age-related inflammatory state of the wild-type comparator is established within this ageing series rather than independently.
Serum cytokine arrays use three pooled samples per age and genotype and report relative intensities, not absolute concentrations.

ABT-737 is a BCL-2-family inhibitor given systemically; the reduction of inflammation follows a reduction of senescent-cell markers but off-target effects are not excluded, and the experiment starts at 18 months, so first formation of the inflammatory state is not tested.
The progeroid LMNA cohorts, the RNA-seq processing and all supplementary figures were not read.

studies.system: Male wild-type and tenascin-C-null (Tnc-null) 129sv mice given dextran sodium sulphate in drinking water
studies.preparation: Give 3 per cent dextran sodium sulphate in drinking water for five days, then plain water, and cull at day 8 (acute) or day 22 (after 17 days of recovery), against age- and sex-matched water-only controls of both genotypes; monitor water intake per cage and score body weight and a daily disease activity index. At cull, measure colon length, divide the colon into proximal, middle and distal segments, and grade colitis histopathology blind on haematoxylin-and-eosin sections for inflammation severity, inflammatory extent, tissue regeneration and crypt damage, each multiplied by a percentage-involvement grade. Stain cryosections for tenascin-C, the epithelial marker EpCAM, basement-membrane collagen IV and markers for macrophages, T cells, blood vessels and lymphatic vessels.
studies.observable: Body weight loss, disease activity index, colon length, blind colitis histopathology scores by colon region and by scoring parameter, and immunostaining for tenascin-C, epithelial EpCAM and basement-membrane collagen IV
studies.finding: Tnc-null colon showed no tenascin-C staining along its length, confirming ablation of the protein, and no baseline histological abnormality. Tenascin-C is described here as acting as a damage-associated molecular pattern through Toll-like receptor 4 and integrins, so the deletion removes an inflammatory ligand as well as a structural matrix component.

studies.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
studies.system: 24,191 students aged 11-15 in 56 New Jersey public middle schools, school year 2012-2013
studies.preparation: Map each school's social network before randomization (every student names up to ten schoolmates they chose to spend time with); randomly assign 28 schools to an anticonflict intervention and, within them, randomly invite half of a blocked set of seed-eligible students (on average 26 seeds per school) to biweekly meetings where they publicly opposed common forms of conflict through posters with their photographs, hashtag slogans and orange wristbands given for friendly behaviour. The share of social referents (students in the top 10% of nominations received) among the seeds varies by randomization. Estimate peer-to-peer effects by inverse-probability weighting across exposure to a referent seed, exposure to nonreferent seeds only, no exposure in treatment schools, and control schools, with intention-to-treat counting of noncompliers.
studies.observable: End-of-year survey reports of descriptive and prescriptive conflict norms, of friends discussing conflict reduction and of wristband wearing, and school disciplinary records of peer conflict
studies.finding: Students in treatment schools exposed to a social-referent seed reported more schoolmates disapproving of conflict than treatment-school students not exposed to a referent seed (P < 0.01 in two randomization-based Wald tests), with nonreferent exposure intermediate, and were more likely to wear the anticonflict wristband than students in all other exposure conditions (P < 0.00001); school-average perceived norms did not differ between treatment and control schools. limitations: One school year in one US state; referent status is a measured network position that the authors do not separate from the students' personal traits.
The experiment varies which position holders carry an anticonflict campaign, not the schools' role structure itself.
The school-level effect on disciplinary reports is not significant at the 0.05 level after the 2018 correction; the supporting appendix was not read.

studies.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
studies.system: Dilute HOD (5 percent) in H2O and aqueous NaBr solutions with 32, 16 and 8 water molecules per NaBr (about 1.5, 3 and 6 M), probed through the OD stretch at room temperature
studies.preparation: Mix 0.025, 0.05 or 0.1 mol NaBr with 0.8 mol of 5 percent HOD in H2O and hold the solutions between CaF2 windows at a 6 micrometre path length; pure HOD in H2O is the control. Record H2O-background-subtracted FT IR spectra of the OD stretch; record heterodyne-detected 2D IR vibrational echo spectra with three pulses of about 60 fs at a series of waiting times Tw and extract the frequency-frequency correlation function by the center-line-slope method together with the linear spectrum; measure polarization-selective IR pump-probe signals (parallel and perpendicular) for orientational and vibrational population relaxation, with the heating signal subtracted.
studies.observable: OD stretch peak position and width; amplitudes and time constants of the frequency-frequency correlation function (spectral diffusion); anisotropy decay and its wobbling and long-time reorientation constants; vibrational population relaxation
studies.finding: As the NaBr concentration rises the OD band moves from 2509 cm-1 in pure water to 2519, 2529 and 2539 cm-1 (n = 32, 16, 8). The slowest correlation-function component, which the source associates with the global rearrangement of the hydrogen-bond structure, lengthens from 1.7 +/- 0.5 ps in pure water to 2.6, 3.5 and 4.8 +/- 0.6 ps, and the long-time orientational relaxation from 2.6 ps to 3.9, 5.1 and 6.7 ps; population relaxation becomes biexponential with a slow component of 3.21 to 5.74 ps against 1.81 ps in water. The authors conclude that the hydroxyl groups are increasingly hydrogen bonded to ions (HOD-Br-, DOH-Br-, HDO-Na+) rather than to other water molecules, that the global rearrangement proceeds by breaking and reforming water-ion hydrogen bonds in a manner analogous to pure water, and that at about 6 M it is about three times slower than in pure water.
limitations: One salt, NaBr, at 1.5 to 6 M; dilute solutions, other ions and the separate roles of Na+ and Br- are not resolved.
Assigning the slowest correlation component to hydrogen-bond rearrangement draws on simulations of pure water, and the extracted correlation functions are approximate because of non-Condon effects.
At the highest concentrations the water-water network is largely replaced by water-ion hydrogen bonds, so the ions change the partners as well as the dynamics of hydrogen bonding.
Equations rendered as images and the figure images were not inspected; the values come from the tables, legends and text.

Repost cascades grew less deep (-39.9% in depth growth) and less viral (-48.5% in structural-virality growth), and at equal growth in cascade size noted posts spread with smaller depth and virality but not smaller breadth. Notes attached within 12 hours of posting cut repost growth by 49.6%, those attached after 47 hours by 6.2%; the placebo test gave null effects.

studies.preparation: C57BL/6 x 129/Sv perforin-deficient mice backcrossed five generations to C57BL/6 were crossed to B6.p53+/- mice, and 48 pfp+/-p53+/- founder pairs produced progeny of all nine genotypes. Mice were genotyped at birth by Southern blot and PCR, raised anonymously in one clean room under standard conditions, monitored and weighed twice weekly for up to two years, killed at any abnormality and examined by full autopsy and histology, with lymphoma surface phenotype by flow cytometry. Nine lymphomas from pfp-/- mice were transplanted intraperitoneally at graded doses into C57BL/6 or B6.pfp-/- mice, with antibody depletion of NK1.1+, Thy-1+ or CD8+ cells on days -2 and 0 and weekly thereafter, and observed for more than 100 days.

studies.finding: No pfp-/-p53+/+ mouse developed cancer before 12 months, after which 10 of 20 died of aggressive disseminated lymphoma of spleen, liver and lymph nodes between 436 and 635 days, against 1 of 16 pfp+/+p53+/+ mice (P = 0.0091), and no lymphoma arose in 20 pfp+/-p53+/+ mice. In p53+/- mice, perforin loss raised both tumour incidence (23 of 27, P = 0.0058) and the proportion of disseminated lymphomas (16 of 23, P = 0.0019) and shortened the mean age at death, while the incidence and onset of sarcomas and other tumours were not significantly different. The lymphomas were of B-cell, T-cell, NKT-cell and uncertain lineage and all expressed MHC class I. On transplantation, as few as 10^3 lymphoma cells killed all B6.pfp-/- mice and all C57BL/6 mice depleted of Thy-1+ or CD8+ cells, whereas up to 10^6 cells were cleared by untreated or anti-NK1.1-treated C57BL/6 mice, a 10^4- to 10^5-fold difference in the tumorigenic dose; one escaping tumour in a wild-type host had lost H-2Kb expression.

A constitutive germline knockout on a mixed C57BL/6 x 129/Sv background backcrossed five generations, under standard rather than pathogen-free housing.
Spontaneous tumour incidence is an endpoint of surveillance failure; the recognition step and the fate of individual transformed cells are not observed.

studies.system: Thermophilic Bacillus PS3 FoF1-ATP synthase lacking the inhibitory C-terminal domain of the epsilon subunit, reconstituted into soybean phosphatidylcholine liposomes
studies.preparation: Every reconstitution uses the same 10 mg of lipid and 75 micrograms of enzyme, with contaminating potassium washed out of the lipid to about 0.05 mM. Proteoliposomes are acidified for 10-20 h with valinomycin at a set internal potassium concentration and then injected into a basic medium with 0.5 mM ADP and 10 mM phosphate at 30 degrees C: the pH difference is set by the buffer pair and the membrane potential by the potassium ratio through the Nernst equation. ATP is followed by luciferin-luciferase luminescence calibrated with three additions of 0.1 nmol ATP, and the initial rate is taken from an exponential fit of the first 6-15 s. Controls add the H+/K+ antiporter nigericin, change the external and internal pH at constant pH difference and potential, and impose either term alone, including against an opposing contribution of the other.
studies.observable: Initial rate of ATP synthesis per enzyme, in turnovers per second, against the pH difference, the membrane potential and the internal and external potassium concentrations
studies.finding: All rates measured over a pH difference of -0.3 to 2.2 and a membrane potential of -30 to 140 mV fall on one curve against the proton-motive force, whatever the division between the two terms and whatever the internal potassium concentration between 1 and 50 mM; either term alone drives synthesis, even when the other opposes, and nigericin, which collapses the force, prevents synthesis. Synthesis sets in only above a force of about 100 mV, which agrees with the about 95 mV at which synthesis and hydrolysis balance for a phosphorylation free energy of 37 kJ/mol and the H+/ATP ratio of 3.3 implied by the ten c subunits. At fixed pH difference and potential the rate is independent of the external pH between 7.2 and 8.0 and falls above 8.0, and it drops when the internal pH is lowered to 5.6.
limitations: One reconstituted thermophilic enzyme at 30 degrees C with saturating ADP and phosphate and almost no ATP present; the force is imposed by an acid-base jump and a valinomycin diffusion potential rather than maintained by a pump.
The membrane potential is calculated from the Nernst equation rather than measured, and the calculation fails below 1 mM internal potassium, where other ion fluxes contribute.
Rates are initial rates from exponential fits with no correction for enzymes facing the wrong way, so absolute turnovers are underestimated.
The supplementary figures, including the equilibration and leak controls, were not read.

studies.system: Clock-mutant mice with wild-type littermates and wild-type mice under chronic weekly light-dark phase shifts, each on control or alcohol-containing liquid diet
studies.preparation: Use two independent models of circadian disorganization. Genetically, compare individually housed 7 to 9-week-old male homozygous Clock delta-19 mutants with wild-type littermates from heterozygous intercrosses on a 12-hour light-dark cycle. Environmentally, subject 6 to 8-week-old male C57BL/6J mice to weekly 12-hour phase shifts of the light-dark cycle for three months before and throughout the experiment, with non-shifted controls. In both models apply the Nanji liquid diet with alcohol at 29 percent of calories after a two-week ramp, or an isocaloric dextrose control diet. studies.observable: Five-hour urinary sucralose, sucrose, mannitol and lactulose recovery, serum lipopolysaccharide and binding protein, cytoplasmic and total colonic occludin, and liver steatosis, inflammation and injury scores
studies.finding: Disrupting the organism's circadian regulation opens the colonic barrier by two independent routes. Clock delta-19 mutants excrete about twice the sucralose of wild-type littermates, 2.07 against 0.96 percent of the oral dose, with no differences in sucrose, mannitol or lactulose, which the source reads as a colon-specific defect; mice under three months of weekly phase shifts likewise excrete more sucralose than non-shifted mice, 0.91 against 0.54 percent. Serum lipopolysaccharide is significantly elevated in alcohol-fed Clock mutants relative to mutants on the control diet, with a significant genotype by diet interaction, whereas control-fed mutants have lower lipopolysaccharide than wild-type littermates; in the environmental model lipopolysaccharide and its binding protein show significant time-of-day effects and schedule by time-of-day interactions. Cytoplasmic colonic occludin, indicating internalized protein, is increased by both genetic and environmental disruption without matching mRNA changes.

In the knockouts, hypoxic iNOS induction is abolished without HIF-1alpha but not without HIF-2alpha, while hypoxic arginase-1 induction is reduced without HIF-1alpha, more strongly reduced without HIF-2alpha and abolished in the double knockout, with basal arginase-1 also attenuated without HIF-2alpha. With abundant L-arginine, nitric oxide is abrogated in HIF-1alpha-null macrophages and elevated in HIF-2alpha-null cells, and after lipopolysaccharide in vivo plasma nitrite plus nitrate falls at 6 h in myeloid HIF-1alpha knockouts and rises at 24 h in myeloid HIF-2alpha knockouts. Loss of HIF-2alpha does not affect Fizz1 or Ym-1 or the hypoxic induction of Glut1 and LDH-A, and interleukin-4 still induces arginase-1 in HIF-2alpha-null cells.
limitations: Mouse macrophages, with much of the knockout analysis performed under 1 percent oxygen, so the stress pathway is engaged by hypoxia rather than by a physiological tissue cue.

The polarization readout is concentrated on the iNOS and arginase-1 arms and on nitric oxide; other M1 and M2 markers are reported only for the HIF-2alpha knockout and in supplemental figures that were not read.
In vitro knockouts use Tie2-Cre and the in vivo experiment LysM-Cre, so the deletions are not identical across the two settings.

studies.system: Schizosaccharomyces pombe drug-sensitive MDR-sup strain expressing Cut11-GFP (nuclear envelope), Hht2-GFP (histone H3), Gar1-GFP (nucleolus), Tel1-GFP or Atb2-GFP (tubulin), with the Cutin-1-resistant fas1-AT point mutant and nuclear-size mutants cdc25-22 and wee1-50
studies.preparation: Cells are treated with the fatty acid synthase inhibitor Cutin-1 (100 µM for time-lapse at 105-s intervals; 30 µM for 5-6 h before fixation and DAPI staining) or DMSO. Nuclear cross-sectional area and long-axis length, spindle shape, chromosome, nucleolus and telomere separation and septation are followed through the closed mitosis; the fas1-AT mutation in the Fas1 dehydratase domain controls for off-target effects; cdc25-22 (larger nuclei) and wee1-50 (smaller nuclei) at 29 C vary nuclear size.
studies.observable: Mitotic nuclear envelope expansion (nuclear area and length), spindle morphology, chromosome and nucleolus segregation, and the frequency of mitotic chromosome defects
studies.finding: Nuclear size increases during mitosis in control cells, but the increase is suppressed in Cutin-1-treated cells and the extension of the nucleus along its long axis is inhibited; both defects and a slight metaphase-anaphase delay (16.5 against 12.5 min of Cut11-GFP at the spindle pole body) are suppressed by the fas1-AT mutation. Spindles become curved and buckled in anaphase. In 13 of 25 filmed treated cells, chromosomes begin to segregate, fail to separate further and re-associate before septation, giving the cut phenotype, and nucleoli frequently remain unseparated. Chromosome defects appear about 3 h after Cutin-1, after nuclear and cell size fall within 1 h, and are reduced in cdc25-22 cells with enlarged nuclei (16.1 against 36.3 percent) and increased in wee1-50 cells with smaller nuclei (64.9 percent). The authors propose that fatty acid synthase-mediated nuclear envelope expansion provides the nuclear volume and elongation needed for chromosome segregation during closed mitosis.
limitations: One yeast with a closed mitosis; in organisms whose nuclear envelope breaks down, daughter nuclei form differently.
Fatty acid synthase is inhibited chemically; the existing nucleus and its envelope persist, and what fails is the expansion and division of the nuclear compartment.
About half of the filmed treated cells still segregate their chromosomes.
Lipid synthesis and membrane amounts are not measured in cells; the target identification section was read only through the Abstract.

studies.system: Young (10-16 weeks) and old (18-22 months) TNF-knockout and wild-type C57BL/6 mice bred in house under specific-pathogen-free conditions
studies.preparation: Breed TNF-deficient and wild-type C57BL/6 mice in the same facility, feeding ageing mice a 14 percent-protein maintenance diet with an exercise wheel, and compare young with old animals within each strain, since the strains came from different source colonies. Measure plasma IL-6 by ELISA and IL-6 production by whole blood incubated 24 hours with or without 100 ng/ml ultrapure lipopolysaccharide, constitutive and inducible IL-6 in lung homogenates and agarose-perfused lung slices, lung cellular infiltrate as a blinded percentage of total lung area on haematoxylin-eosin sections, and pneumococcal killing by bone-marrow-derived macrophages normalized for uptake. Measure in vivo intestinal permeability as plasma fluorescence 4 hours after an oral gavage of FITC-dextran, which the 2018 correction restates as 80 mg/ml, and circulating muramyl dipeptide with a Nod2-dependent HEK293T reporter bioassay on heat-inactivated plasma. Treat old and young wild-type mice with adalimumab or a human IgG isotype control and reassess TNF, the faecal community and permeability.
studies.observable: Plasma and lung IL-6, whole-blood IL-6 with and without lipopolysaccharide, lung infiltrate area, macrophage pneumococcal killing, plasma FITC-dextran, muramyl-dipeptide reporter activity and faecal community divergence
studies.finding: Deleting one inflammatory cytokine prevents the whole age-associated inflammatory state and the barrier and translocation changes that accompany it. In contrast to wild-type animals, aged TNF-knockout mice do not have greater circulating IL-6 in the steady state, and their lipopolysaccharide-stimulated whole blood does not produce more IL-6 than that of young mice; constitutive lung IL-6 is not affected by age in TNF-knockout lung slices, pulmonary cellular infiltrates are not observed in the old knockouts, and their bone-marrow-derived macrophages do not show the impaired pneumococcal killing of old wild-type macrophages. Intestinal barrier function in old TNF-knockout mice was equivalent to young TNF-knockout mice, young wild-type mice and young or old germ-free mice, and their circulating muramyl dipeptide did not increase with age, while their faecal communities diverged less with age than wild-type communities. Adalimumab given to old wild-type mice reduced TNF below the limit of detection and altered the faecal microbial community, but had no measurable effect on intestinal permeability.
limitations: Germline TNF deletion removes the cytokine from development onwards, so it does not separate the formation of the inflammatory state from its maintenance.
Wild-type and TNF-knockout colonies came from different breeding sources, so the authors compare age within strains and not between strains.

The reported adalimumab regimen conflicts between the Figure 5D legend and the STAR Methods by a factor of 800 in dose and by a week in duration, so the administered regimen is unresolved, and its permeability result is reported as data not shown.

The 2018 correction states that several permeability and ELISA experiments were performed simultaneously and analysed as one dataset across figures, and corrects the FITC-dextran concentration to 80 mg/ml.
Circulating microbial components are detected as Nod2-dependent reporter activity standing for muramyl dipeptide, not as identified molecules, and lipopolysaccharide was not measured.
Mice of one background in one facility, with female mice for these figures; supplementary figures were not read.

studies.system: C57BL/6 mice (wild type, antibody-deficient muMT and natural-antibody-deficient Cd19-null) and primary mouse Kupffer cells, challenged with serotype-10A Streptococcus pneumoniae or the serotype-14 strain TH291214
studies.preparation: Mice are infected intravenously with 10^6 colony-forming units of serotype-10A S. pneumoniae (TH86010A and four further isolates) or of the serotype-14 control strain, and bacteraemia is followed over the first 30 min with organ counts at 30 min; antibody-deficient muMT mice receive graded mouse serum, purified natural IgG or purified natural IgM intravenously 5 min before infection; capture is imaged by intravital microscopy of the liver sinusoids; primary Kupffer cells are incubated with either strain in 20 percent serum from normal or antibody-deficient mice; survival is followed after intravenous or intranasal infection with 10^7 colony-forming units; and Cd19-null mice, which lack the B-1a source of natural antibodies and in which anti-capsule antibodies are barely detectable by ELISA, are tested in the same assays. Germ-free and specific-pathogen-free mice and male and female mice are compared as controls.
studies.observable: Bacteraemia kinetics and organ colony counts, bacteria immobilised on Kupffer cells by intravital microscopy and in vitro, serum anti-capsule IgG and IgM by ELISA, and survival
studies.finding: Antibody-deficient muMT mice clear the serotype-14 strain like wild type but completely fail to move serotype-10A pneumococci from the bloodstream to the liver, with significantly fewer Kupffer-cell-associated serotype-10A bacteria by intravital microscopy, while serotype-14 capture is unchanged; the same holds for four further serotype-10A isolates. Giving mouse serum, purified natural IgG or purified natural IgM before infection restores clearance dose-dependently. In vitro, primary Kupffer cells bind serotype-10A abundantly in normal serum but only marginally in muMT serum, whereas serotype-14 binds regardless of the serum source. All muMT mice die after intravenous or intranasal serotype-10A infection and all survive serotype-14 infection, and Cd19-null mice are likewise impaired for serotype-10A but not serotype-14. Clearance is independent of sex and of the microbiota.
limitations: Mouse infection with two pneumococcal serotypes; the readout is bacterial capture, clearance and survival, not the recognition, signalling and effector repertoire of the immune cell as a whole.

muMT and Cd19-null mice lack B cells or B-1a cells, so effects beyond the missing antibodies cannot be excluded, and the reconstitution experiments supply polyclonal serum immunoglobulin rather than a defined antibody.

Capture of the serotype-14 control proceeds without antibody through another receptor, so the dependence shown is target-specific; the complement arm of the same capture is reported in sections that were not read.

studies.system: Human HeLa cells with doxycycline-inducible cytosolic (LbNOX) or mitochondria-targeted (mitoLbNOX) water-forming NADH oxidase from Lactobacillus brevis; primary rat hepatocytes
studies.preparation: HeLa cells in medium with 200 µM uridine and without pyruvate are treated with the electron transport chain inhibitors piericidin (1 µM, complex I), antimycin (1 µM, complex III), chloramphenicol (10 µg/ml, mitochondrial translation) or ethidium bromide (30 ng/ml, mtDNA replication), with or without induced LbNOX or mitoLbNOX, and proliferation is measured; pyruvate, oxaloacetate, lactate and malate are compared under piericidin. NAD+/NADH is assessed by SoNar fluorescence, lactate/pyruvate ratios and HPLC, medium metabolite exchange by LC-MS, PDH phosphorylation by immunoblot, and gluconeogenesis in adenovirally transduced rat hepatocytes. Controls test mitochondrial membrane potential and ETC-derived ATP synthesis.
studies.observable: Cell proliferation, NAD+/NADH ratios, uptake and release of medium metabolites, PDH phosphorylation and gluconeogenic rate
studies.finding: HeLa cells cannot proliferate with the electron transport chain inhibited in uridine-supplemented, pyruvate-free medium; expression of LbNOX or mitoLbNOX rescues proliferation under all four inhibitors, and all nine metabolites whose uptake or release antimycin changes more than two-fold are reversed by either enzyme, a rescue not attributable to mitochondrial membrane potential or ETC-derived ATP synthesis. Oxaloacetate, like pyruvate, rescues the piericidin proliferation defect, whereas malate and lactate do not. With an intact chain, LbNOX and mitoLbNOX lower cytosolic NADH and the lactate/pyruvate ratio and change pyruvate, aspartate and succinate exchange more than two-fold without changing glucose uptake or lactate release; mitoLbNOX almost completely dephosphorylates PDH, and LbNOX raises gluconeogenesis from lactate in hepatocytes to the rate seen with pyruvate. The authors conclude that NAD+ recycling is an essential function of the electron transport chain required for proliferation.
limitations: Redox balance is removed by inhibiting the electron transport chain, which also stops proton pumping; the attribution to NAD+ recycling rests on rescue by an exogenous oxidase and on the membrane-potential and ATP controls in supplementary figures not read.
Cancer-derived HeLa cells in culture for proliferation and flux, primary rat hepatocytes for gluconeogenesis.
Glucose uptake and lactate release are unchanged by the oxidases, so the dependency concerns NAD+-coupled biosynthetic and mitochondrial fluxes, not all of metabolism.

studies.system: Embryonic fibroblasts (passages 2–5) and thymocytes from ASK1−/− and ASK1+/+ mice
studies.preparation: Disrupt the first coding exon of ASK1 and confirm loss of protein and kinase activity. Treat MEFs with TNF plus cycloheximide, the anti-Fas antibody Jo2 plus cycloheximide, or H2O2 with the catalase inhibitor aminotriazole, with or without 1 mM N-acetyl-L-cysteine (Nac); follow JNK and p38 activation by phospho-specific immunoblots, apoptosis by Hoechst/propidium iodide morphology and TUNEL, and caspase-8 activity; re-express ASK1 by adenovirus in ASK1−/− MEFs.
studies.observable: Phospho-JNK and phospho-p38 time courses, TUNEL-positive and morphologically apoptotic cells, and caspase-8 activity
studies.finding: ASK1−/− MEFs lost the sustained phase of TNF- and H2O2-induced JNK and p38 activation and were much less sensitive to TNF- and H2O2-induced apoptosis, whereas Fas-induced apoptosis and caspase-8 activation were intact. studies.system: Balb/c 3T3 fibroblasts, serum-starved for 3-5 days or growing in 10 percent serum
studies.preparation: Microinject an inhibitory antibody against the myosin-binding subunit of myosin phosphatase (M130Ab, 5 mg/ml), a constitutively active MBS truncation (MBS296, 1 mg/ml) or a control fragment (MBS278-415), each with FITC-dextran to mark injected cells; where indicated, pretreat for 30 min with 10 µM Y-27632 (ROCK inhibitor) or 10 µM ML-9 (MLCK inhibitor), and stimulate starved cells with serum for 10 min. Fix and stain with rhodamine-phalloidin, an antibody to Ser19-phosphorylated myosin light chain (MLC) or anti-vinculin; uninjected cells on the same coverslips serve as controls.
studies.observable: Stress fibres, peripheral actin bundles, focal adhesions and phosphorylated MLC by immunofluorescence
studies.finding: Inhibiting myosin phosphatase with M130Ab induces stress fibres and focal adhesions in starved cells, and MBS296 blocks serum-induced stress-fibre and focal-adhesion formation and keeps MLC phosphorylation low while a microfilament network still forms; the control fragment has no effect. In cells growing in serum, Y-27632 disassembles stress fibres (uninjected cells in Figure 5k), whereas ML-9 does not markedly affect them. The authors conclude that MLC phosphorylation is necessary and sufficient for stress-fibre and focal-adhesion assembly, ROCK acting in the cell centre and MLCK at the periphery.
limitations: One fibroblast line; structures are assessed in images with stated numbers of injected cells, and the disassembly of existing fibres by Y-27632 in uninjected cells is reported qualitatively, confirming an earlier report.
10 µM pharmacological kinase inhibitors may act off target.
Actin polymerization into a microfilament network continues when MLC phosphorylation is blocked; intracellular transport is not measured.

studies.system: Proton-antiproton collisions at sqrt(s) = 540 GeV in the UA1 detector at the CERN SPS collider
studies.preparation: Record 18 nb^-1 (about 10^9 collisions) in November-December 1982 with electron, jet, total-transverse-energy and muon triggers in a hermetic calorimeter around a drift-chamber central detector in a 0.7 T dipole field. Select isolated electrons of large transverse energy and, separately, events with large missing transverse energy; scan the surviving events visually and evaluate backgrounds from misidentified hadrons, photon conversions and heavy-quark decays. Bound the W mass from the transverse mass and fit electron angle and energy and neutrino transverse energy with V-A decay kinematics and the W transverse-momentum distribution.
studies.observable: Electron and missing-transverse-energy vectors of the selected events, their transverse mass and the fitted W mass
studies.finding: The electron and missing-energy searches converge on the same events: six electron events without jets (five in the central gondolas, one in the end-cap), each with an isolated electron balanced by missing transverse energy of similar magnitude; no background process considered could simulate them. The transverse mass gives a model-independent bound m_W > 73 GeV/c^2 (90 percent CL), and the fit gives m_W = 81 (+5/-5) GeV/c^2, which the source states is in excellent agreement with the expectation of the Weinberg-Salam model; the introduction gives the predicted mass as 82 +/- 2.4 GeV/c^2 for sin^2 theta_W = 0.23 +/- 0.01 within the unified weak and electromagnetic theory.
limitations: Six events, of which the final analysis keeps the five central ones.
The fitted mass assumes W decay kinematics, V-A couplings and a model of the W transverse momentum.
The Z boson and the photon are not measured in this paper.

studies.system: Clonal raider ant (Ooceraea biroi) colonies of 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12 or 16 genetically identical, age-matched, queenless workers of two clonal genotypes; 112 colonies
studies.preparation: Assemble colonies of 1 to 16 workers (7-9 replicates per size and genotype) from one stock colony and one eclosion cohort, matched for genotype and age, with an equal number of 4-day-old larvae (1:1 ratio), in 5-cm Petri dishes without a nest chamber, fed one prey item per larva every three days. Track paint-marked ants automatically (7-9 frames per hour over 39-41 days), record survival and brood development, and compare group sizes against resampling and rank-shuffling nulls, with paint-marking, density and morphology controls.
studies.observable: Individual spatial spread (RMSD), between-worker behavioural variation, day-to-day and between-cycle rank consistency (specialization), day-to-day colony fluctuations, spatial fidelity, brood neglect, colony growth and larval time to eclosion
studies.finding: Behavioural variation increased with group size; day-to-day specialization became significantly different from random at group size 6, and individual ranks persisted across brood cycles in colonies of 6 to 16 workers (for example r=0.62 at size 6 and r=0.44 at size 16) but not at size 4 (r=0.08, P=0.68). Day-to-day fluctuations in colony behaviour and brood neglect decreased and spatial fidelity increased with group size; colony growth was negative in the smallest colonies and plateaued near 1 at sizes 12 and 16, and larvae took about 10 days (45%) longer to eclose in the smallest than in the largest colonies.
limitations: One clonal, queenless ant species without morphological castes, in small laboratory dishes; division of labour is a continuous spatial-behaviour measure, not caste differentiation.

Group size is the manipulated variable; division of labour, homeostasis and fitness co-vary with it, and only the source's model, not the experiment, apportions homeostasis between group size and division of labour.

studies.system: Semisynthetic KcsA potassium channel in which the backbone amide between Tyr78 and Gly79, which forms ion-binding site S1 of the selectivity filter, is replaced by an ester, compared with the semisynthetic wild-type channel
studies.preparation: Assemble the channel by expressed protein ligation from a recombinant N-terminal fragment and a synthetic C-terminal depsi-peptide carrying the Tyr78-Gly79 ester, fold the ligation product into lipid vesicles and purify the tetramer; confirm the mass by electrospray MS. Measure single-channel currents after fusing the vesicles with planar POPE/POPG bilayers in symmetric 150 mM KCl, and the current-voltage relation and the dependence of current on K+ concentration from 50 to 500 mM, against the semisynthetic wild type. Crystallise the channel as a complex with an antibody Fab fragment in 300 mM KCl, RbCl or CsCl, refine the structures at 2.25 to 2.75 angstroms and compare one-dimensional electron-density profiles along the filter axis with the wild-type channel after scaling the data sets.
studies.observable: Single-channel conductance and its voltage and K+ concentration dependence; refined structure and backbone RMSD; ion and water electron density along the selectivity filter
studies.finding: The less polar ester carbonyl, whose dipole moment is about 1.7 D against 3.5 D for an amide, left the filter backbone essentially unchanged (RMSD 0.15 angstroms over residues 75-80, 0.60 angstroms overall) but changed ion binding and conduction: the zero-voltage single-channel conductance fell to about 50 percent of the wild type, the current-voltage curve became nearly linear where the wild type is voltage-independent above 100 mV, and the K+ current saturated with concentration instead of rising linearly to 500 mM. K+ occupancy at site S1 fell by about 50 percent, with new density appearing at a partially hydrated position S0.5 just outside the filter, Rb+ redistributed from sites 1, 3 and 4 to sites 2, 3 and 4, and the ordered water molecule that accepts a hydrogen bond from the Gly79 amide in the wild type was no longer visible. The tetramer was also less stable, migrating partly as monomer on SDS-PAGE. The authors attribute the changed conduction to the altered electronic properties of the filter.
limitations: One channel and one of the four filter amides, chosen because it contributes to a single ion-binding site; the result does not test the filter's other backbone carbonyls.

The amide-to-ester substitution removes a hydrogen-bond donor and weakens the acceptor as well as lowering the dipole, and also destabilises the tetramer, so the dipole change is not isolated from hydrogen bonding and stability.
Occupancies are read from scaled difference electron density rather than measured independently, and the crystallised construct differs slightly from the one used for electrophysiology.
The conducting channel still forms and conducts, so the evidence bears on the operating regime rather than on the formation of the channel.

studies.finding: Enhancing macrophage efferocytosis with columbamine alleviated the dextran-sodium-sulphate-induced loss of body weight, the colon shortening, the rise in disease activity index, spleen weight and colonic myeloperoxidase activity, improved overall colon morphology on histology and dramatically reduced the number of apoptotic cells in the colon. limitations: The intestinal readouts are histological epithelial damage and disease indices; neither paracellular permeability nor microbial translocation nor circulating microbial components were measured.
One chemical colitis model in male mice, with a seven-day course rather than a chronic barrier regime.
Columbamine is a pharmacological biased agonist whose off-target actions are not excluded, and 3-methyladenine is a broad autophagy inhibitor.
The Fpr2 knockout is constitutive and FPR2 also acts in chemotaxis and neutrophil degranulation, which the authors invoke to explain the lower myeloperoxidase activity in Fpr2-null colon.

studies.system: Variable-domain fragment (Fv) of the anti-lysozyme antibody HyHEL-10 with hen egg white lysozyme, and six mutants that truncate the hydrogen-bonding amide groups of the light-chain residues Asn-31, Asn-32 and Asn-92 (LN31A, LN31D, LN32A, LN32D, LN92A, LN92D)
studies.preparation: Introduce Ala and Asp substitutions at light-chain positions 31, 32 and 92 by site-directed mutagenesis, express the Fv fragments in Escherichia coli and purify them on a lysozyme affinity column. Measure the interaction with lysozyme by isothermal titration calorimetry at pH 7.2 in phosphate buffer at 25, 30, 35 and 40 C (5 microM lysozyme in the cell titrated with 50 microM Fv), averaging at least three independent measurements, and derive the binding constant, enthalpy, entropy and heat capacity. Assay inhibition of lysozyme activity against Micrococcus luteus cells. Determine crystal structures of the LN31D, LN32D and LN92D complexes by molecular replacement from the wild-type complex and compare interfaces, contacts and interfacial water.
studies.observable: Binding constant Ka, Gibbs energy, enthalpy, entropy and heat capacity of the Fv-lysozyme association; inhibition of lysozyme activity; interface structure, contacts and hydrogen bonds
studies.finding: Every substitution that removes an interfacial hydrogen-bonding amide weakened binding, by a factor that depended sharply on how buried the bond was. Against the wild type (Ka 82.1 x 10^7 M-1, dG -51.7, dH -99.7 kJ/mol), LN31D and LN92D lost only 3.8 and 4.5 kJ/mol of binding energy (Ka 17.8 and 14.0 x 10^7 M-1) and still inhibited lysozyme almost like the wild type, while LN31A, LN32A and LN32D lost 16.3, 15.6 and 11.4 kJ/mol, corresponding to about 600-, 500- and 100-fold lower binding constants, and LN31A and LN32A no longer inhibited lysozyme at all. In each case a large loss of favourable binding enthalpy was only partly offset by reduced entropic cost. The structures showed that the complexes still formed and that the effects of the weaker mutations were compensated by conformational changes and new contacts, whereas the loss of the fully buried Asn-32 N-delta-2 to Gly-16 bond could not be compensated even though the mutant interface made more contacts in total.
limitations: One antibody-antigen pair and three light-chain positions; the authors note that the energetic contribution of interfacial hydrogen bonds varies enormously with local structure, and in their cited serine mutants removing hydrogen bonds slightly improved binding.

Asn-to-Ala and Asn-to-Asp substitutions also change side-chain volume, charge and van der Waals contacts, so a single hydrogen bond is not removed in isolation; LN31D converts one hydrogen bond into a salt bridge.
Recognition is weakened, not abolished: all mutants that could be measured still bound lysozyme, and the strongest losses are about three orders of magnitude in affinity.
LN92A could not be expressed and LN32A was measured at one temperature only; the LN31A and LN32A complexes did not yield structures.
The supplemental tables with the interface areas, contacts and serine-mutant parameters were not read.

studies.observable: Adipose caspase-1 cleavage and Il1b expression, plasma IL-18 and IL-6, glucose-tolerance curves, thymic weight and thymocyte numbers and naive versus effector T-cell frequencies
studies.finding: Deleting the sensor that drives age-related sterile inflammation removes much of the aged inflammatory state and the immune remodelling that accompanies it. Ablation of Nlrp3 lowers the ageing-associated caspase-1 activation in adipose tissue and the age-related rise in adipose IL-1beta expression, and significantly reduces the age-related increase in circulating IL-18, which is unaffected in caspase-11 mutants and abrogated in Asc-null mice; by contrast the age-related increase in IL-6 is not affected by loss of Nlrp3 or Asc, and serum IL-1beta is not measurable in 23-month wild-type mice. Nlrp3-null mice show improved glucose tolerance at 19 and 23 months but not at 14 months, whereas Il1r-null mice show no such improvement, so the metabolic effect is not mediated by IL-1 signalling. Aged Nlrp3-deficient mice are significantly protected from age-related thymic involution, with reduced ectopic adipocytes, maintained cortical and medullary architecture and greater thymic mass and thymocyte numbers, and Asc ablation significantly reduces the age-related effector T-cell expansion with a higher naive T-cell frequency in spleen, while caspase-11 mutants are indistinguishable from wild type and Il1r-null mice are not protected from thymic demise.
limitations: Germline deletion of one inflammasome sensor removes part of the aged inflammatory state only: the age-related rise in IL-6 persists.
Nlrp3-null males weighed more than wild type at 9 and 20 months, so genotype cohorts are not matched at every age.
Asc deficiency affects several inflammasomes and the naive T-cell result rests on the authors' Dock2 check rather than on a congenic control.
Thymic and T-cell endpoints are compared between genotypes within an ageing colony; the chronic inflammatory state itself is not titrated.

Only the peripheral Results with the Figure 1 and Figure 2 legends and the mouse, cytokine and statistics Methods were read; the central-nervous-system, transcriptome and healthspan experiments and all supplementary figures were not.

studies.system: Ageing cohorts of Nlrp3-/-, Asc-/-, Casp11-/- and Il1r-/- mice with wild-type littermates, maintained on normal chow to 23-24 months in a specific-pathogen-free barrier facility
studies.preparation: Mutant and wild-type cohorts are aged side by side and compared at 2 months against 15-24 months. LPS-primed bone-marrow-derived macrophages from wild-type and Nlrp3-/- mice are stimulated with age-relevant damage-associated ligands (extracellular ATP, urate, ceramides, palmitate). Caspase-1 activation is read by immunoblot in epididymal adipose tissue, Il1b by real-time PCR in adipose tissue and liver, and serum IL-18 and IL-6 by ELISA and bead assay; glucose tolerance, body composition, thymic architecture and T-cell subsets are separate endpoints.
studies.observable: Cleaved caspase-1 p20 in adipose tissue, adipose and hepatic Il1b mRNA, serum IL-18 and IL-6, active IL-1beta p17 from stimulated macrophages, and glucose tolerance
studies.finding: Multiple age-relevant damage-associated ligands induce IL-1beta activation in macrophages in an Nlrp3-dependent manner. In ageing mice, ablation of Nlrp3 lowers the age-associated rise in adipose caspase-1 activation and significantly reduces the age-related increase in adipose Il1b expression, while no significant age-related change is detected in liver. The age-related increase in circulating IL-18 is significantly reduced in Nlrp3-deficient mice and totally abrogated by loss of Asc, but is unaffected in Casp11-/- mice; serum and plasma IL-1beta in 23-month-old wild-type mice were not measurable. The loss of Nlrp3 and Asc does not affect the age-related increase in IL-6. Nlrp3-deficient animals also show improved glucose tolerance at 19 and 23 months, whereas aged Il1r-/- mice do not.
limitations: Mice of defined knockout lines aged in one barrier facility; the comparison is between genotypes rather than an intervention in an individual animal.
Nlrp3-/- males weighed more than wild type at 9 and 20 months, so genotype differences beyond inflammasome signalling are present.
Asc is shared by several inflammasomes, so the Asc result does not isolate NLRP3.
The cytokine baseline is sampled as adipose Il1b mRNA and serum IL-18 and IL-6; circulating IL-1beta was below detection and the wider cytokine repertoire is not measured.
Read in the PubMed Central author manuscript: the Results on peripheral age-related inflammation with the Figure 1 and 2 legends; the supplementary figures were not inspected.

studies.system: Saccharomyces cerevisiae wild type (W303) and temperature-sensitive kar2 (BiP) alleles kar2-113, kar2-159 and kar2-203, with sec63 mutants and Sec63p-depletion strains
studies.preparation: Cells grown at 24 C are shifted to 37 C for 30 min, or for varying times for kar2-159, then pulse-labelled for 5 min with [35S]methionine; carboxypeptidase Y (CPY, an SRP-independent precursor) and dipeptidyl aminopeptidase B (DPAP B, an SRP-dependent precursor) are immunoprecipitated and resolved by SDS-PAGE, untranslocated precursors being identified by mobility (pre-proCPY against glycosylated proCPY, pDPAP B against mature DPAP B). Sec63p is depleted by promoter shut-off over 3-7 h.
studies.observable: Accumulation of untranslocated pre-proCPY and DPAP B precursor after pulse labelling
studies.finding: All three kar2 alleles show a severe defect in pre-proCPY translocation at 37 C; kar2-159 and kar2-203 also strongly block DPAP B translocation, and kar2-113 only partially. In kar2-159 both defects are nearly complete after 10 min at 37 C. Depletion of Sec63p leads to accumulation of SRP-dependent and SRP-independent precursors. The authors conclude that Kar2p (BiP) is essential for SRP-dependent protein translocation in vivo.
limitations: Untranslocated forms are inferred from gel mobility after pulse labelling; a cytosolic-location assay is not used.
Kar2p is tested for translocation, not for its folding or quality-control roles.
Two reporter precursors in one yeast; transport beyond the ER is not measured.

studies.system: Normal rat kidney (NRK) cells expressing LC3 and LAMP1 reporters, with atg5 or atg7 RNAi, rapamycin or lysosomal protease inhibitors, and fibroblasts from lysosomal storage disease patients
studies.preparation: Starve NRK cells in DMEM without serum and glutamine for up to 12 h; follow autophagy and lysosomes by LC3 and LAMP1 imaging, electron microscopy and gradient fractionation, and mTOR activity by S6K and 4E-BP1 phosphorylation immunoblots. Compare non-specific with atg5 or atg7 RNAi, add rapamycin at 2 h of starvation, or block autolysosomal proteolysis with leupeptin or E64/pepstatin A; starve Scheie, Fabry and aspartylglucosaminuria fibroblasts.
studies.observable: S6K and 4E-BP1 phosphorylation over starvation time, fraction of autophagic cells, lysosome number and size, and autophagic lysosome reformation tubules
studies.finding: S6K and 4E-BP1 phosphorylation fell within 2 h of starvation and was restored by 6 h and thereafter despite ongoing starvation, as autophagy attenuated and lysosomes reformed from autolysosomes. Knock-down of atg5 or atg7 markedly inhibited the recovery of S6K phosphorylation, and inhibiting autolysosomal proteolysis with leupeptin or E64/pepstatin A abolished mTOR reactivation; rapamycin added at 2 h blocked reactivation and lysosome reformation, leaving enlarged autolysosomes, and lysosomal storage disease fibroblasts showed impaired mTOR reactivation. The source concludes that autophagic degradation reactivates mTOR, which terminates autophagy and triggers lysosome reformation.
limitations: Cultured cells, mainly NRK, with starvation defined as withdrawal of serum and glutamine while amino acids and glucose remain.
The atg5 and atg7 knock-down data are partly in supplementary panels that were not read; knock-down is partial.
Senescence-related outputs of mTOR are not examined.

studies.system: Saccharomyces cerevisiae wild type (RH1800) and the temperature-sensitive serine palmitoyltransferase mutant lcb1-100 (RH3809, isolated as end8-1), with the sla2-41 (end4) endocytosis mutant as control
studies.preparation: Cells grown at 24 C are preincubated for 15 min at 24 or 37 C with or without 50 µM dihydrosphingosine (DHS) or phytosphingosine (PHS), then assayed for continuous-presence [35S]alpha-factor internalization, internalized ligand being defined by resistance to pH 1.1 washes. Sphingolipid synthesis is measured after the same preshift by [3H]myo-inositol labelling of base-resistant inositol sphingolipids (IPC, MIPC, M(IP)2C), wild type at 24 C set to 100 percent. DHS rescue is also tested in sla2-41 cells and in lcb1 strains lacking sphingoid-base kinases or modifying enzymes; Lucifer yellow accumulation after a 15 min preshift to 37 C tests fluid-phase endocytosis.
studies.observable: Acid-wash-resistant [35S]alpha-factor internalization, [3H]myo-inositol incorporation into inositol sphingolipids, and vacuolar Lucifer yellow accumulation
studies.finding: The lcb1-100 mutant, isolated as the endocytosis mutant end8-1, has a temperature-sensitive serine palmitoyltransferase activity, the first step in sphingolipid biosynthesis. At 37 C its sphingolipid synthesis is 25-fold lower than wild type and the internalization step of alpha-factor endocytosis is blocked, the defect installing in under 15 min. Adding DHS restores sphingolipid synthesis at 37 C, and DHS or PHS restores alpha-factor internalization, whereas DHS does not suppress the sla2-41 internalization defect. Lucifer yellow accumulation is defective in lcb1-100 and restored by PHS. The authors conclude that sphingoid base synthesis is required for the internalization step of endocytosis and postulate that the relevant lipid is a sphingoid base rather than a phosphorylated base, ceramide or a complex sphingolipid.
limitations: One yeast species and one conditional allele at a restrictive temperature; the cortical actin cytoskeleton is also depolarized in the mutant at 37 C.
The required species is postulated to be a sphingoid base; a role of ceramide or sphingolipids over longer times is not excluded by the authors.
Exocytosis, recycling and vacuolar delivery are not tested as separate steps.
Internalization percentages are shown only in figure graphs, which were not inspected here.

studies.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
studies.system: Helium dimers (4He2) formed in a cryogenic supersonic expansion of helium gas and isolated from monomers and larger clusters by matter-wave diffraction
studies.preparation: Expand helium gas through a 5 micrometre nozzle cooled to 8 K at 450 hPa driving pressure; separate a pure dimer beam by diffraction at a 100-nm-period transmission grating so that only dimers reach the laser focus; singly ionize both atoms of each dimer with photons of 18.5 nm and under 100 fs from the FLASH free-electron laser (a 780 nm tunnel-ionization campaign serves the inner region only); measure the two ions with a COLTRIMS reaction microscope, convert the kinetic energy release of the Coulomb explosion into internuclear distance, subtract random coincidences from residual-gas helium and correct for electron recoil.
studies.observable: Distribution of internuclear distances of the dimer (the square of its wavefunction), its exponential tail and the binding energy derived from the slope, compared with He-He potential calculations
studies.finding: The source describes the dimer as bound only by the van der Waals force, in a He-He potential with a minimum of about 1 meV at about 3 Angstrom. The measured pair-distance distribution runs from the classical turning point at 13.6 Angstrom to beyond 200 Angstrom, with about 80 percent probability that the two nuclei lie in the classically forbidden region. An exponential fit between 50 and 300 atomic units gives a binding energy of 151.9 +/- 13.3 neV (statistical 1.7, calibration 10.2, correction 1.4 neV), in good agreement with the ab initio prediction of Przybytek et al. (139.2 +/- 2.9 neV) and in clear disagreement with the TTY and LM2M2 potentials (114 and 113 neV).
limitations: One dimer of the least polarizable atom; other atoms and molecules are not measured.
The link between the bond and the atoms' electronic structure is the agreement with ab initio He-He potentials; the atoms themselves are not changed.
The measurement cannot distinguish the most recent potential from several older calculations.
Read through a summarising fetch of the PMC page with short quotations; Equations 1-2 were not legible and the figure images were not inspected.

studies.system: Adult male TetTag, cFos-tTA and C57 mice under chronic (eight-episode) or subthreshold (two-episode) social defeat by CD1 aggressors
studies.preparation: Tag hippocampal neurons active during the first two defeat episodes (LacZ in TetTag mice) and count engram cells reactivated by a later defeat in susceptible, resilient and nonstressed mice. In cFos-tTA mice expressing the excitatory DREADD hM3Dq in dorsal CA1 cells active during a subthreshold two-episode defeat, inject clozapine-N-oxide or saline 1 h before the social interaction test, with nondefeated controls. In C57 mice expressing ArchT or GFP through the RAM system in dorsal CA1 cells active during the first two episodes of an eight-episode defeat, deliver 520-nm light during the test session with the aggressor present, with handled controls.
studies.observable: Social interaction ratio (time near an enclosed CD1 mouse relative to an empty enclosure) and CA1 engram-cell density
studies.finding: Susceptible mice had more reactivated defeat-tagged engram cells in dorsal and ventral CA1 than resilient and nonstressed mice, and engram density correlated with social avoidance. Activating the tagged CA1 cells after a subthreshold defeat, which alone did not cause avoidance, reduced social interaction (defeated CNO against defeated saline P=0.036, against nondefeated CNO P<0.001), and silencing the CA1 cells tagged during the first defeats prevented the social avoidance that eight defeats produced in GFP controls (P=0.019).
limitations: Male mice and one social stressor; the outcome of the manipulations is behaviour in the social interaction test, while the neural change is shown by engram counts.
Small optogenetic groups (five to seven mice); silencing was applied only during the test, so persistence of the stress effect after silencing was not tested.
Activity tagging captures cells active during defeat and its context, not a purely social ensemble; the Methods were read only in part.

studies.system: Macaque monkeys performing a spatial attention task with simultaneous recording in area V4 and inferotemporal cortex; 8 deactivation sessions for behaviour, 198 pre- and 214 post-injection V4 units and 28 and 31 IT units
studies.preparation: Collect baseline behaviour and recordings in each session, then inject muscimol at two to four sites in the ventro-lateral pulvinar representing the lower contralateral quadrant that contains the V4 receptive fields, 1 microlitre per site at 0.05 microlitres per minute, and resume recording about 35 minutes after the last injection; place one of the three stimuli in the ipsilateral hemifield as a within-session control, record LGN neurons closest to the injection sites in two sessions, and equate microsaccade frequency before and after deactivation in the power analyses.
studies.observable: Behavioural accuracy by stimulus location, V4 baseline and visually evoked firing rates, the attention modulation index, spike-field and field-field gamma coherence within V4 and between V4 and IT, and low-frequency LFP power
studies.finding: Deactivation reduced accuracy in the lower contralateral field from 74.3 to 10.8 percent with distracters, while the ipsilateral location was unaffected (76.6 against 72.8 percent) and the upper contralateral field fell only from 69.2 to 59.1 percent. V4 visually evoked responses fell by 59.7 percent and the response to the target colour change by 90.7 percent, and the attention modulation index fell from 0.106 to 0.053, a 50 percent reduction that the authors state did not eliminate either the evoked response or the effect of attention. Gamma coherence within V4 fell by 39 percent and the attentional enhancement of that coherence by 49.6 percent, the V4-IT gamma coherence fell by 35 percent and its attentional enhancement by 30 percent, while LFP power below 20 Hz rose markedly; LGN visual responses and IT responses were unchanged.
limitations: Two macaques and one spatial attention task.
Muscimol deactivation spreads over an unmeasured volume, although LGN and IT controls argue against spread to them.
Attentional modulation and evoked responses were reduced but not abolished.
Figures were not inspected here and the recording-only analyses lie outside the read passages.

studies.system: Purified naive OT-I CD8 T cells, wild type or ICAM-1 deficient, activated in vitro and transferred into wild-type C57BL/6 mice
studies.preparation: T cells (5 x 10^4 per well) are activated on plate-bound SIINFEKL-loaded H-2Kb:Ig dimer and B7-1/Fc with 0.05 µg/ml IL-12; clustering is blocked with the anti-LFA-1 (CD11a) antibody M17/4, the non-blocking anti-CD18 antibody M18/2 serving as control, or restored by mixing ICAM-1-deficient with wild-type OT-I cells at varied ratios. Clusters are quantified by live imaging, proliferation by CFSE dilution and cell recovery, activation markers, IFN-gamma and granzyme B by flow cytometry and cytotoxicity on EG7-OVA targets; two-day-activated cells are co-transferred into naive recipients, or naive cells are transferred before OVA/IFA challenge, to follow expansion and KLRG-1 expression.
studies.observable: T-cell cluster number, CFSE dilution and activation markers, IFN-gamma and granzyme B expression, cytotoxicity, in vivo expansion and KLRG-1+ fraction
studies.finding: ICAM-1-deficient OT-I T cells, and wild-type cells treated with M17/4, form negligible activation clusters against high levels in wild-type and M18/2-treated cells, yet they proliferate like wild-type cells and show similar CD44, CD69, CD25 and IL-12 receptor kinetics and viability. Without clustering, IFN-gamma and granzyme B expression are 1.5-2-fold higher at days 2 and 3 (n of at least 15 and 6 experiments) and EG7-OVA killing is enhanced; mixing with wild-type cells re-clusters ICAM-1-deficient cells and lowers their IFN-gamma toward wild-type levels. Clustering limits TCR-signal exposure, raises CTLA-4 and lowers eomesodermin. After transfer, ICAM-1-deficient cells expand less and show a higher KLRG-1+ fraction in draining lymph node, spleen and ear.
limitations: Plate-bound ligand activation of TCR-transgenic cells with added IL-12; with splenocytes the IFN-gamma increase is modest.
ICAM-1 deficiency could act beyond homotypic clustering; antibody blockade and mixed-culture re-clustering are the stated controls.
Flow-cytometric fold changes are normalized to wild type within experiments; raw data were not inspected.

studies.system: Human HeLa cells (and SW480 colon cancer cells for cytotoxicity) exposed to TNF-alpha, IL-1, UV irradiation or cisplatin
studies.preparation: Expose cells to TNF-alpha, IL-1, UV (100 J/m2) or cisplatin and follow EGFR by cleavable surface biotinylation, 125I-EGF binding, immunofluorescence with Rab5 and caveolin-1, gel mobility shift and flow cytometry of surface EGFR; inhibit p38 with SB202190 (10 µM) or p38 siRNA, and clathrin with clathrin heavy-chain siRNA; compare with EGF-induced internalization; test cisplatin cytotoxicity with clathrin siRNA and gefitinib.
studies.observable: Surface and internalized EGFR, EGFR phosphorylation-dependent mobility shift, endosomal localization and cell viability
studies.finding: TNF-alpha induces transient EGFR internalization peaking near 20 min and reversed by recycling, whereas UV induces rapid, persistent internalization with arrest in Rab5-containing endosomes, comparable in 125I-EGF downregulation to EGF. SB202190 abolishes the stress-induced EGFR mobility shift and significantly reduces UV- and TNF-alpha-induced internalization, with only a minimal effect on EGF-induced downregulation; p38 siRNA likewise suppresses UV-induced internalization without affecting EGF-induced endocytosis. Clathrin heavy-chain siRNA reduces UV-induced internalization from 37.8 +/- 1.6 percent to 13.0 +/- 1.9 percent, and internalized EGFR colocalizes with Rab5 but not caveolin-1. Cisplatin activates p38 and lowers surface EGFR by 41 percent, reduced to 6 percent by SB202190, and blocking internalization lessens cisplatin cytotoxicity.
limitations: One receptor in cultured cancer cells; bulk endocytosis, other cargoes and exocytosis are not measured.
SB202190 is a pharmacological inhibitor; p38 and clathrin siRNA knockdowns are incomplete.
Several effect sizes are shown only in figure graphs, which were not inspected here.
